contract.settlement_definition: Six live per-game series, all with rules text. KXNFLPASSYDS, KXNFLPASSYDSPRECISE and KXNFLPASSYDSPROT settle YES when the named quarterback 'records N+ passing yards' in the named game (floor_strike = N-0.5); KXNFLPASSATT and KXNFLPASSCOMP use the same 'N+' construction on passing attempts and passing completions. Non-participation: PASSYDS, PASSATT and PASSCOMP settle at the pre-game fair price if the QB 'is active but does not appear in any live play'; PRECISE uses 'active but never takes a snap'; in all of them one play or snap, even nullified by penalty, locks settlement to the recorded statistic. PROT adds a refund at pre-kickoff fair price when the QB plays in the first half but in no play after it (overtime counts as after the half) unless the rung was already reached. KXNFLPASSYDSH2H settles YES if player A has strictly more passing yards than B, 50/50 on equal yards, and fair price if either does not enter or the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. No text states whether overtime statistics count, which statistics provider is the source of truth, or what happens to an inactive QB (u1, u5).

rules_evidence.quote: Once Trevor Lawrence takes at least one snap, even if nullified by penalty, the market settles based on passing yards recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: A single snap locks the contract to the statistical outcome, so a QB who throws one pass then leaves is a normal loss on every rung; only a never-snapping active QB is voided to fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: this Contract resolves to the fair price prior to the opening kickoff of the game unless the player records the required number of passing yards
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected variant refunds at pre-kickoff fair value when the QB plays in the first half but not after halftime (including overtime), except that already-reached rungs still pay YES, so the protected payoff is asymmetric to benching and injury.

rules_evidence.quote: then all markets will resolve to 50/50
rules_evidence.establishes: H2H equal-yardage tie pays half, and the full text also voids to fair price if either QB does not enter the game; the YES event is the difference of two correlated yardage totals, not a threshold.

rules_evidence.quote: Once Carson Wentz appears in at least one live play, even if nullified by penalty, the market settles based on passing attempts recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Attempt rungs use the 'appears in a live play' participation trigger (not PRECISE's 'takes a snap'), and recorded attempts, not dropbacks, are the settled count, so sacks and scrambles do not count.

rules_evidence.quote: If Carson Wentz records 25+ passing completions
rules_evidence.establishes: Completion rungs are integer 'N+' thresholds on official completions, a thinned count of attempts, so the settled variable is discrete and bounded by the attempt count.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Lock is active but does not appear in any live play, the market settles to the fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: The main passing-yards ladder now has rules text: a non-appearing active QB is refunded at the pre-game fair price, matching the attempts and completions wording rather than PRECISE's snap wording.

variants_and_edge_cases: PASSYDS, PRECISE and PROT share the 'N+' yardage construction (floor_strike = N-0.5); only PROT carries the first-half-only refund. PASSYDS's non-participation trigger is 'does not appear in any live play' while PRECISE's is 'never takes a snap', a wording difference that matters only for a QB who appears in a live play without receiving the snap (e.g. lined up as a receiver or on a special-teams unit).

KXNFLPASSYDSH2H is the only variant whose YES event is a difference of two QBs' totals: 50/50 on equal yards, fair price if either QB does not enter or the game is not started within 48 hours of the original start.

Sampled passing-yards texts never say whether overtime yards count or which statistics provider is the source of truth; the existing draft's 'regulation-and-overtime' is an inference, recorded as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS u1.

NFL official passing yards are gross yards (sack yardage is deducted only from team net passing), plays nullified by penalty are not credited, and a kneel-down is a rush, so dropbacks that end in sacks or scrambles add zero to this contract.

PROT refund versus PRECISE settlement: an early injury exit after a first-half snap refunds PROT (unless the rung is already hit) but is a normal loss on PRECISE, so the same injury hazard prices differently across the two ladders.
Inactive-QB treatment: every per-game ladder text covers only an 'active' QB who never plays; an inactive or scratched QB is not addressed and is carried as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS u5.

KXNFLPASSATT and KXNFLPASSCOMP settle on attempt and completion counts: spikes count as attempts (and incompletions), two-point tries are not passing attempts in official statistics, and a pass nullified by penalty is not counted, so attempt rungs depend on clock-management habits that do not affect yardage.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated in any of the six rules texts (only the 'Governing League' disclaimer); treat official NFL game-book/GSIS statistics as the assumed source and capture the Kalshi expiration value to check stat-correction drift. Sleeper is named only in the fantasy series.

mechanism.summary: A quarterback's passing yards in one game is a compound sum: the number of completed passes times yards per completion, where completions are a thinned binomial of attempts, attempts are dropbacks minus sacks and scrambles (spikes are counted as incomplete attempts), and dropbacks are team plays times a script-dependent pass rate. Each layer has its own noise. Plays are set by both offenses' tempo and clock behaviour; pass rate swings with the score path (trailing offenses throw, leaders run); a pass's yield depends on the QB's accuracy, receiver separation, depth of target and the defence's pressure and shell; and a small number of explosive completions create a heavy right tail around any rung. Before the number of attempts is even defined, the quarterback must start, stay on the field and not be pulled in a blowout, which is a discrete scenario switch with a left-hand mass at low yardage and, for protected contracts, a refund. The same chain settles the attempt and completion ladders: attempts are the count after dropback leakage, completions the attempts thinned by a depth- and pressure-dependent completion probability.

stages.name: Starter status, snap ceiling and removal scenarios
stages.description: Whether this passer is the QB1 for the whole game, plays part of it or never plays sets the mass at zero-to-low yards and decides which contract variants refund. The inputs are the practice and game-day inactive vintages, how the coach handles a bench-in-blowout, and the base rate of in-game concussion or throwing-hand exits. It is a mixture: full game, truncated game after injury, truncated game after benching, backup start. Each scenario carries its own attempt ceiling and the contract variant (precise, protected, H2H, attempts, completions) pays differently in each.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture with an atom at 0-40 yards for exits; benching depends on margin and minute, injury exit is near-memoryless (~3-6% per game for QBs, assumption).

stages.name: Team plays and neutral pass tendency
stages.description: Total offensive plays come from both teams' pace and how long each drive lasts (own tempo, opponent's clock drain, penalties, two-minute situations); the pass share of those plays is the team's neutral pass rate over expected, modified by play-caller regime. Early-season sample sizes are small, so the offensive coordinator and the quarterback change since last year matter more than raw last-season rate. This stage produces dropbacks before game state is applied.
stages.distribution: Plays per game roughly normal (sd ~7 plays), dropbacks ~45-70, mild positive skew from overtime; pass-rate regimes are coordinator-specific and persistent within a season.

stages.name: Score path, game script and dropback inflation
stages.description: The score path rewrites the stage above: trailing teams raise pass rate and play faster until the final minutes, leaders run the clock, large leads can end with the starter benched. Because passing yards are positively linked to deficit but only until prevent-defence and late-lead compression bite, the mapping from pre-game margin to expected dropbacks is hump-shaped, not linear. Overtime and two-minute drills add short high-density volume.
stages.distribution: Margin is roughly normal (sd ~13 points) around the own-rating expected margin (nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior); attempts respond concavely, with the heaviest right-tail mass from trailing-by-10-to-17 paths.

stages.name: Dropback outcome split: sack, scramble, throwaway, attempt
stages.description: Only attempts can produce passing yards, so the leakage of dropbacks to sacks (yardage lost on team net but not QB gross), scrambles and kneels shrinks the count before efficiency applies (spikes remain attempts but add zero yards). A pressured pocket either converts to a sack, a scramble or a rushed attempt depending on the passer's mobility and release time, and offensive-line health shifts the split. This is separate from, and not captured by, overall EPA per dropback.
stages.distribution: Binomial leakage per dropback (sack ~6-8% league average, scramble 2-5% by passer), jointly dependent on pressure rate; adds attempt-count variance of a few throws.

stages.name: Per-attempt yield: completion, depth and yards after catch
stages.description: Given an attempt, yardage is completion probability times yards per completion. The QB's accuracy and decision prior, the target depth distribution, the quality of the receiving corps (separation, yards after catch over expected) and the defensive shell decide the mean; opponent adjustment must be done on a per-unit basis. Receiver and defensive-back absences change both the mean and the skew.
stages.distribution: Yards per attempt ~6-8 with sd roughly 2 yards at the game level; completion count approximately binomial; yards per completion right-skewed.

stages.name: Explosive completions, weather and the heavy right tail
stages.description: Wind and rain remove deep shots, domes inflate them, and a single 50-70 yard play can add a fifth to a third of a typical rung distance. The long-completion rate is largely a team-and-receiver property and is more volatile than the mean yield, so tail probability for the highest rungs should be modelled separately rather than inferred from variance of yards per attempt.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed compound distribution; the top rung (300+) probability is dominated by the tail of both volume and one or two long plays.

stages.name: Settlement, stat provenance and rung coherence
stages.description: Rungs are nested events of one random variable, so their probabilities must be monotone and adjacent rungs are almost the same bet; official yardage can be corrected after the fact, and different variants refund in different ways. These contract mechanics decide how a model's single yardage distribution maps to prices per variant.
stages.distribution: Nested thresholds: P(Y>=k) is decreasing, increments are the discretized density of the yardage distribution.

stages.name: Attempt and completion count rungs
stages.description: KXNFLPASSATT and KXNFLPASSCOMP settle on counts, not yards. Attempts are dropbacks x (1 - nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage) plus the QB's expected spikes added back (that input's measurement counts spikes as leakage, but spikes are official incomplete attempts), so their distribution is driven by team plays, the script-dependent pass rate and the QB's full-game participation, with no efficiency term. Completions are attempts thinned by a per-attempt completion probability that depends on target depth, pressure, receiver separation and the QB's accuracy over expected; short-passing offences convert attempts into completions at 68-72 percent and deep-shot offences at 58-62 percent, so the same attempt count gives different completion rungs. Completions and yards are positively but imperfectly correlated: a dink-and-dunk game can clear a completions rung while missing a yardage rung.
stages.distribution: Attempts: overdispersed count (negative binomial, sd about 7-8 on a mean of 34) with a left mass from early exits; completions: beta-binomial given attempts, integer-valued with nested rungs.

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.label: Quarterback benching rule: margin and clock at which the starter is pulled
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.mechanism: Head-coach-specific rule for resting the starter in lopsided games, which removes dropbacks on the winning side and sets the zero-attempt atom after halftime for the protected variant.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.rationale: Existing exit-risk input treats injury and benching together. For a quarterback on a heavy favourite, benching is a coach habit tied to margin and minutes remaining, not a physical hazard; it lowers the top rungs even when the pre-game model expects a high-yardage game and decides whether a protected contract refunds.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.measurement: For each head coach over the last 3 seasons (shrink coach effect toward league with k=6 games), fit a discrete-time logistic hazard over all starter-QB drives: P(starter's last snap is this drive | lead L in points, minutes remaining m, starter-injury flag excluded) using all games, not just those decided by 17+, with coach random effect. Pregame output: P(pulled before end) and expected minutes lost = sum over simulated margin paths (nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd around the own-model mean from nfl.model_team_points_mean, no betting spread) of the hazard. As-of the last pre-game depth chart.
free_sources: nflverse play-by-play (last QB snap per game)
raw_data: pbp: game_id, qb_id, play order, score_differential, game_seconds_remaining
depth chart / inactives for the backup identity
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.why: Defines the left-tail mass for strong favourites and the refund trigger for KXNFLPASSYDSPROT that the generic exit-risk input cannot separate from injuries.

nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.label: Dropback-to-attempt leakage rate (sack, scramble, spike, kneel) for the QB-offence pair
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.mechanism: Share of dropbacks that never become passing attempts because they end in sacks, scrambles or clock-stopping spikes.
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.rationale: Passing yards credit only attempts and official QB yardage is gross, so the attempts count is dropbacks times (1 - leakage). Leakage is the interaction of the opponent pressure rate and this passer's tendency to escape or hold the ball; two quarterbacks with equal EPA per dropback can differ by 4-6 attempts per game from this alone.
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.measurement: Define leakage rate = (sacks + scrambles) / qb_dropback, excluding spikes and kneels from both numerator and denominator. Per QB over his last 17 starts before the as-of week, time-decayed with half-life 8 games, shrunk to the offence's rate with weight n/(n+150) dropbacks. Opponent adjustment: add b x logit-difference of the opposing defence's pressure rate (last 12 games, participation was_pressure; fall back to sack+QB-hit rate) versus league, with b fit by logistic regression 2018+ and the adjusted rate capped at league mean +/- 3 SD. Output expected fraction of dropbacks that do not become pass attempts.
free_sources: nflverse play-by-play: qb_scramble, sack, qb_spike, qb_kneel flags
raw_data: pbp: game_id, passer_id, qb_dropback, sack, qb_scramble, qb_spike, qb_kneel, pass_attempt
pressure rate faced per defence (participation was_pressure)
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.why: Converts the volume stage into attempts and explains why dropback forecasts overstate attempts for scramble-prone quarterbacks facing strong rushes. Its measurement counts spikes as leakage: correct for the yardage ladders (a spike adds zero yards) but for KXNFLPASSATT/KXNFLPASSCOMP the expected spike count must be added back, because spikes are official (incomplete) passing attempts.

nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.label: Route-weighted receiving-corps quality for the projected active set
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.mechanism: Aggregate of expected separation, catch-probability-over-expected and yards after catch over expected across the receivers and backs projected to run routes, weighted by projected route share.
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.rationale: The passer's yield depends on who catches the ball. A binary flag for WR1 out ignores that a replacement with a much lower route share and weaker separation changes yards per attempt, and that the effect depends on the whole route tree. Need a number that moves when a name changes on the inactive list.
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.measurement: Per receiver: rolling last-12-game score = 0.5 x yards per route run z + 0.3 x catch rate over expected (complete_pass - cp) z + 0.2 x YAC over expected z, each shrunk to the position mean with weight n/(n+60) targets (routes from participation/FTN charting; do not use NGS separation, which is season-aggregate only). Corps score = sum over projected active receivers of projected route share x player score, where route shares are redistributed over the inactive list using each receiver's route share in the last 3 games conditional on the same teammate absence (fallback to proportional). As-of inactive list timestamp (about 90 min pre-kick) else last Friday report.
free_sources: nflverse participation and FTN charting where available
NFL Next Gen Stats public tables (separation, cushion, YAC over expected)
raw_data: targets, receptions, air yards, YAC, cp
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.why: Gives the receiving-corps leg of a passing-yards forecast a continuous quantity rather than the skill-availability flag.

nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.label: Long-completion (20+, 40+ yard) rate and its team-opponent matchup
nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.mechanism: Probability per attempt of a 20+ or 40+ yard completion, which creates the right tail of a quarterback's yardage total.
nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.rationale: The over-rung probability for 300+ is governed by tail events, not the mean. Explosive-pass rate is more erratic than yards per attempt, depends on deep-target share, pass protection time and the opponent's safety play, and is the first thing wind removes.
nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.measurement: Per QB-offence, rate of completions >=20 and >=40 yards per attempt over the last 20 games with half-life 10 games, shrunk with k=200 attempts; opponent factor = opponent's allowed explosive-pass rate relative to league over last 12 games with k=150 attempts; combined multiplicatively on log scale; wind above 15 mph applied as a separate multiplier from nfl.weather_pit. Output: expected count of 20+ and 40+ completions and a compound-Poisson tail for yards.
raw_data: pbp: pass_attempt, complete_pass, yards_gained, air_yards, yards_after_catch, defteam
nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.why: Directly shapes the probability of high rungs and the correlation between a QB's yards and his top receiver's yards.

nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.label: Own-rating margin and total prior for the game-state distribution (market-free)
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.mechanism: Builds the distribution of the expected score path from the team's own offence and defence ratings, home edge and starter quarterback status, so nfl.script is fed without any sportsbook spread or total.
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.rationale: nfl.script's catalog measurement integrates over a margin distribution centred on the point spread; that makes the volume driver an echo of the market. The margin and total centre must come from own opponent-adjusted EPA ratings so it can be compared against Kalshi prices rather than copied from them.
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.measurement: Expected margin = (off_epa_A - def_epa_B) - (off_epa_B - def_epa_A) per play x expected plays per team (nfl.pace), plus a home-field constant fitted on 2015-2025 games (about 1.5 points, refit yearly) and a starter-QB adjustment from nfl.qb_efficiency versus the replacement backup; EPA inputs use a 10-game exponential half-life (about 6 games) shrunk to league mean with k=6 games, opponent-adjusted by ridge. Expected total = sum of the two team expected plays x points per play. Margin sd = 13.0 points, total sd = 9.5 points, re-estimated from own residuals. As-of: last game before kickoff, QB and injury status at the latest inactive list. Contains no spread_line, total_line or moneyline.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, defteam, epa, play_type, qb_dropback
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.why: Supplies the margin-state distribution that drives dropback inflation and the benching line for quarterback yards without using sportsbook lines.

nfl.qb_completion_count_model.label: QB completion-count model: expected completion probability by attempt mix with accuracy over expected (market-free)
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.mechanism: Converts a forecast attempt distribution into a completions distribution using per-attempt expected completion probability (target depth, pressure, receiver separation) plus the QB's shrunk completion-over-expected.
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.rationale: Completion rungs settle on a thinned count; raw completion percentage confounds the QB's accuracy with his offence's target-depth mix and the opponent's coverage, and is noisy over a few games. Separating expected completion probability (scheme and matchup) from completion over expected (QB skill, heavily regressed) is what moves a 25+ completions rung when attempts are fixed.
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.measurement: Per QB-offence: xComp per attempt = mean nflfastR cp (completion probability) over the last 16 games with half-life 8 games; completion over expected = mean cpoe shrunk toward 0 with k=300 attempts; opponent factor = opponent's allowed (complete_pass - cp) over the last 12 games, shrunk with k=250 attempts; p = xComp + cpoe_shrunk + opp_factor (all on the probability scale, clipped to [0.35, 0.85]) with a wind >15 mph adjustment of -2 percentage points. Completions | attempts ~ beta-binomial(attempts, p, rho), rho estimated from 2018-2025 QB-games (about 0.01-0.02). Mixed over the nfl.qb_attempt_forecast distribution. As-of: end of the previous game.
raw_data: pbp: passer_id, pass_attempt, complete_pass, cp, cpoe, air_yards, qb_hit, defteam, game_id
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.why: Supplies the completions distribution for KXNFLPASSCOMP and the joint completions-yards structure, which yardage efficiency alone does not give.

nfl.proe.reason: Volume baseline independent of score; needs coordinator-regime handling and early-season shrinkage, but the right primary driver of dropbacks.

nfl.pace.reason: Plays per game scales dropbacks, but must be built from both teams' tempo and clock drain, not own neutral pace alone.

nfl.script.reason: Score path is the main source of volume variance; its pass-rate-by-lead response surface is kept, but the margin distribution that feeds it must be nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior (own ratings), never the sportsbook spread or total that the catalog measurement text mentions.

nfl.qb_efficiency.reason: Per-attempt yield prior; partial pregame because rookies and QBs with new coordinators lack history.

nfl.pass_efficiency.reason: Team ANY/A mixes QB with receivers and protection; overlaps with qb_efficiency, so use as a team-context check not a second QB talent estimate.

nfl.def_epa.reason: Opponent pass defence efficiency is needed, but it should be pass-specific (EPA per dropback allowed) not total defensive EPA, which includes rushing.

nfl.coverage_scheme.reason: Shell and man/zone rates modulate completion depth; only matters in interaction with the quarterback's target depth, weak as a main effect.

nfl.pressure_qb.reason: Pressure and time to throw drive sacks, scrambles and completion loss; central to leakage and to efficiency.

nfl.pass_rush.reason: Defensive pressure and sack rate and offensive pressure faced are two sides of the same quantity; compute one matchup pressure estimate from both rather than two inputs.

nfl.ol.reason: Line continuity is a real driver of pressure but is partial and noisy; its value is as an input to expected pressure, not an independent effect.

nfl.skill_avail.reason: Receiver availability is a major driver of yield, but as a flag it is weak; replaced in practice by the route-weighted corps score added here.

nfl.air_yards_adot.reason: Depth profile controls the completion/yards trade-off; strongly overlaps long_completion_tail_rate on the right tail but is the better mean-depth measure.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Wind speed and precipitation are material for passing; value depends on using forecast vintages at the time of quote and a nonlinear wind threshold.

nfl.venue.reason: Roof and altitude shift the environment modestly; small after weather is in, and home-field is not a separate yardage driver.

nfl.garbage_time.reason: Blowout mass is already inside the script lattice and the benching threshold; kept as a secondary diagnostic only and removed from the staged input list to avoid double counting.

nfl.two_minute_tempo.reason: Adds short bursts of volume; second-order except around halves and for trailing teams, and double counts with script. Its catalog measurement takes lead/trail states from the spread; only own-rating game states (nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior) may feed it.

nfl.qb.reason: Starter status is the largest single switch; must be timed against the inactive list and handle limited-participation quarterbacks. The catalog measurement values the starter-minus-backup gap from market line moves; that component is a benchmark only and is replaced here by an own valuation (starter versus backup EPA per dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency, or nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop for team ratings).

nfl.in_game_exit_risk.reason: Combines injury exit with blowout benching; the two have different hazard shapes and should be separated (see new pull-threshold input).

nfl.coaching.reason: Play-caller identity drives pass rate and tempo, but the existing text is generic about fourth-down aggression which does not matter for this contract.

nfl.player_stat_variance.reason: Generic boom-bust variance with no specification; the yardage distribution should be built from the compound structure (attempts, completion, tail), not a single shape parameter.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Rungs are nested thresholds of one variable; enforce monotone probabilities across 199.5 to 349.5 rungs, but this is a consistency constraint, not information about the game.

m.rules_text.reason: Variant rules differ materially (protected refund, H2H tie and void, season total); versioned text is needed so the same forecast maps to the right payoff.

nfl.def_personnel.reason: Missing edge rushers or corners shift pressure and coverage the passer sees; overlaps pass_rush and coverage_scheme and is only informative at full-season depth-chart vintages.

m.stat_correction_risk.reason: Relevant only when the final yardage is within a yard or two of a rung; a settlement-risk adjustment, not a forecasting input.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realised frequency by strike conflates yardage mechanics with market bias at round numbers; useful for calibration checks only, not for deriving the game outcome.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe trading liquidity; they carry no information about a quarterback's passing yards.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trade tape is execution context and market-derived; it does not inform the physical yardage distribution and would leak prices into inputs.

interactions.mechanism: For a heavy favourite the starter's dropbacks fall once the lead passes the coach's benching line: before that point the offence runs, after it the backup throws; for a mid-sized favourite the benching line is never reached and the starter finishes the game. The result is a discontinuity in expected attempts at a coach-specific margin, not a smooth decline in the expected margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(starter plays 4th quarter) by coach and own-rating expected-margin bucket; contrast starters' attempts in games with lead>=17 at the 3rd quarter versus lead<=10, by coach.

interactions.mechanism: Pressure turns dropbacks into sacks and scrambles at a rate set by the passer's escape style; a mobile quarterback behind a poor line converts pressure into scrambles that lose attempts but not yardage-per-attempt, while a pocket passer converts the same pressure into sacks. The product of opponent pressure and leakage propensity is what removes attempts.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress attempts per dropback on opponent pressure rate x passer scramble propensity; check the interaction coefficient is positive for scramble-prone passers.

interactions.mechanism: Two-high shells give up short completions and take away depth: a deep-target corps loses yards per attempt against heavy two-high, while a short-area corps with high yards-after-catch holds up. The sign of the coverage effect depends on the corps' depth profile, so it only appears as a conditional contrast.
interactions.how_to_test: Split per-attempt yield by opponent two-high rate terciles and by team aDOT terciles; look for a sign flip of the coverage coefficient between terciles.

interactions.mechanism: Wind above roughly 15 mph removes deep completions and compresses the right tail much more than it reduces the mean; below that threshold the tail rate is unaffected. Cold and rain affect catch rate but not the tail in the same way.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the long-completion rate by wind bin (0-8, 8-15, 15+ mph) for high versus low aDOT offences; test a break at ~15 mph.

interactions.mechanism: A pass-heavy offence (high neutral PROE) already throws near its ceiling when level, so a trailing score state adds fewer extra dropbacks than for a run-balanced offence; the pass-rate response to a deficit is steeper for low-PROE teams, and the heavy-PROE team's attempts are bounded by plays, not by script.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit dropback share by lead bin separately for terciles of neutral PROE and test whether the deficit slope differs; compare out-of-sample rung calibration of an additive versus a PROE-by-deficit model.

interactions.mechanism: A high-efficiency quarterback gains less yards per attempt over a replacement-level one when the defence generates heavy pressure, because pressure forces early throws and sacks that efficiency priors measured against average defences do not capture; the efficiency premium saturates in the high-pressure regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress yards per dropback on qb_efficiency x opponent pressure-rate tercile using opponent-adjusted data; a negative interaction coefficient confirms saturation.

interactions.mechanism: In the head-to-head contract both quarterbacks share tempo and wind (positive covariance in passing yards) while the score path is zero-sum (the trailing side throws more), so the correlation between the two totals is positive in shootouts and negative in lopsided games; the H2H probability depends on the covariance, not on two independent means.
interactions.how_to_test: From historical games compute the correlation of the two starters' passing yards in bins of pregame own-rating margin and of wind; compare H2H win-rate calibration for an independent versus a covariance-aware simulation.

interactions.mechanism: Completion rungs and yardage rungs respond oppositely to target depth: a short-passing plan raises completion probability (more completions per attempt) but lowers yards per completion, and trailing scripts raise attempts while pushing depth up, so the completions ladder and the yards ladder for the same QB can move in different directions when the game plan or script changes.
interactions.how_to_test: In 2018-2025 QB-games, regress completions and passing yards on attempts interacted with aDOT tercile and compare the residual correlation of the two across terciles.

nonlinearities.shape: hump-shaped: attempts rise as the expected deficit grows to about 10-14 points, then flatten or fall as prevent defence, clock-killing and benching take over
nonlinearities.why: Passing volume is not monotone in the expected margin; for 17+ point underdogs yards per attempt fall faster than attempts rise, so a linear expected-margin coefficient mis-prices both tails.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold near 15 mph sustained wind; low sensitivity below, steep above
nonlinearities.why: Deep-pass completion probability drops sharply once wind exceeds the throwing envelope, so the effect on yards is a regime switch and also hits the highest rungs hardest.

nonlinearities.shape: step/atom: a mass at very low yardage for any early exit, nearly independent of the pre-game mean
nonlinearities.why: A concussion or hand injury in the first half creates a discrete outcome far below every rung regardless of efficiency, which is why the left tail of the distribution is a mixture, not a thickened normal.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in the top rungs: small increases in explosive rate move P(300+) far more than P(225+)
nonlinearities.why: A 60-yard completion is worth 20-25 percent of the distance to a 300-yard rung, so the tail probability grows multiplicatively with the explosive rate rather than additively.

contract.settlement_definition: Twelve live per-game series; all but KXNFLLONGESTREC have rules text. 'N+' rungs (KXNFLRECYDS, KXNFLRECYDSPROT, KXNFLREC, KXNFLRECPROT, KXNFLRRYDS) resolve YES when the player's official receiving yards, receptions or combined rushing-plus-receiving yards reach the integer rung; for KXNFLRECYDS, KXNFLREC and KXNFLRRYDS an active player who appears in no live play settles at the pre-game fair price and one live play (even nullified) locks settlement to recorded stats (the sampled PROT texts are truncated before any such clause); the PROT variants add the first-half-only refund (overtime counts as after the half). Escalators pay a cubic function of receptions (capped at 14) or of receiving yards bucketed to tens (capped at 200, negatives pay 0); ladders pay $0.05 per reception (cap 20) or $0.0025 per yard (cap 400). KXNFLRECYDSH2H pays 50/50 on equal yards and fair price if either player does not enter or the game is not started within 48 hours. KXNFLMOSTRECYDS is a max over every player in the game: No for a non-participant, 1/N on ties, fair price if not started within 48 hours. KXNFLLONGESTREC (longest reception) is title-only. Overtime inclusion and the statistics source are not stated in any receiving text (u1).

rules_evidence.quote: Once DJ Moore appears in at least one live play, even if nullified by penalty, the market settles based on receiving yards recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Appearing in one live play, such as a single target or even a nullified play, locks the contract to yards; only players who are active but never play are voided at pre-game fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: Payout Formula = floor(10000 x (min(s, 14) / 14)^3) / 10000
rules_evidence.establishes: The receptions escalator pays the cube of progress to 14 receptions, so value is an expectation of a convex function of the whole distribution and is capped at 14; mean alone does not determine the price.

rules_evidence.quote: The Yes payout per contract is $0.05 per reception constrained between $0.00
rules_evidence.establishes: The receptions ladder is a linear scalar capped at 20 receptions, so its fair value is 0.05 x E[min(receptions, 20)], essentially $0.05 times the expected count, unlike the convex escalator on the same player-game.

rules_evidence.quote: The Yes payout per contract is $0.0025 per receiving yard
rules_evidence.establishes: Yards ladder is linear at 0.0025 per yard capped at 400 yards, so value tracks mean receiving yards with almost no tail weighting.

rules_evidence.quote: does not participate in the game the market will resolve to No
rules_evidence.establishes: Game-most receiving yards is a max over all pass catchers of both teams in which non-participation is a loss, not a refund, and ties pay 1/N, so it needs a field projection, not one receiver's distribution.

rules_evidence.quote: records 90+ rushing and receiving yards combined
rules_evidence.establishes: The combined series settles on the sum of a player's rushing and receiving yards, so a back's carries and targets and their within-game covariance both enter the threshold probability.

rules_evidence.quote: Once Konata Mumpfield appears in at least one live play, even if nullified by penalty, the market settles based on receptions recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: The binary receptions rungs (previously title-only) use the same live-play activation as the yardage rungs, so a player who plays one snap and leaves is a normal loss, not a refund.

rules_evidence.quote: unless the player records the required number of receptions, in which case this Contract settles based on actual statistics
rules_evidence.establishes: The protected receptions rung refunds at pre-kickoff fair price when the player is absent after halftime unless the rung was already reached, so first-half receptions already banked still pay YES.

variants_and_edge_cases: Four payoff shapes share one statistic: binary N+ (KXNFLRECYDS/REC and their PROT versions), convex cubic escalator (KXNFLESCALATORRECYDS: yards bucketed to tens, capped at 200, negative totals pay 0; KXNFLESCALATORREC: capped at 14), linear ladder (cap 400 yards, cap 20 receptions) and the title-only longest-reception series (KXNFLLONGESTREC).
Escalator yards use y = min(200, max(0, 10 x floor(s/10))): bucket rounding down to tens makes the payoff a step function of final yards, so yardage between 190 and 199 pays the same 0.8573.

Sampled texts do not state overtime handling or the official statistics source for receptions/yards; reception credited on a play nullified by penalty is not credited under standard NFL scoring, but the 'live play' appearance rule counts it for activation only.

KXNFLRECYDSH2H voids to fair price if either player does not enter the game and pays 50/50 on equal yards; KXNFLRECYDSPROT adds the first-half-only refund; KXNFLMOSTRECYDS instead resolves No for a non-participant and 1/N on ties, so one injury report moves these variants in opposite directions.

KXNFLRRYDS (rushing plus receiving yards) shares the 'N+' activation wording but its total includes carries, so for running backs the rushing chain (carry share, run efficiency) is part of this archetype.

KXNFLLONGESTREC is the only title-only series: its strike construction, activation rule and the value of a zero-catch game are not visible. The former rules-sampled KXNFLLONGREC was re-filed to the extreme-play-length archetype, so no longest-reception rules text is available inside this archetype. KXNFLREC and KXNFLRECPROT now have rules text matching the yardage rungs.
Scalar escalator and ladder texts carry no activation or refund clause (the binary rungs refund an active non-playing player), so an inactive receiver's scalar position has unstated treatment (u7).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NFL statistics are implied by the 'Governing League' wording but the sampled rules do not name a provider or a correction rule; capture the Kalshi expiration value and compare with the game book.

mechanism.summary: A receiver's yards and receptions are the product of three counts that need separate modelling: how many routes he runs, how many targets he draws per route, and what each target yields. Routes follow snaps, offensive formation and the team's passing volume (which is itself a function of tempo, pass tendency and score path). Targets per route depend on his role (alignment, depth), competition from teammates, the quarterback's tendency to concentrate reads, and the defender and coverage he sees. Targets convert to catches at a rate depending on depth and quarterback accuracy, and catches to yards through air yards and yards after the catch, with a heavy right tail from one long play. Receptions are a small count with strong overdispersion; yards are a compound of receptions and per-catch distance. Contract shape then matters: binary rungs need tail probabilities, linear ladders need means, the cubic escalator needs the upper tail, and the longest-reception contract needs the maximum of the receiver's catch lengths.

stages.name: Availability, snap and route participation
stages.description: Whether the receiver is active and for what fraction of the offence's dropbacks he is running a route is the base of everything. Practice-status vintages, return-from-injury snap caps, the depth chart behind him, and in-game injury drive the route count. A returning player on a pitch count or a third receiver in 12-personnel behaves very differently from a full-time starter; route participation is not equal to snap share because blocking snaps and screens do not count.
stages.distribution: Route participation is bounded (0 to ~100% of dropbacks) with a mass near 0 for inactive, a ramp for returning players, and near-constant for ironclad starters.

stages.name: Team pass attempts available to be targeted
stages.description: The team's dropbacks and pass attempts form the pool: tempo, pass tendency over expectation and the score path define it, and the defence's tendency to force the opponent into passing or running changes the pool. Pool size is a stable function of coordinator regime plus a game-script component, and the receiver's expected share is applied to it, so the pool and the share multiply. The score-path distribution behind nfl.script is taken from the market-free nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior, never from the spread or total. The starting quarterback is the largest single shifter of this pool and of target concentration: a backup start changes attempts, depth of target and which receivers the passer reads, and for the protected variant the receiver's own in-game exit (nfl.in_game_exit_risk) truncates routes after the first half. The catalog measurement values the starter-minus-backup gap from market line moves; that component is a benchmark only and is replaced here by an own valuation (starter versus backup EPA per dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency, or nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop for team ratings).
stages.distribution: Attempts ~28-45 per team-game with positive skew from trailing scripts; overdispersed Poisson-like count.

stages.name: Target share and who absorbs a teammate's vacated targets
stages.description: Given routes, targets per route run depends on alignment, separation skill, role (primary read versus decoy), the quarterback's progression habits and competing receivers. When a teammate is out, targets flow nonuniformly: to the slot, to the tight end or to the back depending on the role the missing player filled and the scheme. The with-without evidence for a specific team is thin, and the redistribution is the largest single source of error for second and third options.
stages.distribution: Target counts are overdispersed (negative binomial-like), team-share fractions are Dirichlet-like across receivers with strong negative correlation among teammates.

stages.name: Defensive allocation of targets and coverage
stages.description: The defence funnels targets by position and alignment (which units it tolerates being thrown at) and uses shell, man or zone coverage and possible shadowing of the top receiver. The effect on a single receiver is conditional on alignment (slot versus outside versus inline) rather than only on position, and a shadow assignment removes both share and efficiency for the covered player.
stages.distribution: Share and yield effects are modest (a few percentage points of share) but lumpy for shadow assignments; position-level aggregates mask alignment-level variation.

stages.name: Catch probability and yards per target
stages.description: Catch probability depends on target depth, receiver hands and separation, quarterback accuracy and pressure; yards per catch splits into air yards and yards after the catch (tackle breaking, scheme). Receptions and yards are linked negatively through depth: deep threats have fewer catches but more yards per catch, so a receptions rung and a yards rung on the same player respond differently to the same inputs.
stages.distribution: Receptions binomial in targets (variance ~ n p(1-p)); yards per reception log-normal-like with heavy right tail; negative correlation between catches and yards per catch across players.

stages.name: Single-play extremes and longest-reception structure
stages.description: The longest reception is a maximum of that player's catches, so it depends on the number of receptions and on the length distribution of each, with a right tail dominated by yards after the catch. For yards escalators, a single 60-yard play moves the value by ten buckets. This stage is separate from the mean because the extreme-length behaviour is a property of the player and offence, not of the average yield.
stages.distribution: Maximum of N heavy-tailed lengths: with N around 4-6 the longest is often 20-35 yards with a long right tail (>60 about 5-8% for a WR1, assumption).

stages.name: Contract payoff mapping and ladder coherence
stages.description: The same predictive distribution must be translated into four payoff shapes: threshold probability, cubic expectation, linear capped mean, and maximum-over-strike. Rungs of one variable are nested, receptions and yards ladders share information, and the void rules determine how availability news is priced.
stages.distribution: Payoffs: indicator, convex cubic with cap, linear with cap, maximum statistic.

stages.name: Game-most receiving yards and rush-plus-receive sums
stages.description: Two live series leave the single-receiver threshold frame. KXNFLMOSTRECYDS asks whether one catcher out-gains every other catcher in the same game: a slot receiver on a team facing a pass-funnel defence can be the favourite even with a lower mean than the opposing alpha, because one 50-yard catch reorders the top. KXNFLRRYDS sums a back's carries and receptions, so the lead back's carry share, his yards per carry and his receiving role all feed one total, with a trailing script trading carries for targets.
stages.distribution: Max over 8-14 catchers is right-skewed with a 1/N tie atom near zero; the rush-plus-receive sum is a convolution of two overdispersed counts with role-dependent correlation.

nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.label: With/without target redistribution matrix for the projected inactive set
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.mechanism: Conditional split of routes, targets and air yards among remaining receivers when a given teammate does not play.
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.rationale: The generic target-competition input says teammates matter; what a model needs is the share each remaining player gains when a specific player is out, because slot, outside and tight end absorbers behave differently and the gain is not proportional to current share.
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.measurement: For each team-season from 2018, compute each receiver's target share and TPRR in games without teammate X versus with X (X = a top-3 target earner), requiring at least 4 games without X over the last 3 seasons, else use a position-role template pooled across teams (shrink with k=40 targets). Apply to the projected inactive list at the last available timestamp. Output: expected target share vector summing to 1 and a standard error per receiver.
raw_data: pbp: receiver_id, target flag, air_yards, game_id
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.why: Directly addresses the largest error source for WR2/WR3/TE/RB reception and yards rungs when a starter is out and prices change within hours.

nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.label: Player reception-length distribution (air yards plus yards after catch), incl. longest-play probability
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.mechanism: Empirical distribution of this receiver's yards per reception and probability that any single reception exceeds 20, 30, 40 and 60 yards.
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.rationale: The longest-reception market and the escalator tails need the upper tail of catch lengths, which differs from the mean yards per catch; YAC-heavy slot players and deep WRs have the same mean and very different tails.
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.measurement: For each receiver take completions from the last 24 games before the as-of date (need at least 40, else pool to the position-alignment template with weight 30 receptions), length = yards_gained. Fit a log-normal body below the 85th percentile of the pooled sample and a generalized Pareto tail above it. Opponent factor f = (defence's allowed rate of receptions >=20 yards per reception over last 16 games, shrunk to league with k=120 receptions) / league rate, multiplied into the tail exceedance probability (capped 0.6-1.7). N = projected receptions from nfl.targets x nfl.catch_rate_oe as a negative binomial. P(longest >= x) = 1 - sum_n P(N=n) (1-S(x))^n where S is the survival function including f; output at each strike; multiply by P(active and snaps).
raw_data: pbp: receiver_id, complete_pass, yards_gained, air_yards, yards_after_catch, defteam, game_id
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.why: Determines the title-only KXNFLLONGESTREC strike probabilities and the upper tail of the yards escalator, which mean and variance of yards alone cannot supply.

nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.label: Defensive target funnel: share of opponent targets allowed by alignment and position
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.mechanism: Fraction of opposing pass targets a defence allows to WRs (slot and outside), TEs and RBs, relative to league and adjusted for the offences it faced.
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.rationale: Defence-versus-position yield tells how efficient receivers are against a defence but not how many targets it sends to each group, which sets a receiver's share before efficiency matters.
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.measurement: For each defence: over the last 12 games (half-life 6 games) compute target shares by alignment, adjusted for opponent offence's usual share using a ridge model (alpha tuned by cross-season validation); shrink toward league with k=100 targets. Output: log ratio of expected share vs the receiver's usual share. Needs alignment tags from charting data.
free_sources: nflverse FTN charting (limited alignment fields), play-by-play
raw_data: target by position/alignment, defteam, play type
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.why: Moves a receiver's expected share at the target stage, independently of dvp efficiency, and is the reason RB/TE reception rungs often shift with opponent scheme.

nfl.qb_target_concentration.label: Quarterback target concentration and first-read lean
nfl.qb_target_concentration.mechanism: Gini or Herfindahl of the quarterback's targets across his receivers, plus the share to the primary read in the last 20 starts.
nfl.qb_target_concentration.rationale: A quarterback who locks onto one receiver gives that receiver both a higher mean and a higher variance, and when the primary receiver is out the concentration determines how widely targets spread.
nfl.qb_target_concentration.measurement: For each quarterback, compute target-share Herfindahl over his last 20 starts (half-life 10 games, min 200 targets; shrink to team-level with k=150 targets) and the primary receiver's share. Apply to the receiver under study as a multiplier on expected target share relative to neutral dispersion: share_adj = share x (1 + b x (conc - league_conc)) with b estimated by out-of-sample regression.
nfl.qb_target_concentration.why: Explains differences in reception overdispersion between teams with equal average shares and controls the second-option response when a primary receiver is out.

nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.label: Game receiving-yards leader: joint simulation of every pass catcher in one game
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.mechanism: Simulates receiving yards for all pass catchers of both teams from one shared game state so the maximum, its ties and a named player's chance of being the maximum are read jointly.
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.rationale: KXNFLMOSTRECYDS pays only if the named player beats every other catcher in the game, including the opponent's top receiver, and gives No to a non-participant. Teammates share one target pool (negative dependence) while both offences rise together in a shootout (positive dependence), so a product of marginals misprices the favourite and the long shot.
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.measurement: Per game: list every WR, TE and RB with snap share >=10 percent over the last 4 games (as-of the inactive list). Draw a shared game state (plays and pass rate per team from nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior-style own ratings, no market lines), split each team's targets by Dirichlet shares centred on target share over the last 8 games (half-life 4, shrink to role prior with k=40 targets), then yards per target from nfl.player_reception_length_distribution. 20,000 simulations; P(max) with 1/N tie credit; inactive players fixed at No. Units: probability; as-of kickoff minus 90 minutes.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, receiver_id, complete_pass, yards_gained, air_yards
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.why: Gives the probability that the named catcher posts the most receiving yards in the game, the only quantity KXNFLMOSTRECYDS pays on.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Cuts deep targets and yards; threshold effect near 15 mph; limited effect on short-area receivers.

nfl.player_stat_variance.reason: A generic boom-bust label; receptions are overdispersed counts and yards compound, so variance should come from route, target and length components.

interactions.mechanism: Expected targets equal team pass attempts times route participation times targets per route run; an error in any term scales the entire expectation, and each is estimated with separate noise. A receiver with strong TPRR on a run-heavy team can have fewer targets than a lesser receiver on a pass-heavy team.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose realised targets into attempts, route rate and TPRR, and compare the explained variance of the product model to a model using lagged target counts.

interactions.mechanism: The target gain of a remaining receiver when a teammate is out depends on which role the missing player filled and on how concentrated the quarterback's reads are: a concentrated passer gives the next read a larger boost, a spread passer distributes gain across several receivers.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate share change by receiver role in games without the top target, split by quarterback concentration terciles.

interactions.mechanism: A shadowing cornerback against the WR1 lowers his share and his yield, but the same defence's funnel toward the slot or tight end offsets for others; the net effect on a given receiver depends on alignment, so position-level opponent features flip sign across alignments.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare target share changes for slot, outside and TE under shadow versus zone defences using play-level alignment tags.

interactions.mechanism: Receptions and yards per reception are negatively correlated at the player level, since deep targets are caught less often; the joint distribution matters for the cubic escalator and for yards rungs because a high-yardage game for a deep threat arrives with few catches, and for a slot receiver with many.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of per-game receptions and yards per reception by aDOT tercile; test whether product-of-marginals mis-prices the yards 80th percentile.

interactions.mechanism: When trailing, pass volume rises and running backs and slot receivers get more routes while tight ends in 12 personnel lose them; the sign of the script effect on routes depends on the receiver's usual personnel role.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress route share on expected margin by position and personnel role and check heterogeneity by role.

interactions.mechanism: The cubic escalator payoff (min(s,14)/14)^3 for receptions and (y/200)^3 for yards is convex only below its cap: for a receiver whose expected total sits well under 14 receptions or 200 yards extra variance raises fair value, but for a high-volume receiver near or above the cap the payoff goes flat and extra variance lowers value, so the sign of the variance effect flips with the mean relative to the cap.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the escalator payoff for receivers across mean tiers with fixed mean and two dispersion levels; check the sign of the fair-value difference changes near 10-14 receptions and 150-200 yards.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: near-zero route share while inactive, ramped fraction (e.g. 40-70 percent of normal) in return games, normal after
nonlinearities.why: Returning players are on routes caps that do not scale smoothly with the injury designation, so the expected route share is a piecewise function with a jump at the first game back.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy upper tail: longest reception exceeding strike rises sublinearly in the number of catches
nonlinearities.why: The maximum of N heavy-tailed lengths grows with log N, so doubling expected receptions raises P(longest over 40) far less than doubling.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: receptions rise concavely with targets at the high end because catch rate falls as target depth and contested rate rise
nonlinearities.why: Players with extreme target share are asked to take lower-quality targets, so extra targets convert at a lower rate than the average target.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold near 15 mph: little effect below, rapid drop in deep targets and yards above
nonlinearities.why: Wind removes deep targets and the yardage tail; receptions of short routes are insensitive, so the effect concentrates in high yards rungs of deep receivers.

nonlinearities.shape: winner-take-all: flat near zero below the field's typical top value, then steeply rising
nonlinearities.why: A catcher's chance of leading the game barely moves while his projection sits below the opposing top receiver's, then rises sharply once it overtakes it, so small mean changes near the crossover are worth far more than elsewhere.

contract.settlement_definition: Eight live per-game series, all with rules text. KXNFLRSHYDS and KXNFLRSHYDSPROT settle YES when the player 'records N+ rushing yards' (floor_strike N-0.5); an active player who appears in no live play settles at the pre-game fair price and one live play (even nullified) locks settlement to recorded yards; PROT refunds at pre-kickoff fair price when the player plays in the first half and in no play after it (overtime counts as after the half) unless the rung was already reached. KXNFLESCALATORRSHYDS pays floor(10000 x (y/200)^3)/10000 with y = official rushing yards floored to tens, capped at 200 and floored at 0; KXNFLLADDERRSHYDS pays $0.0025 per rushing yard capped at 400 yards; neither scalar text has a non-participation clause. KXNFLRSHATT ('9+ rushing attempts') and KXNFLLONGRSH ('longest rush of over 6.5 yards') use the live-play activation rule. KXNFLRSHYDSH2H: strictly more yards is YES, 50/50 on equal yards, fair price if either player does not enter. KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS is a max over every player in the game: No for a non-participant, 1/N on ties, fair price if not started within 48 hours. Overtime and the statistics source are not stated in any text (u1, u6).

rules_evidence.quote: If the player participates in at least one play after the conclusion of the first half
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected contract: a player who plays in the first half and then plays no snap after halftime (any overtime period counts as after the half) refunds unless he already reached the rung; the truncated sample does not state whether overtime yards count toward the statistic, nor what applies to a player with no first-half play (u6).

rules_evidence.quote: If Audric Estime does not participate in the game the market will resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Most-rushing-yards in a game is a max-of-field contract in which non-participation is a loss, not a void, and is not protected by the refund rules of the ladder series.

rules_evidence.quote: If one or both players do not enter the game
rules_evidence.establishes: Head-to-head rushing refunds to fair price if either player never enters; a tie in yards is 50/50, so the event is a difference of two correlated yardage totals.

rules_evidence.quote: the market settles based on rushing attempts recorded
rules_evidence.establishes: The attempts series counts carries, not yards, once the player appears in a live play; kneel-downs are rushing attempts in official statistics, so a back or QB who takes victory-formation snaps gains attempts with negative yards.

rules_evidence.quote: records a longest rush of over 6.5 yards
rules_evidence.establishes: The longest-rush series is a maximum over the player's carries against a half-yard strike, so it depends on carry count and the per-carry tail, not on mean yards.

rules_evidence.quote: y = min(200, max(0, 10 x floor(s / 10)))
rules_evidence.establishes: The rushing escalator floors yards to tens, caps at 200 and floors negatives at zero before a cubic payout, so its value is a convex functional of the upper tail of the yardage distribution.

rules_evidence.quote: The Yes payout per contract is $0.0025 per rushing yard constrained between $0.00
rules_evidence.establishes: The rushing ladder is linear in yards with a 400-yard cap and a $0 floor, so its fair value is essentially the mean of non-negative rushing yards; no refund clause for a non-playing back appears in the text.

rules_evidence.quote: Once Elijah Mitchell appears in at least one live play, even if nullified by penalty, the market settles based on rushing yards recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: The main per-game rushing ladder (previously treated as title-only) has the live-play activation rule: a back who plays one snap and is hurt is a normal loss on every rung.

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLRSHYDSPROT lists a quarterback (Drew Lock, 40+) and a back in the same series: quarterback rushing yards (scrambles and designed runs, sack yardage excluded) and running back yards need different mechanisms, but share one ticker family.

Rushing yards can be negative (kneel-downs count as rushing attempts for the QB or back who takes the knee), which matters near low rungs and for H2H differences, though negative totals are rare in a full game.

Scalar series: KXNFLESCALATORRSHYDS (cubic in yards floored to tens, cap 200, negatives pay 0) and KXNFLLADDERRSHYDS (linear $0.0025 per yard, cap 400) now have rules text; neither states a non-participation refund, so an inactive or non-playing back appears to pay the zero-yard value (u9).
Protected variant: overtime appears only in the definition of post-half participation; whether overtime yards count and how a player with no first-half play settles are unstated and carried as u6.

KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS resolves No for a non-participant and 1/N on ties, while the binary yards, attempts and longest-rush series refund an active non-playing player at fair price and the H2H refunds if either player does not enter (the scalar escalator and ladder texts state no refund); one injury report therefore moves the variants in different directions.
KXNFLRSHATT counts official rushing attempts: QB scrambles and kneel-downs are rushing attempts, so a mobile QB's count includes scrambles, while a back's count comes from designed carries only.
contract.settlement_data_source: The sampled rules never name a provider; 'Governing League' official statistics are implied and the existing draft's mention of kneel-down counting is a statistical convention, not text in the rules.

mechanism.summary: A runner's rushing yards equal his carries times his yards per carry, and both have to be forecast through different chains. Carries are team rushing plays times the share this runner takes; team rushing plays come from total plays and run rate, which respond strongly to the score path (leaders run to burn clock, trailers abandon the run), and the share depends on his role in a committee by down, distance and the goal line, backup handoffs in blowouts, and his health and snap ramp. Yards per carry come from the blocking and the front he faces (box count, run gap), the runner's ability to create yards over what the blockers provide, and a heavy right tail from explosive runs that makes yardage rungs very discontinuous. For quarterbacks the same contract records scrambles and designed runs, which come from pressure and scheme instead. The settlement rules decide whether the position is refunded, lost or settled when a runner is injured or rested.

stages.name: Who carries the ball: lead back, committee and quarterback share
stages.description: The runner's share of team rushes is set by his designated role (early down, passing down, goal line, change of pace), by the quarterback's own designed runs, and by the competition for touches in the room. Committee rotations are partly predetermined and partly reactive to performance and fatigue. The prior is the last several games' carry share conditioned on game state, but a coaching change or an acquisition can reset it.
stages.distribution: Carry shares among backs are Dirichlet-like with strong negative correlation; a lead back's share is typically 55-80 percent of running back carries, with persistent regimes.

stages.name: Health, snap ramp and in-game exit
stages.description: Running backs carry the highest in-game injury rate among skill positions, and returning runners are held to snap counts; either removes carries quickly and non-linearly, and a loss of the lead back hands carries to the next on the depth chart rather than reducing the team's carries. The outcome is a mixture of full-workload, ramp, and early-exit scenarios.
stages.distribution: Mixture distribution with a large mass at truncated workloads (a back exits in perhaps 8-12% of games, assumption), producing a left tail not captured by the mean.

stages.name: Team rushing volume from plays and run rate
stages.description: Team rushes follow total plays (tempo and clock) times run rate; a low-PROE team has more neutral-situation runs, and a run-first coach keeps running under pressure. This stage determines the pool the share applies to, and is correlated with the quarterback and the line's health.
stages.distribution: Team rushes ~20-35 per game; moderately dispersed with weak positive skew from clock-killing finishes.

stages.name: Score path: leading offences run, trailing offences stop
stages.description: The pre-game margin distribution, realised as the game unfolds, determines late-game carry volume: favourites generate extra clock-killing carries (often to backups when starters rest), underdogs shift to the air by the third quarter. Garbage-time carries are low-efficiency and may be taken by a different back, so volume and yield change together.
stages.distribution: Margin ~ normal around the own-rating expected margin from nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior (sd ~13), never the spread; carries are convex in lead in the leader's fourth quarter and capped by the clock.

stages.name: Yards per carry: blocking, front and scheme match
stages.description: Yards before contact depend on the offensive line's run-block quality and the front and box count, while yards after contact depend on the runner. Zone-versus-gap scheme and the defensive front's per-gap weakness determine the run direction yield, and stacked boxes concede explosive plays when beaten. These interact, so an offence-defence pairing rather than separate rankings is needed.
stages.distribution: Yards per carry per game ~ 3.5-5.5 with a per-carry distribution heavily right-skewed (median 3, mean 4.4, long runs of 15+ are 5-8% of carries).

stages.name: Explosive-run tail and quarterback scramble yield
stages.description: One or two 20-plus runs decide whether a back clears a high rung, and these are property of the back, the blocking scheme and the opposing safeties. For a quarterback, scrambles on pressured plays and designed runs produce the yards, with yardage per scramble depending on coverage and the passer's speed.
stages.distribution: Compound of carries with a Pareto-like right tail; per-game rung probability for 100+ driven by 0-2 explosive runs.

stages.name: Contract rules: refunds, non-participation, ties
stages.description: Each variant maps availability and ties differently: the protected ladder refunds for first-half-only participation, H2H refunds when a player does not enter, the attempts and longest-rush series refund only an active player who never appears, and game-most gives No to a non-participant with 1/N on ties. A correct valuation applies a different participation probability to each payoff while sharing one carry and yardage forecast. The scalar series add two more payoff shapes on the same yardage distribution: the escalator is a cubic in yards floored to tens (value concentrated in the 120-200 yard tail) and the ladder is linear with a 400-yard cap (value equals the mean), and neither text refunds a non-playing back.
stages.distribution: Variant-specific payoff functions of the same yardage and participation random variables.

stages.name: Game rushing leader and carry-count rungs
stages.description: KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS compares the named runner with every ball carrier on both sides, so the opposing workhorse and a running quarterback are rivals; the projected winner's lead back usually holds the top because clock-killing carries come late. KXNFLRSHATT counts carries rather than yards, so it rests on carry share and team rush volume (stages s1-s4) with no yardage term, and KXNFLLONGRSH is a maximum over the runner's carries driven by the per-carry tail of nfl.rush_yardage_tail, which gives P(k+) per carry for k = 7 to 40 and so covers low strikes such as over 6.5 yards.
stages.distribution: Leader indicator from a joint simulation with a small 1/N tie mass; carry counts are overdispersed integers (variance about 1.5x the mean); longest rush is a maximum over carries of heavy-tailed per-carry draws.
