nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.label: Late-lead clock-killing carries: expected volume and yield by back
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.mechanism: Number of carries a runner takes while his team leads in the second half and their yards per carry, which differ from neutral-game carries because defences stack boxes and runs are designed to burn clock.
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.rationale: Volume rises for favourites but each carry yields less, so counting these carries at the average yards per carry overstates yardage, and the carries often go to a different back than the one who carried in neutral situations.
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.measurement: Using play-by-play from the last 3 seasons, for each team compute carries per game in second-half states with lead >= 7 by back, and yards per carry in those states (shrink toward the league leading-state yield with k=25 carries). Forecast = integral over pre-game margin distribution of lead-state carries x lead-state yield, using the back depth chart at the last report. Units: carries and yards per carry.
raw_data: pbp: rusher_id, run_gap, score_differential, game_seconds_remaining, yards_gained
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.why: Prevents the common error of letting spread-driven carries inflate expected yards at the neutral yards-per-carry rate in the favourite's own rung.

nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.label: Run-scheme versus defensive front match by gap and direction
nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.mechanism: Matches the offence's distribution of runs by gap and direction (inside zone, outside zone, power) and blocking scheme with the defence's yards-allowed by the same gap and its front alignment.
nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.rationale: Team-level rush defence hides that a front may be soft to the outside and stout inside; the runner's yardage depends on how often the offence attacks the weak gap.
nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.measurement: For each offence compute share of rushes by run_gap and run_location over the last 16 games (shrink to league with k=60 carries); for each defence compute yards per carry and success rate allowed by the same bins (shrink with k=40). Matchup score = sum over bins of offence share x (defence allowed - league), as expected yards over average per carry. Add nominal front type (odd/even) as a context flag.
raw_data: pbp: run_gap, run_location, rusher_id, defteam, yards_gained, success
nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.why: Converts opponent run defence from a single rank into a game-plan-specific yard expectation for each runner.

nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.label: Runner explosive-run rate (10+, 20+) and opponent explosive allowed
nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.mechanism: Per-carry probabilities of 10+ and 20+ yard runs for this runner and the matching rate the defence allows.
nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.rationale: The 100+ rung is rarely reached through steady 4-yard carries; it needs one or two long runs, and the per-carry explosive probability is a separate parameter with its own persistence and opponent dependence.
nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.measurement: For each runner, explosive rate over the last 25 games with half-life 12 games, shrunk to the position-role mean with k=60 carries; opponent factor = defence's allowed 10+ rate vs league over last 16 games (k=100); combine on a log scale; use in a compound simulation of yardage with carries from stage s1-s4. Output: P(10+), P(20+) per carry.
nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.why: Retained for reference only: its 10+/20+ per-carry rates are a subset of the catalog's nfl.rush_yardage_tail (P(k+) for k = 7-40, opponent-adjusted), which is staged instead in s6 and s8 so the yardage rungs, KXNFLLONGRSH and the game-leader simulation read one fitted tail.

nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.label: Quarterback scramble and designed-run yield conditioned on pressure
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.mechanism: For a quarterback: probability that a pressured dropback becomes a scramble, yards per scramble and designed-run carries per game by situation.
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.rationale: For quarterback rushing contracts yardage arises from scrambles under pressure and from scheme, not from handoffs; scramble conversion depends on coverage downfield and on the passer's mobility, and designed runs are a coaching feature.
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.measurement: For each QB, scrambles per pressured dropback and yards per scramble over the last 24 games (half-life 12), designed-run carries per game from the last 12; shrink with k=80 dropbacks (scramble) and k=5 games (designed). Opponent adjustment: opposing pressure rate (log-odds) and spy/contain tendencies from charting. Output: expected carries and yards with variance. Needs pressure flags from a charting vendor or the sack/hit proxy.
raw_data: pbp: qb_scramble, rushing_yards for QB, run_location
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.why: Provides the QB-specific mechanism for Drew Lock style 40+ rushing rungs in the protected series, which a running-back chain would misprice.

nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.label: Game rushing-yards leader: joint carry and yardage simulation for all ball carriers
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.mechanism: Draws one game script per simulation and allocates both teams' carries among backs and quarterbacks, so the game's rushing maximum and each named runner's chance of holding it are computed jointly.
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.rationale: KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS is lost if the opposing lead back or a scrambling QB out-rushes the named player. Carries are zero-sum within a backfield and the winning side's script adds late carries to its lead back, so the leader is concentrated on the projected winner's workhorse; independent marginals overstate committee backs and understate the favourite's lead back.
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.measurement: Per game: rushers with carry share >=8 percent over the last 4 games plus both starting QBs. Each simulation draws a final margin from own ratings (no spread), sets team rush attempts by the score-state run-rate surface (nfl.script response with own margin), splits carries by Dirichlet shares (last 6 games, half-life 3, shrink to depth-chart role with k=30 carries) and draws per-carry yards from nfl.rush_yardage_tail. 20,000 simulations; P(max) with 1/N tie credit; inactive named player fixed at No. As-of the inactive list.
free_sources: nflverse snap counts and depth charts
raw_data: pbp: rusher_id, rush_attempt, rushing_yards, qb_scramble, score_differential
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.why: Supplies the joint probability that the named runner has the most rushing yards in the game, which is the KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS payoff.

nfl.carries.reason: Role by down and goal line is the core of the share; must be conditioned on game state because committee splits shift by score.

nfl.script.reason: Score path decides leader carries; a convex function of lead in the second half, not a linear spread term. The catalog measurement centres the margin distribution on the sportsbook spread and total; only the score-state response surface is kept, and the margin distribution must come from own ratings (nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior or the own team-score model), never from market lines.

nfl.proe.reason: Neutral run rate sets the carry pool; weaker for a lead back's share but crucial for team volume.

nfl.pace.reason: Total plays bound rushes, but run-heavy low-pace teams still generate carries by clock use; weak alone.

nfl.rush_efficiency.reason: Team yards before contact and run blocking set the baseline yield; correlated with the OL input and needs opponent adjustment.

nfl.rb_efficiency.reason: Yards over expected and after contact are noisy and regress heavily; useful in small weight and for explosive tails.

nfl.run_defense.reason: Opponent front quality, box counts and stuff rate shape yield and volume; extended by the gap-level match.

nfl.ol.reason: Run-block continuity is a real driver but overlaps with rush_efficiency; keep as an availability adjustment.

nfl.skill_avail.reason: Backfield teammate availability redistributes carries, usually the single largest update on game day; partial pregame.

nfl.qb_rushing.reason: Designed runs and scrambles cannibalise carries and add competition, essential when the runner is a quarterback.

nfl.limited_player_discount.reason: Snap caps for returning backs are a first-order effect on carries; discount size is unspecified.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Cold, wind and rain raise run rate; the yield effect is smaller and sign-ambiguous.

nfl.in_game_exit_risk.reason: Backs have high exit hazard; the probability should be applied as a mixture, but exit is partly a function of workload.

nfl.garbage_time.reason: Garbage-time mass is the tail of the script distribution; keep as part of the script lattice and treat the benching effect via late-lead carry yield.

nfl.player_stat_variance.reason: Boom-bust is an output of carry count and explosive rate; naming it an input hides the two parameters that drive it.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Attempts and yards ladders on one player share information and enforce monotonicity; a consistency tool.

m.rules_text.reason: Variant differences in refunds and non-participation are material; the draft mislabelled this context but it is needed for every variant.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Observed rung frequencies mix quality and market bias; can calibrate a model's tails but does not generate the outcome.

m.volume_oi.reason: Liquidity metrics carry no information about yards gained by a runner.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades are prices; using them as inputs makes the model a market echo rather than a forecast of carries and yards.

nfl.rush_yardage_tail.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on nfl.carries x nfl.rush_yardage_tail: Yards in a game combine a number of carries with a heavy-tailed per-carry yield; the probability of a high run; non-linearity declared for this input) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s4) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: When a favourite leads in the second half the extra carries go to whichever runner is on the field, often the backup, and they gain fewer yards per carry because boxes are loaded; the lead back's expected yards therefore rise less than team carries, and the backup's rise more.
interactions.how_to_test: Split the lead back's carry share and yards per carry by lead state and quarter; compare to backups' in the same states.

interactions.mechanism: Yards before contact multiply blocking quality by the defence's weakness in the gaps the offence uses most; a strong line against a stout front in its chosen direction yields little, while a mediocre line attacking a soft gap does well.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress yards before contact on blocking score x gap-weighted front weakness; check the product term beats separate additive rankings.

interactions.mechanism: When the lead back is limited, carries move to the backup by more than the reduction in the lead's share and a third back often takes goal-line work, so the share vector shifts discontinuously at certain snap-count caps rather than smoothly.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate share vectors for games with lead back at 0, 1-50 and 51-100 percent of normal snaps and test for a break at the cap.

interactions.mechanism: Designed quarterback runs and scrambles use up goal-line and short-yardage carries that would go to the back, and the effect is largest when the quarterback is a runner and the opponent pressures heavily.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare back carries per game with and without a running quarterback, split by opponent pressure rate.

interactions.mechanism: Bad weather raises the run share, but whether yield per carry rises or falls with blocking style (zone/power versus perimeter runs) is a hypothesis only, not evidenced here; the net yardage effect is the sum of a volume gain and an unsigned yield change.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact weather indicators with run-scheme type in a yards model and see whether the net weather effect changes sign across schemes.

interactions.mechanism: Yards in a game combine a number of carries with a heavy-tailed per-carry yield; the probability of a high rung depends on the covariance of carries and explosive rate (a heavy workload gives more draws from the tail), so volume and explosiveness compound rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate yards with carries and explosive draws independent versus joint and compare P(100+) calibration across runner types.

interactions.mechanism: The probability that a lead back tops the game's rushing list rises steeply with his team's expected margin because late clock-killing carries go to the winner; for a committee back the same margin raises a teammate's chance instead, so the margin effect is conditional on carry-share concentration.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2016-2025 games, regress an indicator of leading the game in rushing on own-rating expected margin interacted with carry-share Herfindahl of the back's team.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in the leading side: carries accelerate once a lead exceeds about a touchdown late in the game and flatten once the clock is nearly exhausted
nonlinearities.why: Late-lead carries are mostly forced by the clock, so a spread of 3 and a spread of 10 differ in expected carries by more than the linear spread difference suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: a jump from near full workload to a capped share at the first game back
nonlinearities.why: Teams use snap counts on returning backs, so carry shares are step-like in practice rather than continuous in injury severity.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed: P(100+) is roughly linear in explosive rate times carries, while P(60+) is nearly independent of it
nonlinearities.why: The highest rungs are reached only through long runs; below it the steady-yardage mass determines the probability, so the response of rung probabilities to the explosive rate increases with the rung.

nonlinearities.shape: hazard-mixture: a point mass at truncated carries proportional to time of exit
nonlinearities.why: A first-half exit leaves a runner under most rungs regardless of efficiency, causing a bimodal outcome distribution for backs.

contract.settlement_definition: Twenty-seven live series, 21 with rules text (title-only: KXNFLOROY, KXNFLDROY, KXNFLOPOY, KXNFLDPOY, KXNFLCOACH, KXNFLHOFINDUCTEES). Single-winner awards resolve YES if the named candidate 'wins' the award from the named body: AP for KXNFLMVP ('AP Regular Season MVP'), OPOTY, DPOTY, OROTY, DROTY, COTY and CPOTY; Pro Football Writers of America for KXNFLEXECOTY; KXNFLWPMOTY (Walter Payton Man of the Year) and KXNFLPROOTY (Protector of the Year) name no body. COTY and EXECOTY list 'Tie/Co-Winners' as its own outcome. Monthly awards (KXNFLROTM, KXNFLPOTM) pay $1/N rounded down to the cent among N co-winners. Slot selections: KXNFLALLPRO (All-Pro First-Team, per side) and KXNFLALLROOK (PFWA All-Rookie, offence, defence and special teams) resolve on the selection 'as reported by one of the Source Agencies'; KXNFLAWARDFIN resolves on the named finalists and resolves No for every candidate if finalists are not announced before the winner; KXNFLHALLOFFAME resolves No once the 2027 class is announced without the candidate; KXNFLT100 (exact rank) and KXNFLT100TOP (top N) settle on the player-voted NFL Top 100 list. Specials (KXNFLMVPSPECIALS by division, KXNFLOPOYSPECIALS and KXNFLDPOYSPECIALS by conference) settle on the winner's team at the time of the announcement, 1/N across distinct groups for split co-winners. No series has an injury void; ballot close dates and the annual-award tie method are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If Derrick Moore wins the Pro Football AP Defensive Rookie of the Year in the 2026-27 season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The annual award is defined by the AP's Defensive Rookie of the Year, so the electorate is the AP panel and the candidate set is defensive rookies; there is no participation or games-played clause.

rules_evidence.quote: where N is the number of awarded players
rules_evidence.establishes: The monthly award can have several simultaneous winners, which pays 1/N and makes the outcome a set-valued selection; a candidate's expected payout is the probability of being in the winner set weighted by 1/N.

rules_evidence.quote: If the inductees are announced by any of the Source Agencies and Willie Anderson is not included, the market will resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Hall of Fame contracts settle on the announced class: a candidate not named when the class is announced resolves No, so the event is selection by the committee in that year's vote, with no carry-over.

rules_evidence.quote: voted on exclusively by active NFL players as published by the Governing League
rules_evidence.establishes: The Top 100 contract settles on a player-voted league list, a different electorate from the AP media panel, so peer reputation and the prior year's list drive it rather than media narrative.

rules_evidence.quote: wins the Pro Football AP Regular Season MVP
rules_evidence.establishes: The MVP contract settles on the AP regular-season award, so postseason performance cannot enter and the electorate is the AP media panel.

rules_evidence.quote: regardless of which team(s) they played for earlier in the season
rules_evidence.establishes: Division specials settle on the winner's team at announcement, so a mid-season trade moves a candidate's contribution to another division; the price is a sum of candidate win probabilities grouped by end-of-season team.

rules_evidence.establishes: Conference specials pay fractionally only when co-winners split across conferences; same-conference co-winners pay that conference in full.

rules_evidence.quote: This event includes offensive, defensive and special teams players.

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLOROY / KXNFLDROY / KXNFLOPOY / KXNFLDPOY / KXNFLCOACH (NFL-titled) are title-only, while their AP-titled twins (OROTY, DROTY, OPOTY, DPOTY, COTY) have rules naming the AP; whether the NFL-titled series settle on the same AP award is unverified.
Monthly awards (KXNFLROTM, KXNFLPOTM) cover roughly four or five games (the texts name only the month, see u5), so an injury or bye inside the window matters far more than for a season award.

KXNFLMVP rules text names the AP Regular Season MVP but not the ballot format, tie handling or ballot close date; a top-5 10-5-3-2-1 ballot is seen in search-result copies for 2023 and 2025 (primary page not fetched), the 2022 start year and the tie rule are unverified, and the ballot enters the model as parameters.

Coach of the Year and Comeback Player rules name the AP award only; both reward change relative to the prior season, a different driver from production, and COTY lists 'Tie/Co-Winners' as a separate outcome, so a named coach's treatment under a shared award is not stated.
Monthly window definition (calendar month versus week block) and MVP ballot format are not stated in sampled text and are carried as unresolved u5 and u7.

Multi-slot selections differ from single-winner awards: All-Pro and All-Rookie name one or two players per position, award finalists name three to five, a Hall of Fame class has a capped number of modern-era inductees, and the Top 100 contract is a rank cutoff, so a candidate competes for a slot rather than for first place.
KXNFLHALLOFFAME settles at the class announcement before the Super Bowl, months after the eligible career ended; season production plays no role, while finalist history and the class cap do.
Conference and division specials (OPOY/DPOY by conference, MVP by division) settle on the winner's team at announcement; co-winners in one group pay that group in full, split groups pay 1/N.
KXNFLAWARDFIN resolves every candidate No if finalists are not announced before the winner; KXNFLT100 settles on an exact rank (#3), a much narrower event than KXNFLT100TOP's top-N cutoff.

Non-production honours: KXNFLWPMOTY (community service, chosen from one nominee per team) and KXNFLEXECOTY (front-office executive) are decided on criteria unrelated to on-field statistics; KXNFLPROOTY (Protector of the Year) names no awarding body or criteria in its text.

Ballot format by award, modelled as parameters (voters V, places K, points vector w) with evidence status; sources are search-result copies of AP wire text only, no AP page was fetched (evidence_zblk/NFL_u7_ap_ballot.json): MVP 2025 V=50, K=5, w=10-5-3-2-1 (seen in search copies); MVP 2023 K=5, w=10-5-3-2-1 (seen in search copies); other seven AP awards 2025 K=5, w=10-5-3-2-1 (seen in search copies; Coach of the Year result reported as Vrabel 302/19 vs Coen 239/16); 2022 MVP top-5 with top-3 5-3-1 for the other awards: reported in search copies of an AP statement, unverified, and the season of the change to five places is unknown; pre-2022 single vote, voter count outside 2025 and tie rule: not found. PFWA (Executive of the Year), Hall of Fame selection, All-Pro, Walter Payton Man of the Year and the player-voted Top 100 use their own processes, not this ballot.

Blueprint-inherited context inputs (m.external_lines, m.quote_history, nfl.award_stats) are benchmark-only or weak and are not used by any stage of this record; they were detached from the archetype list by patch.

mechanism.summary: An award is decided by a bounded electorate that ranks candidates from what it saw, not from true value. The chain starts with who is eligible (rookie status, offence versus defence) and who plays enough to be considered. Production is then measured relative to the peers the voters implicitly compare against, mostly through the counting stats and milestones they remember (yards, touchdowns, sacks, interceptions) rather than efficiency. Team success acts as a multiplier, strongly for the MVP and the Coach of the Year. The narrative path (hot streak, late-season surge, primetime exposure, injury timing relative to ballots) moves a candidate within the list, and among close candidates the split of votes across teammates and similar profiles decides the points total. Finally the contract adds mechanics: ballot close, ties paying 1/N, and monthly windows with only a handful of games. Predictions must therefore be of voter behaviour on a candidate set, not of player quality. Three honours sit outside the production chain (Executive of the Year, Walter Payton Man of the Year, Protector of the Year) and need their own candidate models, and the conference/division specials are sums of candidate probabilities grouped by the winner's team.

stages.name: Eligibility and candidate pool
stages.description: Eligibility defines the pool: rookies for the Rookie awards, offence or defence for the position-split awards, the month window for monthly awards, and any quarterback bias in the MVP. Pool size is small (3 to 8 live candidates for a typical award at the end of the season) and non-uniform: recent history shows that most MVPs are quarterbacks on top seeds, while non-quarterbacks win Offensive Player of the Year.
stages.distribution: Candidate set is a short list; probability mass concentrated on 2-4 names with a long tail of those who need a late surge.

stages.name: Realised production relative to peers
stages.description: Voters see counting statistics and milestones: passing and rushing yards, touchdowns, sacks, interceptions, receptions, with a lean to visible plays. Production per game and cumulative both count, so injuries trade rate for volume. Production must be compared with the pool of candidates at the same position and across positions for the cross-position awards. Defensive candidates (DPOY, DROY) are scored on a sack, pressure, interception, tackle-for-loss composite and offensive skill candidates on EPA, all ranked within the eligible pool by nfl.position_peer_production_index, with banked totals extended by nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.
stages.distribution: Production totals approximately normal across the season with heavy tails for TDs; ranking relative to peers is what matters, and seasonal rank changes slowly late in the year.

stages.name: Team success multiplier
stages.description: Team record, seed and division title are strong predictors of award votes, especially for the MVP and Coach of the Year: the same stat line earns a vote share depending on the team's seed. The standings simulation gives the distribution of final record and seed, which is a function of the remaining schedule and injuries across the roster.
stages.distribution: Seed distribution is discrete; vote share is a step-like function of seed (top-seed premium) rather than linear in wins.

stages.name: Availability and games-played risk
stages.description: Injury and rest before the ballot date eliminate or discount candidates; an injury after ballots close has no effect. Because games missed have a visible penalty in voting, the probability of playing the remaining games matters in a non-linear way: missing a few games costs far less than missing a month.
stages.distribution: Games-played distribution with a mass at full availability and a left tail; voters apply a penalty that jumps at roughly 3+ missed games (assumption, to be estimated).

stages.name: Narrative, exposure and milestone effects
stages.description: Voters respond to milestones (1,000 yards, 2,000 yards, sack or touchdown records), to national-television performances and to recent games. The distinction between realised and expected production (touchdown luck) matters because voters do not regress, so the luck inflated stat line wins votes even if its true value is lower; the model should predict what voters see.
stages.distribution: Narrative effects are discrete and path dependent: a milestone or record chase produces a jump in the vote probability rather than a gradual change.

stages.name: Vote aggregation: ranked-points ballots (50-voter panel seen in search copies for the 2025 awards only) and vote splitting
stages.description: The AP awards are decided by ranked-points ballots from a media panel, not by first-place plurality, and the ballot is modelled as parameters per award and season (voters V, places K, points vector w) with explicit evidence status, as listed in nfl.vote_outcome_model: the MVP ballot with five places scored 10-5-3-2-1 and V=50 for 2025, and a top 5 scored 10-5-3-2-1 for all eight AP awards in the 2025 season, are seen in search-result copies of AP wire text, with the AP primary pages not fetched. A 2022 start of the ranked MVP ballot, a top-3 5-3-1 scheme for the non-MVP awards (reported in search copies of an AP statement, unverified, change season unknown), pre-2022 single-vote seasons, the voter count outside 2025 and the tie rule are unverified. The winner is the candidate with the most points, so second- to fifth-place support can beat a first-place-vote lead (reported in search copies as the 2025 MVP tally: Stafford 366 points with 24 firsts beat Maye 361 with 23; the season attribution of one cited page date is unconfirmed). Win probability is the chance a candidate's simulated point total exceeds every rival's under a ranked-ballot model; teammates and same-position rivals split first places but can both collect lower-place points, so the split penalty acts mainly on the first-place share. The aggregation itself is nfl.vote_outcome_model: a rank-ordered ballot model simulating V ballots per draw with that award-season's points vector; nfl.leader_order_statistic only supplies each candidate's production rank among peers as a ballot feature (it is not a max-of-production winner rule), and the split penalty adjusts first-place placements.
stages.distribution: Each voter's ballot ranks K candidates (K=5 seen in search copies for the MVP and, in 2025, every other AP award; other seasons' K unverified); the point total is a weighted sum of placement counts with heavy concentration on two or three finalists; ties in points are rare but possible, and the tie rule was not found

stages.name: Award-specific drivers: coaches, comebacks and monthly windows
stages.description: Coach of the Year follows the surprise in team wins relative to a pre-season expectation, Comeback Player depends on the severity of the prior-year setback, and monthly awards are decided on four or five games with the bye week removing games from some teams. These contracts need their own sub-model on top of the common chain.
stages.distribution: Window sums over 3-5 games have much higher variance than season totals; coach surprise is approximately normal in wins but selects the top few overachievers.

stages.name: Slot selections: All-Pro teams, finalists, Hall of Fame class and Top 100 rank
stages.description: Several honours are capacity-limited selections rather than a single plurality winner. All-Pro and All-Rookie fill one or two places per position from media ballots, finalists are the top three to five vote-getters, the Hall of Fame class is chosen by a committee from about fifteen modern-era finalists under a class cap, and the Top 100 is a rank produced by players' votes on the previous season. Probability comes from where a candidate sits in the queue for a slot, not from beating one favourite.
stages.distribution: Selection indicators with strong year-to-year persistence for Hall of Fame finalists and Top 100 ranks; capacity limits induce negative dependence among same-position candidates.

stages.name: Non-production honours: executive, Man of the Year and offensive-line protector
stages.description: KXNFLEXECOTY is a PFWA writers' vote on a general manager or front-office head, driven by the team's win improvement over its pre-season expectation and by how visibly the executive's moves (trades, free agents, draft class, coaching hire) explain it. KXNFLWPMOTY is chosen by a selection panel from 32 team nominees on community and charitable work plus on-field standing, so nominee status, tenure and media visibility of the charitable programme matter, not statistics. KXNFLPROOTY rewards an offensive lineman's protection, so pass-block pressure and sack allowance, games started and team sack rate, plus reputation, decide it. Each is a small-panel vote with sparse history, so priors dominate. The nominee-profile input is context only because roughly 16 past winners cannot support a fitted multinomial model (u10).
stages.distribution: Categorical over a small candidate set (often a clear favourite plus 3-6 contenders); very few historical winners, so posterior probabilities are wide and heavily prior-driven.

stages.name: Conference and division specials: grouping winners by team
stages.description: KXNFLMVPSPECIALS, KXNFLOPOYSPECIALS and KXNFLDPOYSPECIALS do not name a player: they pay if the winner's team at announcement is in a given division or conference. Their value is the sum of each candidate's win probability over candidates on teams in that group, so they inherit every candidate model above, plus correlation within groups (two NFC West quarterbacks split the same voters) and the small chance a candidate changes team by trade before the award. Co-winners pay the group in full when both are in it and 1/N across distinct groups otherwise.
stages.distribution: Sum of correlated candidate probabilities; group probabilities are concentrated (one or two groups carry most mass for MVP) with a fractional-payout atom for split co-winners.

talent_strength.note: Player production (cross-position index including a defensive composite), QB efficiency and team strength; the WEAK nfl.award_stats input is detached from this archetype and not used.

opponent_matchup.note: A season award is decided from a whole-season body of work, not from a specific opponent; opponent strength enters only through remaining schedule and through who the candidate faced in highlighted games, already in the schedule input.

role_personnel.note: Rookie role and position determine the candidate pool; cross-position comparison uses the position-peer production index (the WEAK fantasy-points translation is detached).

availability_news.note: Games-played attrition and news before the ballot; ballot close timing is in award_voting_mechanics.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach of the Year relies on team over-performance; scheme is relevant to players only through production.

environment.note: Weather, venue and altitude affect single games, not an annual vote; their effect is absorbed in the production and record that voters see.

game_context_script.note: Accrual and remaining opportunity for milestone chases.

pace_volume.note: Remaining games and the number of games in the monthly window.

efficiency_conversion.note: Production versus expected; voters see raw totals but regression shows which leaders are fragile.

distribution_variance.note: Ranked-points ballot aggregation (nfl.vote_outcome_model) with a vote-split penalty for similar candidates; the leader statistic is only a production-rank feature of the ballot model, not a plurality or max-of-production winner rule.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Remaining schedule and primetime exposure; clinch-driven rest reduces counting stats late (not modelled).

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not influence a voting outcome; any penalty effect on production is already inside the stat line.

settlement_contract.note: Awarding body per series, 1/N for monthly co-winners and split specials, finalist no-announcement rule, Tie/Co-Winners outcome; annual-tie rule and ballot close remain unresolved.

nfl.award_milestone_proximity.label: Milestone and record proximity for each candidate
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.mechanism: Distance of a candidate's projected final total from round-number or record milestones that voters respond to (e.g. 2,000 rushing yards, 5,000 passing yards, 20 sacks, franchise or league records).
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.rationale: Vote probability is not smooth in production: reaching a milestone adds a discrete narrative bump and a record chase draws attention for several weeks, so award probability has a cliff near thresholds.
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.measurement: Per candidate and award: thresholds T_k = round-number milestones (e.g. 1,000/1,500/2,000 rush yds, 4,000/5,000 pass yds, 15/20 sacks) plus the career or season record for the stat, and the 20th percentile of prior winners' totals over the 15 seasons ending before the scored season. Projected final total = banked total + sum over remaining games of expected stat per game (rate over the last 8 games, half-life 4, shrunk to career rate with k=4 games) x P(plays) from nfl.games_played_dist; normal approximation with game-level variance from nfl.player_stat_variance. Feature = P(final >= T_k) and games needed at current rate. As-of after each week's games.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference season stats and award voting history
raw_data: historical AP award winners with their season stat lines
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.why: Captures threshold effects in voting that a smooth production-to-vote function misses, especially for OPOY, DPOY and rookie awards driven by round-number totals.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.label: Teammate and look-alike candidate vote-splitting penalty
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.mechanism: Reduction in a candidate's ballot placements caused by another strong candidate with the same team, position or narrative; under ranked-points ballots it acts mostly on first-place share, because both rivals can still collect lower-place points.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: AP awards are ranked-points ballots (MVP 10-5-3-2-1 over five places and, in 2025, the other AP awards too, all seen in search-result copies with the AP primary page not fetched; earlier non-MVP schemes are reported but unverified), so two similar candidates split first places but not all support: a candidate can win on second- and third-place points (reported in search copies as the 2025 MVP tally: Stafford 366 points with 24 firsts, Maye 361 with 23; season attribution unconfirmed). A penalty fitted to first-place shares under plurality overstates the split for ranked seasons and must be estimated by regime.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: Rank-ordered logit latent utility for candidate i on voter ballot = x_i'theta - beta_r x max over same-team or same-position rivals j of x_j'theta, where x are the nfl.vote_outcome_model features and r indexes the placement (first place versus lower places). Estimate theta and beta_r by maximum likelihood on placement counts per candidate for seasons with published AP placement counts, with places K and points w read per award and season (see the ballot-parameter table in nfl.vote_outcome_model; evidence status per parameter is explicit there), and on first-place vote shares under a Dirichlet-multinomial for the pre-2022 seasons as a separate single-vote regime (the single-vote format is UNVERIFIED and the 2005 start is an arbitrary sample window); ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, shrink beta_r toward 0. Output winner probabilities from simulated V-voter ballots scored by that award-season's points vector. As-of ballot close.
raw_data: AP vote shares by candidate-season, team, position
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.why: Needed to make winner probabilities sum to one and to price second-tier candidates on a team that has a front runner.

nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.label: Rookie opportunity: draft capital, starter status and snap/role share
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.mechanism: Draft pick number, starter status in Week 1 and cumulative snap share of rookies, plus team context (quarterback, line) that gives opportunities.
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.rationale: Rookie awards go to rookies who played substantial roles on visible teams; draft capital predicts both opportunity and the voters' prior, and the role is determined by early-season depth charts and injuries ahead of him.
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.measurement: For each rookie at as-of week w (w >= 1): features = log(draft pick), depth chart rank in the week-w report, snap share and touches (or pressures) per game over games 1..w-1 shrunk to the draft-slot mean with weight (w-1)/(w-1+3). Target = rest-of-season production per game (weeks w..17). Fit OLS/ridge on 2010-2025 rookies separately by position group, evaluated by leave-one-season-out. Output expected rest-of-season production and SD. Never use games on or after the as-of week; for w=1 use draft capital and preseason depth chart only.
free_sources: nflverse draft picks and snap counts
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.why: Defines the viable candidate set and base rates for KXNFLDROTY, KXNFLOROTY, KXNFLROTM and Rookie All-Team, the awards sampled in the rules text.

nfl.award_month_window_games.label: Monthly award window: games, byes and stat accrual inside the calendar window
nfl.award_month_window_games.mechanism: Number of games each candidate's team plays in the contract's calendar month and the candidate's stat production within that window.
nfl.award_month_window_games.rationale: Monthly awards are decided on three to five games, so a team on a bye, a rest day or a Thursday game changes the sample; a candidate with five games has more chances than one with three.
nfl.award_month_window_games.measurement: For each award month, from the league schedule: games per team in the window (3, 4 or 5); expected stats per game from the candidate's role and an opponent adjustment; window total = sum over games; standard deviation scaled by sqrt(games) with game-level variance from the player's last 20 games. Output probability that the candidate leads the window at his position.
nfl.award_month_window_games.why: The October rookie-of-the-month sample contract is decided inside a short window; opportunities vary by bye and the model must use the real game count.

nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.label: Coach surprise: wins above own pre-season expectation
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.mechanism: Team win total minus the expected wins from a pre-season rating built without betting-market inputs (own roster and last-year efficiency prior).
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.rationale: Coach of the Year is a vote for surprise rather than quality, so the relevant measure is outcome minus prior expectation; using a sportsbook win total would import a market price as an input, so the prior must be from the model's own rating.
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.measurement: Preseason expected wins E0 = sum over all scheduled games of P(win_g) from the Week-1 frozen own rating (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free preseason prior: last-year efficiency regressed with roster continuity and a QB-change term; no sportsbook win total). Projected final wins W = banked wins + sum over remaining games of the current rating's win probability (or mean of nfl.standings_sim). Surprise = W - E0 in wins; optional tiebreak bonus = 0.5 x P(division title) x historical COY winners' division-title share. As-of after each week; E0 never re-estimated in season.
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.why: Gives KXNFLCOTY (and the Comeback/COTY style awards) a quantity that responds to over-performance, which the existing production-based inputs lack.

nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.label: Voter exposure: primetime games, national attention and public straw polls
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.mechanism: Count of primetime and national games for the candidate's team so far and standing in published writers' ballots or straw polls from non-market sources.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.rationale: Voters see the nationally televised games and discuss candidates in public straw polls; this is a signal of voter sentiment distinct from production and is not a market price.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.measurement: Primetime-game counts and share of the candidate's yards or touchdowns in those games to date; rank in published straw polls (e.g. by members of the voting panel) at each week (rank points via Borda). Combined into one score with weights from historical regression on vote share, as-of each Tuesday; no betting prices or Kalshi quotes used.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.why: Provides a voter-behaviour signal without importing prices, helping to distinguish the front runner from candidates with equal production.

nfl.position_peer_production_index.label: Cross-position production index versus peers (offence and defence)
nfl.position_peer_production_index.mechanism: Converts a candidate's season-to-date production into a position-neutral standing among eligible candidates, using EPA-based value for offensive players and a defensive-production composite for defenders.
nfl.position_peer_production_index.rationale: The record's production stage relied on WEAK inputs and one QB-only input, so DPOY, DROY and OPOY (skill positions) had no calibrated production measure. Voters compare a sack leader with a coverage corner, so a within-position percentile is needed; it must also be shrunk for small samples early in the season.
nfl.position_peer_production_index.measurement: Offensive: per-game EPA contributed (QB: EPA per dropback x dropbacks per game + 0.5 x CPOE-based EPA; RB/WR/TE: rushing or receiving EPA per game from pbp) converted to a z-score vs all same-position players over 2015-2025 at the same week of season; Defenders: z = 0.40 sacks/g + 0.20 QB hits/g + 0.15 TFL/g + 0.15 (interceptions + passes defended)/g + 0.10 forced fumbles/g using only public weekly fields (no pressures), weights fit by conditional logit on past DPOY voting, ridge toward the stated values. Shrink z toward 0 with weight g/(g+5) (g=games). Rank within eligible pool (rookie flag for rookie awards); output rank and z-gap to next. As-of last completed week.
free_sources: nflverse weekly player stats (sacks, QB hits, interceptions, passes defended, TFL)
raw_data: weekly player stats: player_id, week, position, sacks, qb_hits, def_interceptions, passes_defended, tackles_for_loss, forced_fumbles
nfl.position_peer_production_index.why: Gives DPOY/DROY/OPOY/OROY a production measure that is comparable across positions, instead of the weak award-stats and QB-only fields.

nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.label: Rest-of-season statistical projection to the ballot cutoff
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.mechanism: Projects each candidate's final regular-season totals by adding expected remaining-game production to banked totals, with a games-played hazard.
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.rationale: Awards are voted on final-season body of work, and Kalshi prices trade in October to January while about half the games remain; ranking by banked stats ignores that a candidate on a bye or with a tough schedule will fall behind. The projection is for production rank, not a price.
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.measurement: Projected total = banked total + sum over remaining games g of P(plays g) x expected per-game rate_g, where the per-game rate is a 50/50 blend of season-to-date per-game rate and a 3-year prior (shrunk with k=6 games), scaled by opponent defence adjustment from nfl.schedule_strength (+-10 percent cap) and by P(plays g) from nfl.games_played_dist; uncertainty from a negative-binomial per-game sd fitted on 2015-2025. As-of: before the next kickoff window; cutoff = last regular-season game (ballot close date assumed at the end of the regular season, unverified, see u3).
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.why: Turns banked production into a projected final production rank, the quantity voters ultimately compare, at the date the contract trades.

nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.label: Hall of Fame candidate progression: years as semifinalist and finalist, category and class cap
nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.mechanism: Hall of Fame induction is a committee vote in which candidates usually advance from semifinalist to finalist over several years and the modern-era class is capped, so the candidate's place in that queue predicts selection.
nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.rationale: Career statistics are fixed long before the vote; what changes year to year is the candidate's standing with the selectors (consecutive finalist years, first-ballot status of competing candidates at the same position) and the class cap, so a resume-only model misses the queue that decides KXNFLHALLOFFAME.
nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.measurement: For each candidate and year 2000-2026: category (modern-era, seniors, coach/contributor), years eligible, count of prior semifinalist and finalist years, whether a first-year-eligible candidate at the same position is on the finalist list, and the modern-era class size. Logistic model of induction among finalists with candidate random effect, shrinkage to the category base rate with k=10 finalist-years; output P(inductee) as-of the finalist announcement and again after the class announcement date is known.
free_sources: Pro Football Hall of Fame semifinalist, finalist and class announcements (public pages, manual capture)
Pro-Football-Reference Hall of Fame pages (terms unchecked)
raw_data: candidate, category, position, semifinalist/finalist/inducted flags by year
nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.why: Sets the probability that a named candidate is in the announced class, which is the only event KXNFLHALLOFFAME and KXNFLHOFINDUCTEES settle on.

nfl.executive_move_attribution.label: Executive of the Year attribution: win surprise explained by front-office moves
nfl.executive_move_attribution.mechanism: Scores each team's general manager by the team's wins above its own pre-season expectation, weighted by the share of that surprise attributable to new acquisitions, the draft class and a new head coach.
nfl.executive_move_attribution.rationale: The PFWA executive vote rewards a visible turnaround that writers credit to roster building; a team that over-performs on luck or an incumbent star does not earn the same credit, so win surprise alone over-predicts and the attribution share is the subtle part.
nfl.executive_move_attribution.measurement: For each team-season: win surprise = actual wins minus own pre-season expected wins (from nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior's prior); acquisition share = snap-weighted approximate value (PFR AV) of players new to the roster this season (trades, free agents, rookies) divided by total team AV; new-coach flag. Score = win surprise x (0.5 + acquisition share) + 1.0 x new-coach flag; softmax over teams with temperature fitted to PFWA winners 2000-2025, candidate shrinkage k=5 seasons. As-of each week; final as-of end of regular season.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference team rosters and approximate value (terms unchecked)
raw_data: PFWA Executive of the Year winners
nfl.executive_move_attribution.why: Gives KXNFLEXECOTY a candidate model; none of the player-award inputs describes front-office credit.

nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.label: Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee profile: community record, prior nominations and visibility
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.mechanism: Ranks the 32 team nominees by indicators the selection panel uses: scale and tenure of the nominee's charitable work, prior nominations, veteran status and media visibility of the cause.
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.rationale: The award ignores on-field statistics beyond standing; repeat nominees, long-running foundations and veterans near retirement win disproportionately. There is no structured data on charitable work, so the input is a hand-coded profile with a strong prior on repeat nominees.
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.measurement: For each nominee-year 2010-2025: number of prior nominations, years in the league, Pro Bowl count (standing proxy), foundation existence and age in years, count of national news articles on the charity in the 12 months before announcement (manual or news-API count). Multinomial logit over the year's 32 nominees fitted to past winners with ridge penalty; shrink coefficients toward equal probability with k=8 award-years. As-of nominee announcement (December).
free_sources: NFL.com Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee announcements (manual)
raw_data: nominee list by year and team
prior nominations, seasons played, Pro Bowls
foundation founding year and news counts
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.why: Provides the only candidate model for KXNFLWPMOTY, whose outcome is unrelated to production inputs. Estimability limit: about 32 nominees per year and one winner per year over 2010-2025 give roughly 16 winners, too few to fit a multinomial model reliably, so it is context and not a primary estimator.

nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.label: Offensive-lineman protection record: pressures and sacks allowed per pass-block snap
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.mechanism: Measures an offensive lineman's pass protection (pressures and sacks allowed per pass-block snap, penalties), games started and team context, the evidence a Protector of the Year vote would reward.
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.rationale: Linemen have no counting statistics in box scores, so voters lean on charting grades, reputation (prior All-Pro/Pro Bowl) and team sack rate; the individual pressure-allowed rate is paid charting data and team sack rate confounds the quarterback's habits, which is the subtle part.
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.measurement: Per lineman-season to date: pressures allowed and sacks allowed per 100 pass-block snaps (PFF or SIS charting), penalties per 100 snaps, starts, and team sack rate adjusted for QB time to throw; shrink each rate toward position mean with k=300 pass-block snaps; composite z-score plus prior-honour indicator (All-Pro or Pro Bowl in last 2 seasons). As-of each week; final as-of end of regular season.
raw_data: lineman pass-block snaps, pressures and sacks allowed
team sack rate and QB time to throw
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.why: KXNFLPROOTY and the All-Pro offensive-line slots depend on protection evidence that no production input supplies.

nfl.award_stats.reason: The entry says only 'production and historical voting model' with no calculation; it merges production, narrative and voting history, and should be replaced by specified inputs (milestones, split penalty, exposure). Detached from season_awards by patch in round 7 (WEAK, staged nowhere); only the blueprint-inherited award_stats remains and is not used.

nfl.standings_sim.reason: Voters reward team success; the seed distribution, not wins, is the key quantity, and the simulation must include the top-seed premium.

nfl.award_voting_mechanics.reason: Electorate size, ballot date and tie rules decide what information can still matter; currently only a label without data on AP versus NFL-titled variants.

nfl.news.reason: Injury and suspension news matter only before ballots close; role changes are meaningful for rookies.

nfl.games_played_dist.reason: Missed games before ballots are the main route to eliminating a leading candidate; the penalty is non-linear.

nfl.qb_efficiency.reason: Relevant for MVP and quarterback-dominated awards, but voters weight totals and team success more than efficiency; irrelevant for defensive and non-quarterback awards.

nfl.td_luck.reason: Useful to assess fragility of leaders but voters do not regress, so it predicts reversion of future games rather than votes.

nfl.season_to_date_pace.reason: Accrual plus remaining games defines milestone chances; duplicates the standard season-stat projection.

nfl.schedule_strength.reason: Voters rarely adjust for schedule strength, and remaining strength moves production slightly; weak for the voting process itself.

m.quote_history.reason: The Kalshi price path is market output; it can calibrate narrative momentum after the fact but it is not a driver of the vote. Detached from the archetype list in round 7; inherited blueprint context is not used here.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook award odds are another market price; the draft listed them as a primary input, which would make a model an echo of other odds. Detached from the archetype list in round 7; inherited blueprint context is not used here.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the awarding body, window, eligibility and tie payment; two of the sampled series show different bodies (AP vs league).

nfl.leader_order_statistic.reason: Under ranked-points ballots the winner has the most ballot points, not the top statistic; the max-of-N production rank is kept only as a ballot feature inside nfl.vote_outcome_model and misses placement and vote splitting on its own.

nfl.fantasy_points_model.reason: A position-neutral fantasy translation is not what voters use; defensive awards have no fantasy analogue, and the PPR weighting differs from voter preferences. Detached from season_awards by patch in round 7 (WEAK, staged nowhere); only the blueprint-inherited award_stats remains and is not used.

nfl.vote_outcome_model.reason: The ranked-ballot aggregation, parametrised by voters, places and points vector per award and season (10-5-3-2-1 for the MVP and, in 2025, every AP award is seen in search-result copies only; earlier non-MVP schemes, the 2022 start and the pre-2022 single vote are unverified) that converts candidate features into winner and finalist probabilities; it is the stage s6 aggregator.

interactions.mechanism: MVP voters effectively require a top-two seed for quarterbacks: below that line a leading efficiency edge earns little, above it the same edge translates into most of the first-place votes. The effect of production is therefore conditional on the seed distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare winners' seeds historically and fit vote share as a function of production separately for seeded and unseeded candidates.

interactions.mechanism: A record or milestone chase concentrates the narrative when the candidate is on pace with games to spare; missed games reduce both the total and the probability of reaching the threshold, so the milestone effect is conditional on staying healthy through the remaining weeks.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(milestone) with and without injury risk; compare vote-share residuals for candidates who reached versus narrowly missed thresholds.

interactions.mechanism: Candidates with correlated support (same team, same position) have negatively correlated chances of winning, so the joint distribution of winners is not a product of marginals; a rival's collapse benefits his teammate more than the field.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a joint vote model on historical ballots and compare the log-likelihood to independent softmax; test beta > 0.

interactions.mechanism: An injury changes a candidate's vote probability by an amount that depends on whether it occurs before or after ballots close and on how many games remain, so the ballot model must be fed the injury and the ballot-close date together, not the injury alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Split news events by weeks before ballot close and measure change in vote share and in the model's own ballot-based probabilities.

interactions.mechanism: Touchdown luck is rewarded by voters only when it is visible: the vote-share boost from touchdown counts above expectation is multiplied by primetime and highlight exposure, so for a low-exposure candidate a lucky touchdown total adds little, while for a high-exposure candidate it adds vote share even though regression predicts it will fade.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress past vote share on td_luck x exposure index (primetime snaps share, straw-poll rank) and test the product term against td_luck and exposure alone.

interactions.mechanism: For a monthly rookie award the chance to be selected is roughly proportional to the number of games in the window times expected production per game, so a high draft slot with a bye in the window can lose to a lower slot with five games.
interactions.how_to_test: Model window outcomes with games in window as an exposure term and test the coefficient against 1.

interactions.mechanism: Executive and Coach of the Year voters credit the same turnaround to different people: when a new head coach arrives with few roster additions, writers credit the coach; when the roster turned over through trades and free agency under an incumbent coach, they credit the executive, so the two awards' candidate probabilities for one team are partly substitutes conditional on the cause of the win surprise.
interactions.how_to_test: Across 2000-2025 team-seasons with win surprise above +3, compare the rate of COTY versus Executive of the Year wins by new-coach flag and acquisition-share tercile.

nonlinearities.shape: step-like: vote share jumps at the first seed or division title and is flat elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: Voter behaviour treats a number-one seed as a qualification, so the expected vote is a step in seed rather than linear in wins.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: nearly no penalty for 1-2 missed games, steep penalty beyond about 3 missed games
nonlinearities.why: A candidate who misses three or more games is often dropped from the ballot, so award probability is not linear in games played.

nonlinearities.shape: cliff near round-number thresholds and records; flat elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: Voters remember totals like 2,000 yards or the single-season sack record, so probability changes sharply across the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: square-root scaling of variance with games in the window, with a mean proportional to games
nonlinearities.why: A 5-game window has a different winner distribution than a 3-game window; ignoring the count mis-estimates the favourite's probability by changing both mean and sd.

contract.settlement_definition: Twenty-two live series, 19 with rules text (title-only: KXNFLLEADERPINT, KXNFLCAREERRSHTDS, KXNFLSEASONRUSHYDS). Season rungs (KXNFLSEASONPASSYDS, SEASONPASSTDS, SEASONRSHYDS, SEASONRSHTD, SEASONRECYDS, SEASONREC, SEASONRECTD) resolve YES if the player 'records N+' of the statistic 'during the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season'; missed games have no refund. KXNFLTSPEC (team specials) uses regular-season stats only, counts a traded player's combined totals across teams, and defines team passing yards as net of sack yardage. Career rungs (KXNFLCAREERPASSYDS 89,215+, CAREERRECYDS 22,896+, CAREERRSHYDS 18,356+) count career regular-season totals reached before the player or a Source Agency announces his retirement. Record series resolve YES only if the record is broken, not tied: KXNFLSZNRECORD (rookie sacks, 14.5), KXNFLSACKRECORD (season sacks, more than 22.5) and KXNFLRECYDSRECORD (season receiving yards, more than 1,964); the sampled record markets are for the 2025-26 season. Weekly-most series (KXNFLWEEKMOSTPASSYDS/RECYDS/RSHYDS) are maxima over all players in the week: No for a non-participant, 1/N on ties. Team extremes (KXNFLTEAMPTS most/least points scored, KXNFLTEAMDPTS fewest/most points allowed) are over all teams for the whole regular season with dead-heat 1/N on ties. No text states overtime treatment or the statistics source.

variants_and_edge_cases: Season rungs are one-sided and unrefunded: a player who misses the season fails the rung, unlike per-game ladders with a void rule, so games-played risk is a loss and not a refund.
Weekly-most series resolve over every player in the week and give No to a non-participant with 1/N on ties; the contender set is an open field, not a list of names.

Career rungs end at a retirement announcement and the sampled strikes equal the all-time record plus one (Brady 89,214 passing, Rice 22,895 receiving, Emmitt Smith 18,355 rushing), so the horizon is several seasons and the contract expiry date, not visible in the sample, may end it earlier (u1).

KXNFLSZNRECORD (rookie sacks, 'broken, not tied', 14.5) and KXNFLSACKRECORD (season sacks, more than 22.5) are defensive accruals and KXNFLLEADERPINT (title-only) is presumably an interceptions leader; they need individual defender inputs, unlike the offence-yardage series.
The 2026-27 schedule has 18 weeks with 17 games per team, so remaining games differ by team through byes, and Week 17-18 rest of clinched starters truncates the final total.
KXNFLSEASONRSHYDS (rules sampled) and KXNFLSEASONRUSHYDS (title-only) share the title 'Rushing Yards' and may be one series spelled twice (u7).

Team extremes (KXNFLTEAMPTS, KXNFLTEAMDPTS) pay 1/N dead heats over tied teams and cover the entire regular season; KXNFLTSPEC's team stat definitions are truncated in the sample after 'Team Passing Yards: Recorded as net yards', so other team stat definitions are unseen (u8).
KXNFLTSPEC player markets count combined statistics across teams after a trade, while the record and weekly series do not mention trades.

mechanism.summary: A season statistic is the sum over games played of a per-game output, and the contract is decided by three quantities that are separate in kind: how many games the player appears in (a discrete attrition process), what per-game rate he runs at once on the field (a role and efficiency process that is autocorrelated within the season and can switch regimes after an injury, trade or coaching change), and the realised total already banked. For threshold contracts the probability is the chance that banked plus remaining output crosses the rung, which depends on remaining games and the variance of the sum, larger than independent-game variance because of the persistent role state. For leader contracts the question is a maximum over many correlated contenders, where covariance among teammates and shared schedules matters and the open field of unlisted players holds real mass. Late-season rest of clinched teams and weather add a seasonal truncation to the final weeks. Team-level series (most/least points scored and allowed, team specials) follow the same banked-plus-remaining logic at team grain, with the extreme taken over the league's teams.

stages.name: Banked total and games remaining
stages.description: Season-to-date output is known, so the forecast begins from the realised accrual and counts the games each team still plays, with byes and the Week 18 finale deciding how many chances remain. The remaining chances are discrete and unevenly spread across contenders: one player with four games left behind another with five changes the leader odds by a visible margin.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the schedule; remaining games are 0 to 17, and early in the season most of the variance is in the not-yet-played games.

stages.name: Availability: games played and attrition
stages.description: Each remaining game has an appearance probability set by injury status, age and position, suspension risk and (late) rest by clinched teams. Attrition is a hazard process with absences clustering across weeks (a hamstring injury costs several games), so the games-played count has a heavy left tail and strong dependence on the current report.
stages.distribution: Discrete count; near-binomial but with clustered absences, so variance exceeds binomial; mass at 0 additional games for players on injured reserve.

stages.name: Role and usage regime across the remaining season
stages.description: The per-game rate depends on a role state (target share, carry share, snap share) which persists but can change when a teammate is hurt, a depth chart is reshuffled, an offensive coordinator is replaced or a player is traded. Regimes are detected late and priced late, so the regime-change hazard widens the distribution beyond what current usage implies.
stages.distribution: Mixture of regimes: stable role with persistent shares plus a small probability of a shift of 20-40 percent in share (assumption), producing season-level variance beyond sum of independent games.

stages.name: Team volume and efficiency conversion
stages.description: Passing and rushing opportunity come from the team's plays and pass rate, and yield from the quarterback and line; touchdown totals regress heavily and so the per-game expected touchdown rate must be separated from the realised one. A quarterback change can reset volume and efficiency for every skill player on the team.
stages.distribution: Per-game output is a compound count with overdispersion; touchdown counts are low-count Poisson-like with strong regression to role-based expectation.

stages.name: Distribution of the remaining sum with persistent state
stages.description: Remaining output is the sum of games with a within-season autocorrelation: good weeks cluster with a stable role and bad weeks with changed role, so the standard deviation of the sum is larger than sqrt(n) times single-game standard deviation. The distribution over games played and rate is a compound mixture rather than a normal.
stages.distribution: Compound with positive intra-season correlation (roughly 0.1-0.3 at the game-rate level, assumption); right-skewed for touchdowns and receptions.

stages.name: Leader order statistic and contender covariance
stages.description: For a leader contract the event is that one player's total exceeds every rival's: the probability depends on the gap, the remaining games and the dispersion of each contender, and on covariance (teammates share volume negatively for rushing, positively for team-level volume), and is not a product of marginals. The field of less-visible contenders carries mass for position-wide leaders.
stages.distribution: Maximum of N correlated heavy-tailed totals; the probability of leading is a steep function of gap divided by remaining-sum standard deviation.

stages.name: Weekly leaders and settlement rules
stages.description: Weekly leader contracts are single-game maxima over the full player pool, so the tail of the per-game distribution and the ties convention (1/N) matter and are completely different from cumulative leader contracts; regular-season-only wording and statistic source decide eligibility.
stages.distribution: Single-game maximum of ~hundreds of players; heavy right tail; dead-heat splitting of ties.

stages.name: Career record chases and defensive season accruals
stages.description: The career series are set one unit above the all-time records, so they ask whether a player in his late twenties or thirties keeps playing long enough at a high enough rate: the gap, an age decline curve and a retirement or release hazard decide them, and a retirement announcement ends the contract. The rookie and all-player season sack records (14.5 and 22.5, both must be broken) and the interceptions leader are defensive accruals: pass-rush snaps, pressure rate and a heavily regressed conversion to sacks, or coverage targets and an interception rate.
stages.distribution: Career attainment is a survival-weighted mixture over 0-6 more seasons with a heavy left tail from retirement; individual sack and interception season totals are overdispersed Poisson counts with strong regression of conversion rates.

stages.name: Team season totals and league-wide team extremes
stages.description: KXNFLTEAMPTS and KXNFLTEAMDPTS ask which team scores or allows the most or fewest points over the regular season, and KXNFLTSPEC includes team statistics such as net passing yards. Each team's final total is banked points plus the sum over remaining games of its points for or against, which depends on its offence and defence ratings separately, the remaining opponents, pace and the clinched-team rest of starters in Weeks 17-18. The extreme is an order statistic over the league's teams with shared rating uncertainty, and dead heats pay 1/N. Net team passing yards subtract sack yardage, so pass protection enters the team total but not the player passing totals.
stages.distribution: Sum of remaining-game team scores (approximately normal with sd about 35-45 points over 8 games) plus banked total; the extreme over teams is a max/min order statistic with mass concentrated on two or three teams by mid-season.

talent_strength.note: QB prior and regression of touchdown totals; position-specific skill priors for non-QBs are not attached.

opponent_matchup.note: Remaining opponent defences and who a contender competes against for volume.

role_personnel.note: Usage shares and the hazard that they change.

coaching_scheme.note: Coordinator change and play-caller turnover are the coaching route to a role shift; coach tendencies are not otherwise attached.

environment.note: Season totals sum 17 games across venues and weather, which average out; December weather changes pass rates in individual games but is second-order for a season-long total.

pace_volume.note: Team volume tendencies and games remaining.

efficiency_conversion.note: Yield per opportunity and touchdown regression.

distribution_variance.note: Season-sum variance with persistent state, max over contenders and single-game maxima.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Resting of starters after seeds are clinched; short-week fatigue is not modelled.

officiating_rules.note: No officiating mechanism changes a season total in a way separate from usage and efficiency; league-wide rule changes affect the baseline across seasons, handled by using current-season rates.
