nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.label: Role-regime change hazard (trade, teammate injury, coordinator change)
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.mechanism: Probability per week that a player's share of targets, carries or snaps shifts materially because of an event outside his own performance.
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.rationale: Season projections assume the current role persists; events that rewrite a depth chart or play-calling are the main source of large forecast errors and do not appear in per-game variance.
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.measurement: From 2012-2025 weekly data, define a regime shift as a change of at least 25 percent in a 4-game rolling usage share relative to the prior 4 games; estimate hazard per week by event type (teammate injury, trade, coordinator change, rookie return) with logistic regression, shrunk with k=20 events per type; apply to each contender conditional on the current team state; output expected share distribution (mixture) for the remaining games.
free_sources: nflverse weekly stats, rosters, transactions (roster moves)
raw_data: team transactions and coaching staff changes with dates
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.why: Adds the largest unmodelled variance source for season totals: a 25 percent share change on 8 remaining games moves a season total by far more than game-level noise.

nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.label: Within-season persistence of per-game rate (variance components)
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.mechanism: Decomposition of per-game output variance into a persistent player-season component and a game-level noise component.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.rationale: Season-sum variance is sqrt(n) times game sd only if games are independent; role persistence makes the sum more dispersed, so the probability of reaching distant rungs is larger than an independent model says.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.measurement: For each position x stat in {targets, receptions, receiving yards, carries, rushing yards, pass attempts, passing yards, TDs} fit on 2012-2025 player-games (player played at least 1 snap) a Poisson/negative-binomial GLMM y_ij ~ NB(mu_ij, phi) with log mu_ij = a_pos + u_i,season + log(exposure_ij), u ~ N(0, sigma_u^2); report sigma_u, phi and ICC = sigma_u^2/(sigma_u^2+mean within variance). Season-to-date posterior of u_i uses only games before the as-of week with shrinkage weight n_games/(n_games + phi/ sigma_u^2 scale); remaining-games total variance = m x Var(e) + m^2 x Var(u|data) where m is remaining games from nfl.games_played_dist.
raw_data: player-game stats: player_id, season, week, position, targets, receptions, rec_yards, carries, rush_yards, pass_att, pass_yards, TDs
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.why: Provides the correct dispersion for threshold and leader probabilities and is why season-stat rungs are wider than normal-approximation estimates.

nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.label: Clinched-seed rest: expected snap fraction of starters in the final two weeks
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.mechanism: Probability and magnitude of reduced snaps for starters in Week 17-18 when seeds or division titles are clinched.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.rationale: In the final weeks teams with nothing to play for rest key starters, which truncates cumulative totals just when leader races are decided; the effect depends on the coach's history and on the clinch state.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.measurement: For each team, compute the probability of each clinch state by Week 16 from the standings simulation; from 2015-2025, estimate expected snap fraction in Weeks 17-18 for starters by position as a function of state (clinched top seed, clinched any seed, eliminated), coach-specific rest history (shrink with k=2 occasions), and player age; output expected fraction of normal snaps and its distribution.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.why: Cuts the expected games and snaps of the leading contenders in the exact weeks when many leader contracts are decided, which season-to-date pace ignores.

nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.label: Pairwise covariance of remaining output among contenders
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.mechanism: Covariance of remaining-season output between contenders sharing a team, position room or quarterback.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.rationale: Leader probability involves the probability that one exceeds the other, so independence overstates the probability of both being high; teammates' rushing is negatively linked, and passing and receiving of a QB and his top receiver positively.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-seasons, estimate residual correlation between remaining-season output of pairs (same team same stat; QB-WR pairs; RB-RB) after removing season-level means, using the last 8 weeks as the test window; shrink pairwise correlation to the category average with k=30 pairs; use in a multivariate normal or copula simulation of the contender field.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.why: Needed so leader probabilities sum correctly across the field and so a teammate's injury changes the leader odds of another candidate.

nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.label: Distribution of the weekly leader's value by position and statistic
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.mechanism: Baseline distribution of the single-game maximum over all players of a position in a given week and the number of near-miss contenders.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.rationale: The weekly leader market is decided by the top of a very large field; the winner's threshold, not the favourite's mean, sets the chance, and the leader's value is heavy-tailed.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.measurement: For each position and statistic, from 2010-2025 weeks collect the weekly maximum and top-5 values; fit a generalized extreme value distribution by position; condition on number of games in the week (Thursday, Monday, bye-heavy weeks) and weather. Output P(player i is the weekly max) via simulation of the active-player field with player-specific distributions.
raw_data: player-week stats, number of games in the week
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.why: Weekly leader contracts are a different statistical object from season leaders and cannot be priced from the season-to-date pace input.

nfl.career_record_chase_survival.label: Career record chase: seasons remaining, age decline and retirement hazard
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.mechanism: A career rung set one unit above the all-time record is reached only if the player keeps playing enough seasons at a sufficient rate, so the forecast is a survival-weighted sum over future seasons.
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.rationale: Career contracts in this archetype (passing, receiving, rushing) need the gap to the record, the per-season output path by age and the probability the player retires, is released or is injured out first; a single-season model gives zero information about year three, and the retirement announcement ends the contract.
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.measurement: Gap = rung minus career regular-season total as of the last game. Per future season s: P(active in s) from a discrete-time retirement and release hazard by position and age fitted on 1990-2025 players with at least 5 seasons (logit on age, prior-season games and output percentile, k=20 player-seasons shrinkage); output in s = current rate x position aging curve (estimated from 2000-2025 same-position players, ratio by age) x expected games (nfl.games_played_dist). Simulate 20,000 career paths; P(cumulative >= gap before retirement and before the contract expiry). As-of the latest game.
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.why: Prices KXNFLCAREERPASSYDS, KXNFLCAREERRECYDS, KXNFLCAREERRSHYDS and KXNFLCAREERRSHTDS, whose strikes are all-time records plus one and whose horizon is the rest of a career.

nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.label: Individual defender sack and interception accrual (season totals and leaders)
nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.mechanism: A defender's season sacks or interceptions are his snaps times pass-rush or coverage opportunity times a low conversion rate that regresses strongly, accumulated over the remaining games.
nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.rationale: KXNFLSZNRECORD (rookie sack record 14.5, must be broken) and KXNFLLEADERPINT (interceptions leader) depend on individual defensive counts that none of the offence inputs describe; sacks are a noisy fraction of pressures and interceptions an even noisier fraction of targets, so pressure and target rates predict the rest of season better than banked counts.
nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.measurement: Per defender: pass-rush snaps per game (last 6 games, half-life 3) x pressure rate per rush snap (season to date shrunk to position prior with k=150 rush snaps) x sack-per-pressure (shrunk hard to the league rate of about 0.15 with k=60 pressures); interceptions = targets in coverage per game x INT per target (shrunk to about 0.03 with k=150 targets). Remaining-season totals simulated over games played (nfl.games_played_dist), banked counts added; for records require strictly greater than the record; for leaders take the max over all defenders. As-of the latest game.

nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.label: Team season-statistic accrual for non-points team totals (net passing, rushing yards) and late-season rest scaling
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.mechanism: Projects a team's final regular-season net passing or rushing yards as banked total plus a simulated sum over its remaining games, and applies Weeks 17-18 starter-rest scaling to every team-season total; season points for/against are taken from nfl.team_points_for_against_rates, not recomputed.
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.rationale: Team extremes and team specials settle on season totals, so a per-game rating is not enough: byes, the remaining opponents' defences or offences, late-season starter rest and the sack deduction in net passing yards change the remaining sum. The extreme over teams then needs every team's total jointly simulated with shared rating uncertainty.
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.measurement: Points for/against: use the season-total simulation of nfl.team_points_for_against_rates unchanged (its banked-plus-remaining draws and 1/N extreme rule), only multiplying Weeks 17-18 expected scores by the starter-rest factor from nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability. Net passing yards per remaining game g = expected team dropbacks (nfl.pace x nfl.proe) x [(1 - sack rate) x gross yards per attempt - sack rate x mean sack yards (about 6.5)], with sack rate = team sack rate allowed x opponent pressure factor, gross yards per attempt opponent-adjusted over the last 17 games (half-life 8 games, shrink to league mean with k=6 games); rushing yards analogously from rush attempts x opponent-adjusted yards per carry. Per-game sd from 2012-2025 residuals (about 70 net passing yards); team strength errors are the same per-simulation draw used by the points model (nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error), not an extra one. Sum over remaining games plus banked total; 20,000 simulations. As-of the latest completed game.

interactions.mechanism: The season total is the product of a discrete games-played count and a persistent per-game rate, so a high-rate player with a high attrition hazard has a bimodal distribution; moments of the total from independent components understate the left tail and overstate the median.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the total from games and rate jointly versus from independent normal approximations and compare calibration at the 10th and 90th percentiles.

interactions.mechanism: Targets and carries move together after an event: when a teammate is lost, one player's share rises and another's falls, and a coordinator change shifts the pass-run balance for everyone, so the rate is a mixture whose weights are updated by news.
interactions.how_to_test: Detect regime shifts around events and compare usage share before and after, by position.

interactions.mechanism: The expected snaps of starters fall at the point a team clinches a seed (usually Week 16-18) and the effect is concentrated in the last two weeks; before that point pace extrapolation is valid and after it drops.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Weeks 17-18 snap shares of starters on clinched versus unclinched teams.

interactions.mechanism: Leader probability for a player depends on the variance of his lead over each rival: positive covariance between two contenders on one offence (quarterback and a receiver sharing team passing volume) shrinks the variance of their gap so the better one is more reliably ahead, while negative covariance within a backfield (competing for the same carries) widens the gap variance and makes order flips more likely. The sign is positive for same-team passing pairs and negative for same-position teammates.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit leader probabilities from a covariance-matrix simulation versus an independent simulation, and compare Brier score and calibration on historical position leaders, separately for same-team positive-sign and same-position negative-sign pairs.

interactions.mechanism: Banked touchdown excess fades toward the role-based rate only to the extent it came from luck (long scores, fumble-recovery touchdowns); excess that rests on a stable red-zone share persists, and a role-regime change redefines the role-based rate itself, so the shrinkage of banked touchdowns toward expectation depends on how stable the underlying role is.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress remaining touchdowns on banked touchdowns, role-based expectation and an indicator of red-zone share stability or a regime-change event; test the banked x stability term and the null that banked excess has no effect.

interactions.mechanism: The weekly leader's probability depends on the tail of a player's single-game distribution rather than on its mean, so two players with equal means can differ several-fold in leader probability; this effect is a function of the tail index.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare weekly-leader frequency among players by tail-heaviness (95th percentile over mean) controlling for mean.

interactions.mechanism: For a career record chase a lost season matters only if it pushes the expected crossing past the likely retirement age; a player 400 yards short is barely affected by missing three games, while one needing two more full seasons at 35 loses most of his chance from a single long injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate attainment with and without a one-season absence across gap and age bins and compare with historical record chases (players within two seasons of a career record since 1990).

interactions.mechanism: A team leading the league in points scored that clinches early rests starters in Weeks 17-18, cutting its last two games' scoring by several points each, so the most-points market leader is penalised precisely when its season is strong; for fewest-points-allowed the same rest weakens the defence and raises points allowed, so clinching moves both team-extreme markets against the clinched team.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Weeks 17-18 points for and against of clinched versus unclinched top-seed teams in 2012-2025 relative to their season-to-date rates.

nonlinearities.shape: bounded and left-skewed: total increases linearly with games but the probability of a rung drops steeply when the required games approach the games remaining
nonlinearities.why: A threshold requiring almost every remaining game at an above-average rate becomes very sensitive to a single missed game, so the rung probability is nonlinear near the feasible limit.

nonlinearities.shape: sigmoid in the standardized gap (lead divided by remaining-sum standard deviation), saturating near 0 and 1
nonlinearities.why: A lead of one standard deviation yields only about 84 percent, while a two-sd lead yields 98 percent, so leader odds change quickly in the middle range and slowly in the tails.

nonlinearities.shape: shrinkage toward the role-based mean: realised touchdown excess decays with remaining games
nonlinearities.why: Banked touchdown luck does not carry into remaining games, so the extrapolated total regresses by a factor that depends on how many games remain.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy right tail: extreme-value shape parameter above zero for yards and fantasy points
nonlinearities.why: The weekly leader has a distribution with a long tail, so very high weekly leader values are more likely than normal-extreme extrapolation implies.

contract.settlement_definition: Ninety-eight live series, all with rules text, settling on the 2026-27 regular season or postseason. Win totals: KXNFLWINS ('wins at least 9 games'), per-team KXNFLWINS-* ('more than N wins') and KXNFLEXACTWINS* ('exactly N wins'), with the per-team texts stating 'Ties do not count as wins' (the sampled per-team markets are for 2025-26); KXNFLWINS-ANY asks whether any team wins 17; KXNFLWINSWEEK counts games scheduled in weeks 1-12 only; KXNFLH2HWINS is 50/50 on equal wins. Division aggregates: DIVISIONWINS (at least N total wins), DIVMOSTWINS and DIVLEASTWINS ($1/N rounded down among tied divisions). Standings: division winners (KXNFLAFCEAST etc.), exact order (KXNFLDIVISIONORDER) and worst-to-first under the league's official tiebreak methodology; seeds at the end of the regular season (KXNFL1SEED, KXNFLSEED, KXNFLSEEDOU '#N seed or better'). Postseason: PLAYOFF, PLAYOFFC (both teams), ROUNDQUAL (qualifies for the divisional round), STAGEOFELIM (round of elimination, with failure to qualify as its own outcome), PLAYOFFHOST (scheduled to host a playoff game, championship excluded), MATCHUP (conference-championship pairing), AFCCHAMP/NFCCHAMP and SBOUTCOME. Sequence contracts: KXNFLWINSTREAK (any team with at least N consecutive regular-season wins), KXNFLLASTTOLOSE (week of first loss; a tie is not a loss; same-week losses tie), KXNFLLASTTOWIN (week of first win), KXNFLDIVUNDEFEATED (a tie is not a loss). KXNFLENDSTREAK prices the season of a team's next playoff appearance and resolves No if the franchise ceases or relocates first. Whether the bye-holding #1 seed 'qualifies for the divisional round' is not stated (u6).

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington is the #1 seed in the National Football Conference at the conclusion of the 2026-2027 Pro Football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: The seed contract settles on the final regular-season seed after all tiebreakers, so it is a function of the full standings and the league's tiebreak procedure, not of the playoff results.

rules_evidence.quote: A tie (game result) does not count as a loss.
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties exist as a distinct game result and are treated as not-a-loss for the undefeated-in-division contract; a division record of 5-0-1 resolves YES, so tie probability affects this contract directly.

rules_evidence.quote: If either team is eliminated from contention for its specified role, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: The exact-pairing contract is a joint event over both conference champions and the final result, resolving No as soon as either team is eliminated, so its probability is a product of correlated bracket paths.

rules_evidence.quote: If the New York J Pro Football team ceases to exist, permanently relocates
rules_evidence.establishes: Multi-year streak-ending contracts carry franchise-existence clauses and a horizon of several seasons, a different process from one-season win totals.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution is based on games scheduled within weeks 1-12 only.
rules_evidence.establishes: The wins-by-week series counts only games scheduled in weeks 1-12, so it is a truncated win total read from the same simulation with a week cutoff, and byes inside the window change the number of games.

rules_evidence.quote: measured by the Pro Football week of its first win, rather than the exact date or time
rules_evidence.establishes: The last-to-win series ranks teams by the week of their first win with same-week wins tied and winless teams last, a first-passage hazard on the weekly grid.

rules_evidence.quote: Ties do not count as wins.
rules_evidence.establishes: Per-team win-total rungs count only wins, so a 9-7-1 team has 9 wins and a 'more than 9' rung needs 10 outright wins; tie probability lowers every rung slightly.

rules_evidence.quote: has exactly 17 wins in the 2025-26 regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact-win contracts settle on one point of the win pmf (sampled for the 2025-26 season), so the full simulated distribution, not a mean and sd, is required.

rules_evidence.quote: A tie (game result) does not count as a loss.
rules_evidence.establishes: The last-undefeated contract is a first-loss passage time on the weekly grid where ties keep a team undefeated and byes do not end a run.

rules_evidence.quote: Wins recorded in preseason or the playoffs do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The any-team win-streak contract counts regular-season runs only, so a streak cannot be extended by playoff wins and late-season rest games can end it.

rules_evidence.quote: the Pro Football championship game will not count as hosting a playoff game for the designated home team
rules_evidence.establishes: Hosting is read from scheduled home playoff games before the championship, so it depends on seeds 1-4 (division winners host the wild-card round) and on bracket advancement (a wild-card team can host a later round against a lower seed), not on the Super Bowl designation.

variants_and_edge_cases: Per-team KXNFLWINS-* ('more than N wins') and KXNFLEXACTWINS* ('exactly N wins') state 'Ties do not count as wins'; the main KXNFLWINS series ('at least N games') and KXNFLWINS-ANY do not repeat the tie line. The sampled per-team markets reference the 2025-26 season, so 2026-27 listings are assumed to keep the wording. Ties occur at roughly 0.25 percent per game (about 9 in 3,700 games since 2012, to be recomputed from nflverse schedules).

KXNFLSBOUTCOME (exact winner and runner-up) and KXNFLPLAYOFFC (both teams make playoffs) are joint events: for same-conference or same-division pairs the events are negatively correlated through zero-sum games, for different conferences close to independent.

Regular-season contracts (seed, win totals, division) are fixed at the end of Week 18 under the league's tiebreaker rules, while KXNFLROUNDQUAL and the pairing market depend on the playoff bracket and reseeding; KXNFLENDSTREAK spans several future seasons.

KXNFLROUNDQUAL: with seven playoff teams per conference the #1 seed skips the wild-card round, so whether it 'qualifies for the divisional round' changes P(contract) by about P(1 seed); the sampled rule has only the primary sentence (u6).

KXNFLENDSTREAK asks in which season a team next makes the playoffs (2030-31 in the sample), a multi-season first-passage problem with roster and coaching turnover, and resolves No if the franchise relocates or ceases first.

KXNFLDIVMOSTWINS pays 1/N among tied divisions, KXNFLH2HWINS 50/50 on equal wins, and KXNFLLASTTOWIN ties teams whose first wins fall in the same week, so the simulation must keep exact tie states rather than rounding.
KXNFLLASTTOLOSE measures the week of first loss: ties do not end the run, same-week losses are ties, and a team on a bye is still undefeated that week; KXNFLLASTTOWIN mirrors this for first wins.
KXNFLSTAGEOFELIM includes a 'Regular Season' outcome for failing to qualify, so its outcomes partition the season; KXNFLPLAYOFFHOST excludes the championship game and counts scheduled hosting.

KXNFLWINS-ANY (any team to 17 wins) and KXNFLWINSTREAK (any team to N straight) are maxima over all 32 teams, driven by the strongest teams' rating uncertainty and remaining schedules rather than one team's mean.
contract.settlement_data_source: The rules refer to the league's regular-season standings, the 'Governing League' official tie-breaking methodology (division order, worst-to-first) and announced playoff schedules; no explicit data vendor is stated.

mechanism.summary: Season outcomes are produced by a hierarchical process. Each team has a latent strength with real uncertainty at the start of the season (the prior is a blend of last-year performance, roster continuity and quarterback change, regressed hard toward the league mean) that is learned slowly from games, and that shared uncertainty acts on every game the team plays, making win totals more dispersed than independent games would give. Each game's win probability is a function of rating difference, home field, rest, and the availability of the quarterback and a handful of other key players, which are random across the season and correlated within a team. Win totals aggregate 17 such games, ties are possible, and standings follow from all teams' results through the league's tiebreakers, where division games are zero-sum and who plays whom decides leverage. Seeds give a bye only to the top seed, and playoff single elimination turns seed and full-strength roster into title odds. Cross-market consistency then follows from the same simulated worlds.

stages.name: Latent team strength with persistent uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's latent strength enters every game and is updated by results; early in the season most of the uncertainty is the shared prior error, which does not average out across 17 games. The prior combines previous efficiency (regressed), roster continuity, quarterback change and coaching change, and the posterior is revised by opponent-adjusted performance with luck-related components removed.
stages.distribution: Normal prior on the own rating with sd about 4.0 points of margin before Week 1 (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, assumption to recalibrate) shrinking to about 2.5 points after 17 games; the shared error induces correlation between a team's game results.

stages.name: Key-player availability, especially the quarterback
stages.description: The quarterback accounts for a larger share of team strength than any other player, and his missed games change the whole team's rating for those games; other key players (edge, tackle, cornerback) matter less. Injuries are a random process across the season with clustering, and the drop to the backup depends on who the backup is.
stages.distribution: Mixture across scenarios: QB1 plays all games (about 70% of teams), misses 1-4 games, or misses a large block; rating shift of several points between QB1 and backup, team-specific.

stages.name: Game-level win probability and schedule
stages.description: For each remaining game win probability is a logistic function of the rating difference plus home field and rest/travel, and the schedule composition determines both the expected wins and the leverage. Ties can occur, contributing half-win in standings and a not-lost result in some contracts.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with probability in roughly 0.1-0.9; ties ~0.2-0.3% per game; outcomes conditionally independent given ratings and availability.

stages.name: Win-total aggregation and exact-win distribution
stages.description: The number of wins is the sum of game outcomes, with variance larger than the binomial because of shared rating uncertainty and correlated availability. Exact-win and threshold contracts need the full probability mass function, and a 9.5 line is much more sensitive to the tails than to the mean. The simulation is conditioned on games already played (banked wins, ties and tiebreak state as of the current week) and on current injury and quarterback status, not re-run from Week 1. KXNFLWINSWEEK reads the same simulated games truncated at games scheduled in weeks 1-12, KXNFLH2HWINS the joint win totals of two teams (50/50 on equal wins), and KXNFLDIVMOSTWINS/DIVLEASTWINS/DIVISIONWINS the sums over a division's four teams.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed Poisson-binomial with sd approximately 2.0-2.4 wins; exact-win probabilities peak around 15-20 percent at the mean.

stages.name: Standings, tiebreakers and zero-sum leverage
stages.description: Division and seed contracts are determined jointly: division games produce a winner and a loser, so a team's chance depends on rivals' results, and ties at the same record are resolved by the league's tiebreak ladder (head-to-head, division record, common opponents, strength of victory and others). Games between direct competitors are more informative than other games. The same standings draws settle the exact division order (KXNFLDIVISIONORDER), worst-to-first (a 2025-26 fourth-place team finishing first) and the division-wins aggregates.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution across all 32 teams' win totals with negative correlation among division rivals; tiebreak resolution is a deterministic function of full results.

stages.name: Seed, bye and bracket path to title
stages.description: Only the top seed receives a bye, and seed determines home field and opponent strength; the title contract is the product of three or four game win probabilities in a reseeded bracket where roster health at playoff time matters and regular-season rest games distort the rating. Playoff win probabilities use a full-strength rating rather than season-average. Round-reached contracts (KXNFLSTAGEOFELIM, KXNFLROUNDQUAL) and the conference-championship pairing (KXNFLMATCHUP) are read from the same bracket draws.
stages.distribution: Product of 3-4 correlated game probabilities; convex in seed because of the bye; title odds heavy-tailed across the top teams.

stages.name: Sequence and extreme futures: undefeated, win streaks, any-team-17 and first-win races
stages.description: Several contracts depend on the order of results rather than the total: the last undefeated team (week of first loss, ties do not count as losses, same-week losses tie), the last team to win (week of first win), undefeated in division, any team reaching N consecutive regular-season wins, and any team reaching 17 wins. Each is a first-passage or maximum over 32 correlated team paths, so it must be read from the same simulated season paths, keeping weekly order, byes and tie results, rather than from win-total marginals. Late-season rest of clinched teams and tanking of eliminated teams change the hazard of ending runs.
stages.distribution: Passage times on the weekly grid (discrete, with ties at the same week) and maxima over 32 teams; heavy dependence on the one or two strongest teams' rating draws.

stages.name: Multi-season horizon: season of the next playoff appearance
stages.description: KXNFLENDSTREAK prices which future season ends a team's playoff drought, so it extends the current-season simulation with a year-to-year model of team strength: roughly one third reversion toward average each offseason, a random component from roster churn, a jump when a new starting quarterback arrives, and a playoff probability per season from the fourteen-team format. The current season's playoff probability is the first term; later seasons carry most of the uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Discrete first-passage distribution over seasons, geometric-like after the first year with a rate set by the reverted rating and QB-change jumps.

talent_strength.note: Own market-free rating (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free) with uncertainty and playoff-time full-strength rating; the catalog nfl.ratings input mixes market-implied history, is audited BENCHMARK_ONLY and is removed from stages and coverage.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent strength and the matchups among direct rivals.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and replacement quality dominate role effects at the team level.

availability_news.note: Injury vintages and scenario tree for the quarterback.

coaching_scheme.note: Head-coach and coordinator changes are part of the preseason prior but have no specified quantity; the effect of a new play-caller on team win expectation is not defined in the catalog.

environment.note: Venue and weather matter in single games but their season-level effect on win totals is small and symmetric across teams, except through home-field and dome versus outdoor schedules already in the rating and rest inputs.

game_context_script.note: Seed and bracket path define playoff game contexts; in-game script is not relevant at season level.

pace_volume.note: Season-level wins are not driven by a count of opportunities such as plays or possessions as a modelling stage; pace enters only through the rating's efficiency measures.

efficiency_conversion.note: Close-game and takeaway luck removal from ratings.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed win totals and joint division outcomes.

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not alter season outcomes beyond what is already captured in the team's results; the tiebreaker rules are the relevant rule set and are included under standings.

settlement_contract.note: All 98 series have rules text: per-team WINS-*/EXACTWINS* say ties do not count as wins, sequence contracts define bye, same-week and tie conventions, standings contracts cite the league tiebreak methodology; open: tie line absent from KXNFLWINS/WINS-ANY (u1), #1-seed bye under ROUNDQUAL (u6), no cancelled-game clause (u7).

nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.label: Shared team-rating uncertainty (posterior sd) carried across all games
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's latent rating, applied as a common draw across all of that team's games in a simulation.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.rationale: If every game is simulated at a fixed rating, win totals are too concentrated and tail probabilities for 4-win or 13-win teams are underestimated; the shared error is the main reason season win-total distributions are wider than binomial.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.measurement: Prior sd = 4.0 points of margin rating at the preseason (assumption: preseason win-total errors have sd about 2.9 wins against a binomial sd of about 2.1, implying a rating sd near 4 points; re-estimate from residuals of own preseason ratings against final ratings over 2002-2025); posterior sd after n games = 1/sqrt(1/prior_sd^2 + n/s^2) where the game-level residual standard deviation is 13.5 points, so s^2 = 13.5^2 = 182.25 points^2. Sample one team-level strength draw per simulation and keep it across all remaining games. Output: sd by team and week.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.why: Controls tail mass of wins and playoff probabilities in the season simulation, which the current catalog states as 'with uncertainty' without a defined quantity.

nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.label: Team-specific quarterback scenario tree and rating drop to the backup
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.mechanism: Expected loss in team rating, in points, when the starting quarterback is replaced by the depth-chart backup, and the probability distribution of missed games.
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.rationale: Quarterback change is the largest swing in team rating, and the size of the drop varies from one point for teams with a competent backup to ten points for teams with a replacement-level one.
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.measurement: Per team: rating drop (points per game) = (EPAdb_QB1 - EPAdb_QB2) x 38 expected dropbacks, where EPAdb = career-regressed EPA/dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency shrunk toward league mean with weight n/(n+300) dropbacks and the 38/game and slope (1 EPA per dropback = 1 point of margin per dropback, not a separate regression constant) are refit by regressing team game margin on QB EPA prior 2010-2025. Missed-games distribution: negative binomial of QB games missed per season by age bucket and prior-season games missed (2010-2025, ridge). Scenario tree: QB1 plays all remaining games, part, none; output expected wins lost (drop x 0.03 wins per point) and distribution. As-of latest depth chart and injury report.
raw_data: QB dropbacks and EPA by player
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.why: Directly converts quarterback availability into a team win distribution, which the current catalog treats as a flag.

nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.label: Direct-competitor leverage: remaining games among teams contending for the same slots
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.mechanism: Matrix of remaining games between teams whose division or wild-card outcomes are linked, with each game's swing in the target contract's probability.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.rationale: Games among rivals are zero-sum for the division and seed contract, so they move probabilities by roughly twice as much as other games, and the head-to-head tiebreaker also locks in earlier results.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.measurement: For each remaining game g and target contract C (division, seed, playoff, bye): run the standings simulation N=20,000 times with game g fixed to a home win and again fixed to a road win (other games random, common random numbers); leverage_g = P(C | home win) - P(C | road win) in probability points, signed for the team, and weighted leverage = |leverage_g| x 4 x p_g(1-p_g) for p_g own-model win probability. Aggregate by team as sum over its remaining games and by division/wild-card group. Include head-to-head results to date as first-tiebreak state. As-of after each week; no sportsbook probability used.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.why: Explains why division and seed contracts are not functions of expected wins alone and identifies when a single rival game decides the contract.

nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.label: Full-strength playoff rating versus season-average rating
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.mechanism: Team rating computed on games with the current starting lineup (healthy QB, lines, defence) excluding games with rested starters or garbage time.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.rationale: Regular-season averages include injuries that have healed and rested-starter games in Weeks 17-18, which bias the rating used for playoffs and title futures.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.measurement: Select team-games where the current Week-N starting QB and at least 80 percent of the current expected starters (by offensive/defensive snap share over the last 4 games, as of the latest inactive list) played >=50 percent of snaps, excluding Week 18 games where >=3 starters were healthy-inactive. Inside those games compute opponent-adjusted EPA/play margin using only plays where an own win-probability model (score differential, time, possession, timeouts; no spread) is between 5 and 95 percent. Shrink to the season-average rating with k=5 games; output rating in points of margin (EPA x 55 plays) and the difference from season average. As-of after each week.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.why: Title and round-qualification futures depend on playoff-time strength, not on the average over games with a different lineup.

nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.label: First-overall-pick race: bottom of standings, strength-of-schedule tiebreak and pick ownership
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.mechanism: Distribution of the team that ultimately makes the first pick, from the worst-record contest with its tiebreak and from ownership of traded picks.
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.rationale: The first-pick contract depends on who has the worst record, the tiebreak for ties (strength of schedule rather than team strength) and whether the pick has been traded, so it is an extreme-value problem of losing, not winning.
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.measurement: Simulate final records, take the minimum-wins team with the league's draft-order tiebreak (lower strength of schedule gets the higher pick, as an assumption flagged SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), then map the draft slot owner via a table of traded picks; add a small tanking adjustment (reduced win probability for teams eliminated by Week 12, estimated from history).
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.why: Retained for reference only: the first-overall-pick series (KXNFLDRAFT1ST) has been re-filed to the draft-selection archetype, so this input no longer feeds a stage here; the worst-record race still informs the last-to-win contract's bottom-of-standings dynamics.

nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.label: Own opponent-adjusted team rating with preseason prior (market-free)
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.mechanism: A Bayesian margin rating per team built only from game results, play-level EPA, roster continuity and quarterback status, with a home-field constant and a preseason prior, used as the latent strength for every futures simulation.
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.rationale: Every contract in this archetype depends on team strength, and nfl.ratings is built by inverting spreads and totals, which makes it a copy of the market. A rating from results, EPA and roster inputs can be compared with Kalshi prices as an independent estimate; the subtle part is the preseason prior, which dominates in September and October.
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.measurement: Weekly rating in points of margin per game: ridge regression (penalty lambda chosen by leave-one-season-out CV, start at 20 game-equivalents) of capped game margin (cap +/-24) on team and opponent indicators plus a home indicator (home constant refit yearly, about 1.5), over all games since the start of the prior season, weights exp(-ln2*games_ago/10); average 50/50 with an opponent-adjusted EPA/play margin rating converted to points (EPA margin x about 63 plays per team-game, refit yearly). Preseason prior = 0.67 x last-season final rating + 0.10 x (returning-production pct minus league mean pct)/10 points, where returning production = share of prior-season snaps (offence and defence) held by players on the roster at the week-1 cutoff, + QB-change term = (EPA/dropback prior of new starter minus old starter) x 38 dropbacks. Prior sd 4.0 points; posterior sd = 1/sqrt(1/4.0^2 + n/13.5^2). As-of next kickoff; spread, total and moneyline excluded.
free_sources: nflverse rosters and snap counts for returning production
raw_data: schedules: game_id, season, week, home_team, away_team, home_score, away_score
pbp: game_id, posteam, defteam, epa, play_type
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.why: Defines the latent strength that all win-total, exact-win, seed, division and title simulations consume, without sportsbook ratings or spreads.

nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.label: Multi-season playoff-appearance hazard (season of next playoff appearance)
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.mechanism: The season in which a team next makes the playoffs is a first-passage time of a mean-reverting team-strength process over several seasons, with jumps from quarterback and coaching changes.
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.rationale: KXNFLENDSTREAK pays on the specific future season of the next playoff appearance; this year's standings simulation answers only the current season, while later seasons depend on how fast NFL ratings revert (roughly one third per year), draft capital from bad seasons and the chance of a new starting quarterback, which a one-season model cannot give.
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.measurement: Year-end own rating (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free) evolves as r_{t+1} = 0.67 r_t + e, e ~ N(0, sd fitted on 2002-2025 year-to-year changes, about 4.5 points), with an added jump term when the starting QB changes (probability from contract year, age and draft capital; size from nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop). P(playoffs | rating) per season from the standings simulation calibrated on 14-team formats (2020+). Simulate 20,000 paths of 6 seasons; P(first appearance in season s); apply the franchise-continuity clause as a negligible hazard. As-of the latest game.
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.why: Provides the probability distribution over the season of a team's next playoff appearance for KXNFLENDSTREAK.

nfl.ratings.reason: Catalog measurement inverts historical spreads, totals and moneylines, so the rating is market-derived; it is a benchmark for the own rating only and appears in no stage, coverage claim or interaction (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free replaces it).

nfl.roster_continuity.reason: Regresses the preseason prior by returning production; matters early in the season and fades with games played.

nfl.schedule_strength.reason: Opponent strength sets expected wins, but remaining strength must come from current ratings; the previous-season record is stale.

nfl.pythag_luck.reason: Close-game luck regression corrects overstated records; modest effect after games played accumulate.

nfl.turnovers.reason: Takeaway luck inflates records; only a small adjustment to ratings and overlaps with efficiency.

nfl.qb.reason: Quarterback status and replacement quality are the largest team-level swing and need scenarios, not a flag. The catalog measurement values the starter-minus-backup gap from market line moves; that component is a benchmark only and is replaced here by an own valuation (starter versus backup EPA per dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency, or nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop for team ratings).

nfl.games_played_dist.reason: Key-player absence distribution widens win distributions; duplicated partly by the QB scenario input but relevant for other positions.

nfl.injuries_pit.reason: Current injuries and return dates adjust near-term ratings; timestamps matter most for in-season futures.

nfl.bracket_path.reason: Seed, bye and path are central for conference, title and round-qualification contracts.

nfl.motivation_seeding.reason: Late-season rest and incentives affect the last weeks and the ratings used for playoffs; small for most teams.

nfl.rest_travel.reason: Bye and short-week effects change game probabilities by a point or less; low value as a season-level input.

nfl.futures_coherence.reason: Coherence across linked prices is derived from market quotes; logical constraints are useful for checks but the coherence value does not inform the outcome.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures are a vig-heavy benchmark; using them as a primary input makes the model an echo, though they are a legitimate comparison target.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price drift shows how fast the market reacts but carries no independent information about team strength.

m.rules_text.reason: Determines tie counting, pick ownership, elimination wording and pairing semantics; needed because the same simulation maps to different payoffs.

m.volume_oi.reason: Open interest and volume describe liquidity and carry no information about win totals.

interactions.mechanism: A single team-level strength draw and a quarterback-absence scenario both apply to all of a team's remaining games, so they jointly widen the win-total distribution beyond the binomial; the shared draw dominates early in the season while the absence scenario adds a discrete left shift, and the two together create the fat tails at the 4-win and 13-win lines.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest win-total and exact-win calibration at the 10th and 90th percentiles of the simulated distribution for (a) independent games, (b) shared strength draw only, (c) shared draw plus QB scenario mixture.

interactions.mechanism: The cost of a quarterback's missed games depends on who the games are against: a miss in a division rival game costs more in a tied race and in a weak week of the schedule costs little, so the timing of absence interacts with schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the same absence in different weeks and measure the change in playoff probability.

interactions.mechanism: Division outcomes are zero-sum: a rival's win is a loss for another contender, so probabilities of division titles across four teams are negatively correlated and sum to one; late-season motivation changes the leverage once a team is clinched or eliminated.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare division-winner probabilities from a joint simulation with independent probabilities and measure the sum-to-one error.

interactions.mechanism: Title probability is convex in seed because only the top seed receives a bye and home field, and convex in full-strength rating because a team must win three or four games in a row; a small rating edge compounds across rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate title probability by seed and rating bucket using historical playoffs.

interactions.mechanism: Teams with a record better than their point differential carry an inflated results-based rating that regresses; the regression is strongest early in the season and for teams whose own rating has a large posterior sd, so pythag luck should shrink the own rating by an amount conditional on that sd.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress second-half win rate on first-half record and point differential, interacted with games played.

interactions.mechanism: Once a team is eliminated from the playoffs it may lose more often (tanking incentives, starters rested), and a clinched top seed rests starters in Weeks 17-18; both switch the per-game win hazard late in the season, which ends long win streaks of clinched teams and delays the first win of a winless eliminated team, so sequence contracts cannot assume a constant rating across the season.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare win rates relative to rating-implied probability for eliminated and clinched teams in Weeks 15-18 versus Weeks 1-14 over 2012-2025, and the frequency of streaks ending in Weeks 17-18.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped: playoff probability rises steeply from about 8 to 11 expected wins and flattens outside
nonlinearities.why: The qualification threshold lies in the middle of the win distribution, so a change of one expected win moves playoff probability by 15-20 points near 9 wins and by a few points at 5 or 13 wins.

nonlinearities.shape: step: the top seed receives a bye and the other six seeds do not
nonlinearities.why: A step function in seed distinguishes the number-one seed from the rest, so the title probability rises discontinuously and a team's expected wins only partly determines it.

nonlinearities.shape: mixture: a discrete loss of several rating points with probability equal to the chance of the miss
nonlinearities.why: The quarterback's absence shifts team rating by a lump, so the rating is a mixture rather than a normal, and the win distribution has a heavier left tail for teams with weak backups.

nonlinearities.shape: variance of the win total grows with the square of games played times the rating variance (rating sd about 4 points before the season, shrinking as results arrive)
nonlinearities.why: The shared error contributes quadratically to the variance of wins, so it dominates binomial variance by season end for a given rating uncertainty.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNFLTEAMTOTAL is the only live series: it settles YES when the named team scores over the strike (floor_strike, half-point rungs such as 'over 7.5') in the named game 'originally scheduled for' the listed date, so the settled quantity is one team's final points and a score equal to the next integer above the strike is YES. The rules text names no source of truth and is silent on whether overtime points count and on what happens if the game is postponed, suspended or cancelled; those are carried as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS (u1). The former joint 'both teams score N' series (KXNFLBOTH) was re-filed to game_total and no longer belongs to this archetype.

rules_evidence.quote: If Minnesota scores over 7.5 points in the Buffalo vs Minnesota Pro Football game originally scheduled for Nov 9, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The contract is a strict over on one team's final score with a half-point strike, so a team score of exactly 8 is YES and the settled quantity is the team's points, not combined or margin.

rules_evidence.quote: then the market resolves to Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement is a single binary YES on the over condition for one rung; the text contains no overtime, void or tie clause, so the half-point strike avoids pushes but overtime inclusion is not established.

variants_and_edge_cases: Only an over-strike ladder exists (floor_strike 7.5 in the sample); every rung is a nested event of the same team score, and low rungs near 7.5 are driven by the chance of a near-shutout rather than offence quality.

Points include non-offensive scores (interception and fumble returns, kick returns, safeties credited to the scoring team), so a team's offence is not the only source; the contract is about the scoreboard, not offensive points.

Overtime handling is not stated in the KXNFLTEAMTOTAL text; unconditionally overtime adds roughly 0.1-0.2 points to each team's expected total (about 6 percent of games reach overtime, about 2-3 extra points per team in those games), so the pmf is kept in two versions, with and without overtime, until the rule is confirmed.

'Originally scheduled for' anchors the contract to a specific game, but the text gives no postponement or cancellation rule (no 48-hour window or fair-price clause appears), so a rescheduled game's treatment is unknown.

Team scores cluster at 3 and 7 multiples, so rungs on the half-point such as 17.5, 20.5 and 23.5 correspond to different integer score masses and the same-sized gap in mean moves the probability by different amounts.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the sampled text; official game result by the league scoreboard is implied. Two-point conversions and extra points count as points in the final score by standard scoring.

mechanism.summary: A team's final score is the sum of points from a discrete sequence of possessions plus rare non-offensive scores. The number of possessions is set by both offences' tempo and style, the result of each possession is a discrete lottery over touchdown, field goal, no score and turnover with the points of 7 (or 6 or 8), 3, 0 and a chance of opponent return score, and the probabilities depend on starting field position, own offence against the opponent's defence, personnel and weather. Coach decision rules (go for it versus kick, one versus two points) change the points attached to a stalled drive. The score path then rewrites late possessions: leaders run clock, trailers throw and score faster. Because the discrete clusters at 3 and 7 are dense, the response of rung probability to the mean is lumpy and the correct object is the whole score distribution, not a mean plus normal noise.

stages.name: Possessions available to this offence
stages.description: The count of own possessions comes from combined pace, rushing share and clock use of both teams, penalties, turnovers (which add possessions) and the half-end structure; it is typically 10-13 drives per team, and the opponent's ball-control style removes possessions from this offence. A slow, run-heavy opponent cuts this team's chances in a way that own pace alone misses. Roles to avoid double counting: nfl.pace gives plays per minute, nfl.drives gives the possession count, nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial is the opponent term inside that possession estimate (not an extra independent driver) and nfl.drive_result_lattice conditions on the resulting count.
stages.distribution: Drives per team per game roughly 9-14 (sd ~1.5); correlated with the opponent's drive count and with game script.

stages.name: Drive start position and field-position inputs
stages.description: Where drives start (after kickoffs, punts, turnovers, returns) determines the expected points per drive, as does the quality of special teams. Turnovers by the opponent give short fields and high scoring chances, so the distribution of start positions reflects both defence and special-teams play.
stages.distribution: Starting yard line ~ distribution centred at the 27-30 yard line with a right tail of short fields after takeaways.

stages.name: Drive outcome lottery: touchdown, field goal, no score
stages.description: Each drive ends in a touchdown with probability that depends on the team's offence, the matchup with defence (pass rush, coverage, run front) and red-zone efficiency, in a field goal when drives stall inside kicker range, or in no points. The points per drive distribution is discrete and the team's total is a convolution across drives.
stages.distribution: Drive points take values 0, 3, ~7 with probabilities ~ 0.65, 0.12-0.15, 0.20-0.25 (league average assumption); sum over ~11 drives gives a discrete distribution with clusters.

stages.name: Kicker and fourth-down decision rules
stages.description: On stalled drives the coach decides to kick or go for it, and the kicker's accuracy by distance and weather decides the three points; changes in 4th-down aggressiveness convert a 3-point outcome into a 0 or 7 gamble. The extra point and two-point decisions add a variance term of about 0.5-1 point per touchdown.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes with decision-dependent probabilities; FG make probability falls from ~95% at 30 yd to ~65% at 55 yd.

stages.name: Personnel availability and offensive-line health
stages.description: The starting quarterback, line and skill players determine the offence's rate; a backup quarterback behind a weak line can reduce the team's expected score (the 4-7 point size is an unsourced assumption to be estimated from starter-versus-backup games, see u5). These status changes arrive late and are partially known at kickoff, and can happen in-game.
stages.distribution: Mixture over personnel scenarios with a heavy shift for the quarterback scenario; in-game injuries produce a smaller shift.

stages.name: Weather, score path and non-offensive scoring
stages.description: Wind and cold reduce passing and field goals, and a blowout compresses the leader's late scoring while the trailer's passing yields more. In addition, the team's defence and special teams can score directly (pick-six, return touchdowns, safeties), adding points independent of its offence, and the opponent's equivalent scores add to the opponent's total but also end the team's drives.
stages.distribution: Defensive/special-teams touchdowns occur in ~10-12% of team games (assumption); weather effects scale with wind above ~15 mph.

stages.name: Discrete score distribution and ladder mapping
stages.description: The team total's rungs are nested events of the same discrete variable; key numbers 3, 7, 10, 14, 17 and so on make the cumulative distribution step-like. The model has to produce the integer probability mass function and read every rung from it, with overtime included or excluded once the rule is known. The pmf is built around the model's own mean points per team (no sportsbook line); the opponent's score enters only through the script coupling (a team that falls behind passes more and scores faster), captured by the paired-score covariance.
stages.distribution: Discrete multi-modal distribution; the rung probability from a smooth normal approximation is biased by 2-4 points near key numbers.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted offence and defence; nfl.off_epa is the main prior, regression window unspecified.

opponent_matchup.note: Pass and run components of both offence and defence via nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides; coverage_scheme, run_defense and pass_rush are decompositions removed from the stage as overlapping.

role_personnel.note: Starter status at quarterback, skill and kicker.

availability_news.note: Quarterback and line status as of kickoff; in-game exits not attached to this archetype.

coaching_scheme.note: Fourth-down and two-point decision rules; play-caller identity and tempo choices enter through pace.

environment.note: Wind and temperature for kicking and passing; roof and home-field venue constant are attached via nfl.venue and the paired-score input.

pace_volume.note: Plays and possessions, with the opponent's ball-control denial as the opponent term of the possession estimate.

efficiency_conversion.note: Points per drive, red-zone conversion and field position.

distribution_variance.note: Discrete score pmf with key numbers around the own mean, plus the paired-score correlation used for script coupling; the market-derived team_total_split and the line-centred score_resid are removed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Short rest, travel and late-season clinch rest of starters influence a team's scoring, but no schedule or motivation input is attached to this archetype.

officiating_rules.note: Penalties extend or end drives and shape scoring slightly, but a crew effect on one team's points is second-order and can be captured inside the offensive and defensive efficiency inputs.

settlement_contract.note: The team-total rules text does not say whether overtime counts, gives no postponement rule and names no settlement source; the archetype attaches no rules-text input, so this remains a gap (u1).

nfl.drive_result_lattice.label: Drive-result lattice: touchdown, field goal, turnover, punt probabilities by start position
nfl.drive_result_lattice.mechanism: Per-drive probabilities of touchdown, field goal and no score for this offence against this defence conditioned on starting field position and game state.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.rationale: Team points are the convolution of drive outcomes, not a smooth function of EPA per play: two offences with equal EPA can have different touchdown-to-field-goal mixes, and the mixture decides the cluster of the score.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.measurement: From drive-level play-by-play 2016-2025 estimate multinomial logit of drive result on start yard line, offence rating, defence rating, down-and-distance style, with team-level random effects (shrink team deviations with k=10 drives); output P(TD), P(FG), P(none) for each of 11 drives by start-position distribution and compute the discrete points distribution by convolution including 2-point and XP outcomes.
raw_data: drive: start_yard_line, result, points, posteam, defteam, plays, time
nfl.drive_result_lattice.why: Creates the discrete team-score distribution that the team total ladder needs and replaces a mean times variance approximation.

nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.label: Fourth-down go-for-it versus field-goal decision rate and two-point policy
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.mechanism: Coach-specific probability of going for it on fourth down by field position and distance, and of attempting a two-point conversion.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.rationale: The decision converts a stalled drive into 3 points, 0 points or 7 points; aggressive coaches raise the variance and shift the mean of team totals, and two-point attempts change points per touchdown.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.measurement: For each head coach over 3 seasons: P(go | yard line bin, distance bin, score and time bin), shrink to model-based optimum with k=15 decisions; two-point attempts per touchdown shrunk with k=10; expected points per stalled drive = P(go) x [conv x 7 + (1-conv) x 0] + (1-P(go)) x P(make FG | distance) x 3; output delta in expected points per game and variance. As-of last completed game.
raw_data: pbp: down, ydstogo, yardline_100, play_type, field_goal_result, two_point_attempt
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.why: Alters the mean and variance of the points associated with the same drive state, and is a coaching feature absent from this archetype's inputs.

nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.label: Non-offensive scoring rate: defensive and special-teams points for and against
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Expected points per game from interception returns, fumble returns, kick and punt return touchdowns and safeties credited to the team, and the equivalent against it.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These points enter the team's total independent of offence, and when scored against the team they end drives; ignoring them biases rungs low for teams with opportunistic defences.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team, count of defensive and special-teams scoring plays per game over the last 25 games with half-life 12, shrunk heavily toward league (k=40 games) because these events are rare; split into takeaway-driven part (own takeaway rate x return-score probability) and special-teams part; opponent's rate against the team computed symmetrically. Output expected points and probability of at least one such score.
free_sources: nflverse play-by-play (touchdown with td_team differing from posteam, safety flag)
raw_data: pbp: td_team, posteam, interception, fumble_lost, return_touchdown, safety
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.why: Directly adds a team-total source that the offence-only inputs omit and shifts the lower rungs through the chance of scoring without the offence.

nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.label: Opponent ball-control denial: expected drives and time removed from this offence
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.mechanism: How much the opponent's time of possession, run share and clock usage cut this offence's number of drives relative to its neutral pace.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.rationale: A team's own tempo says nothing about drives if the opponent holds the ball; the effect depends on the matchup of styles and is not captured by pace alone.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.measurement: For each opponent compute average seconds per play, run rate in neutral situations and drive length over the last 12 games (half-life 6); expected own drives = league drives x (own-share model) where own share = own pace / (own pace + opponent pace) adjusted by a regression on historical game drive counts; output expected drives for each side and variance. As-of last game.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.why: Gives the possession count its two-sided structure, which the existing own-pace input lacks.

nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.label: Own-mean team score probability mass function with key-number structure (market-free)
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.mechanism: Converts the model's own expected points for a team into a discrete integer score distribution that carries the extra mass at 3, 6, 7, 10 and 14, so every rung of the ladder is read from one pmf.
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.rationale: The catalog score residual is defined around the closing spread and total, and the team-total split is derived from the same lines, so both are market echoes. The key-number lumpiness is real, but it must be fitted around own predicted means; otherwise the model inherits the market's mean and the comparison with Kalshi prices is circular.
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.measurement: From all regular-season team-games 2010-2025, bin by the pregame expected team points from nfl.model_team_points_mean computed walk-forward (for seasons before the drive model's window use the ridge EPA-points rating of nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, no betting data), in 1-point bins from 10 to 35 (pooled outside). Within each bin fit a negative-binomial body (dispersion per bin) times a smoothed correction ratio observed/NB at scores 0,3,6,7,9,10,13,14,16,17,20,21,23,24,27,28 shrunk to 1 with weight n/(n+60). Keep two pmfs: including overtime points and regulation-only. Output P(score >= n) for n=0..60 as of the final pre-kickoff mean.
raw_data: schedules: game_id, team scores, overtime flag
own pregame expected team points per team-game
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.why: Provides the integer pmf from which every KXNFLTEAMTOTAL rung is read, without importing market lines. The catalog measurement keeps an OT-inclusive and a regulation-only pmf and no longer refers to KXNFLBOTH; for KXNFLTEAMTOTAL the overtime choice stays open (u1).

nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.label: Paired team-score covariance from pace, script and weather (market-free)
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.mechanism: Estimates the dependence between the two teams' scores through shared pace, shared weather and the score path and outputs their joint integer pmf, from which the single-team conditional pmf (team totals), the both-teams-at-least-N tail (game_total's KXNFLBOTH) and the game-total tail (slate extremes) are read.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.rationale: Team scores are positively correlated through plays and drives and conditionally negative through script (a leading team slows play and shortens the other side's comeback window). The sign and size vary by expected total and weather, so any contract on one team conditioned on the game, on both teams' tails or on the sum needs the joint pmf rather than a product of marginals; the dependence is strongest in the high-total tail.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.measurement: Using 2010-2025 regular-season games, compute residuals of (home score - own model home mean) and (away score - own model away mean), where means are walk-forward outputs of nfl.model_team_points_mean including the home shift and dome flag. Bins: expected total (<40, 40-50, >50 model points) x wind (<10, 10-15, >=15 mph; roofed games count as calm), 9 cells. Per cell fit a Student-t copula on the probability-integral transforms of the two scores (correlation rho_b and degrees of freedom nu_b in 2..30 by maximum likelihood), shrinking rho_b toward the pooled value with weight n_b/(n_b+150) and log(nu_b) toward pooled with the same weight; upper-tail dependence lambda_U follows from (rho_b, nu_b). Simulate pairs from the copula and map each margin through that team's nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean marginal (OT-inclusive or regulation-only per contract). Tail check: compare simulated and empirical P(both >= N) for N = 28, 35, 42 per bin on held-out seasons. Output the joint pmf P(home=h, away=a) for h, a in 0..70, rho_b, nu_b and lambda_U per cell; consumers read P(team>=n | game draw), P(both>=N) and P(home+away>=T). As-of kickoff weather forecast and model means; no betting total used.
free_sources: nflverse schedules (final scores, roof, wind, temp)
raw_data: schedules: game_id, scores, roof, wind, temp, home_team
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.why: Couples this team's score to the opponent's through shared pace, weather and the score path; the catalog definition (patched in input_patches/NFL_a.json) now outputs the joint home/away pmf and the conditional single-team pmf used here, while game_total reads the both-teams-N tail of KXNFLBOTH from the same joint.

nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.label: Pass and run EPA split for both offence and defence, opponent-adjusted
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.mechanism: Separates each side's points production and prevention into pass and rush components so the matchup between an offence's style and the defence's pass and run strengths can be computed.
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.rationale: Collapsing the opposing defence to one defensive EPA hides whether it is strong against the pass or the run; a pass-heavy offence is hurt by a pass-defence strength and a run-heavy one by a run-defence strength. The split needs both offences and both defences with enough shrinkage.
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.measurement: Per team, from 2016+ regular-season plays excluding kneels, spikes and plays with pre-play wp below 0.05 or above 0.95 (no-spread nflfastR wp): off EPA per dropback, off EPA per rush, def EPA per dropback faced, def EPA per rush faced, each opponent-adjusted by ridge over the last 12 games with exp half-life 6 games, shrunk to league mean with weight n/(n+150) for pass and n/(n+100) for rush (n = plays). Expected EPA/play for team A vs B = pA x (offA_pass - defB_pass) + (1-pA) x (offA_rush - defB_rush) where pA = A's neutral-situation pass rate = league expected pass rate (nfl.proe model) + A's PROE, as of last completed game. Output four components plus the blended rate.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, defteam, play_type, epa, wp, qb_kneel, qb_spike, qb_dropback
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.why: Gives the opponent-style matchup the team-total chain needs, while the single defensive EPA input hides the pass and run split.

nfl.team_total_split.reason: Splits the game spread and total into team means, so it is market-derived by construction; it is a benchmark for the rung, not an independent input, and should be compared against own team means.

nfl.off_epa.reason: The team's opponent-adjusted offence is the main driver; per-play EPA must be turned into drive outcomes rather than treated as points.

nfl.def_epa.reason: Opponent defensive efficiency; heavily overlaps coverage_scheme, run_defense and pass_rush, which decompose it.

nfl.pace.reason: Own pace sets plays but not drives; kept only as the plays-per-minute term inside the possession estimate and not as a second possession driver alongside nfl.drives.

nfl.drives.reason: Drives are the opportunities for scoring, but need the opponent's ball control, added as a separate input.

nfl.redzone.reason: Red-zone touchdown rate is noisy and regresses; stronger when combined with drive-start data.

nfl.kicker.reason: Accuracy by distance and range converts stalled drives into 3 points, affecting key-number masses; modest in total expected points.

nfl.qb.reason: Starter status is the dominant availability driver of an offence's score; resolves late. The catalog measurement values the starter-minus-backup gap from market line moves; that component is a benchmark only and is replaced here by an own valuation (starter versus backup EPA per dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency, or nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop for team ratings).

nfl.ol.reason: Line health shifts sack and run-block rates; partial pregame and overlapped by quarterback scenario.

nfl.skill_avail.reason: Missing receivers and backs reduce the ceiling; effect size depends on replacement quality.

nfl.field_pos.reason: Starting field position and special teams change points per drive; correlated with turnovers.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Wind and cold reduce passing and long field goals; style-dependent, thresholded.

nfl.script.reason: Lead and trail effects on late scoring; for team totals the leader's late scoring compresses and the trailer's rises. The catalog measurement centres the margin distribution on the sportsbook spread and total; only the score-state response surface is kept, and the margin distribution must come from own ratings (nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior or the own team-score model), never from market lines.

nfl.score_resid.reason: Catalog measurement defines residuals around closing spread and total, so it is market-derived; the key-number structure is retained by the market-free nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean and this input is used only to compare against lines.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook team totals are the comparison price for the rung, not a physical input; the draft marked it primary.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Rungs of a single team's points are nested and must be monotone and consistent with game total and spread; a constraint, not information.

m.volume_oi.reason: Trading volume and open interest say nothing about how many points a team scores.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trade history is market output; using it as an input makes the model circular.

nfl.coverage_scheme.reason: Coverage shell is a component of the opposing pass defence already summarised in defensive EPA; keep only as a decomposition when available.

nfl.run_defense.reason: Run-defence component is needed separately from the pass component (see interaction 0), so it is carried by nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides rather than as an independent input; its box-count detail overlaps the run EPA.

nfl.pass_rush.reason: Pass-rush pressure is part of the pass-defence EPA component of nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides; not staged separately to avoid double counting.

nfl.venue.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s6) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: A pass-heavy offence is hurt more by a strong pass defence and a run-heavy one by a strong run defence, and the script chooses which side the offence leans on, so the opponent effect on points depends on the offence's style mixture and the expected score state.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team points on offence pass-share x opposing pass-defence EPA and offence run-share x opposing run-defence EPA, separately by expected score state; the separate coefficients differ in sign pattern from a single defensive EPA.

interactions.mechanism: In wind or cold the effective kicking range shrinks by 5-10 yards, and a coach who would kick from 48 yards goes for it, which changes the expected points of stalled drives from 2.4 to a 0 or 7 gamble; the decision flips at a threshold distance that depends on weather.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate go-for-it probability and make rate by yard-line bin split by wind; test threshold shifts.

interactions.mechanism: Total points are a convolution over a random number of drives, and the number of drives is correlated with drive outcomes (long touchdown drives remove possessions, quick scores add them), so independent treatment of drive count and outcomes understates the dispersion.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated team total variance with realised variance, using independent and joint draws of drives and outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: A backup quarterback behind a weak line and a thin receiver room compounds: pressure rises, completion probability falls and yards after catch fall, so the points loss is greater than the sum of single-position losses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare scoring in games with combined absences versus single absences, controlling for opponent.

interactions.mechanism: The probability mass at key totals (3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 14) depends on the touchdown versus field-goal split, so rung probabilities move discontinuously as the red-zone touchdown rate or the kicker accuracy changes the mixture even if the mean points are constant.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the score pmf with a mixture model and test the change in P(total >= 17) with fixed mean but varying TD/FG mixture.

interactions.mechanism: Non-offensive scores arrive more often when the opponent is trailing and passing (more interceptions) so the team's total gets a lift in precisely the game states where its offence is conservative; the contribution is conditional on opponent script.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate return-score frequency by opponent score state and pass rate.

nonlinearities.shape: lumpy: rung probability changes in steps around the key numbers 3, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 24
nonlinearities.why: The own-mean score pmf has mass concentrated on sums of 3 and 7, so a shift in the model's own expected points moves P(over 13.5) and P(over 16.5) by different amounts rather than smoothly; this shape is fitted around own means, not closing lines.

nonlinearities.shape: steep decay of make probability beyond about 50 yards, and decision threshold at about 50-55 yards for go-for-it
nonlinearities.why: Field-goal accuracy decays nonlinearly with distance, and coaches switch policies at a similar distance, so points per drive near the 35-yard line is a nonlinear function of range.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold effects near 15 mph wind and near freezing temperature on kicking and deep passing
nonlinearities.why: Wind affects long field goals and deep passes sharply above a threshold, so team points fall in a step-like pattern in wind speed.

nonlinearities.shape: concave for the leader: points per late drive fall as the lead grows because of clock-killing runs, convex for the trailer
nonlinearities.why: A large lead reduces the leader's late scoring chance even as expected margin increases, so team total for a favourite is not monotone in the own-rating expected margin.
