contract.settlement_definition: Eleven of the twelve live series settle on Sleeper's full-PPR fantasy points (KXNFLFFPTS: 'Sleeper's default full-PPR scoring', 'no additional rounding', corrections after expiration not considered; the KXNFLFFPTSLADDER text says 'standard Points Per Reception (PPR)', a wording variant to confirm). Per-game tickers (KXNFLFFPTS) refer to the 'Full game (including overtime)' and a player who does not play or has no Sleeper value scores 0; the weekly leader and top-5 texts include overtime and rank all players in the group with membership fixed by Sleeper at expiration, non-players scoring 0; KXNFLFFH2HSEASON treats a non-player as 0 and pays 50 percent on a tie; any-game highs (KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH, KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE) use any single regular-season game; top-N ranks pay 1/N at the cutoff tie; KXNFLFFPLAYOFFLEADER sums Weeks 15-17 and excludes defence/special teams, kickers and IDP. The exception is KXNFLFANTASYMOST (most fantasy points in one game, sampled for the Feb 8, 2026 Seattle vs New England game), which uses 'ESPN's FFL Points Per Reception (PPR) scoring', counts only points scored during that game and pays 1/N among tied players; its primary sentence says 'during the full game' but no sentence defines overtime or treats non-participants. Which of these sentences apply to which series is as sampled, not generalised across all twelve. The final series assignment keeps all twelve series here, including the season total, season H2H, position leader, top-N, weekly leader and Weeks 15-17 leader, so season accrual (stage s9) is part of this record.

rules_evidence.quote: Players who do not play or are not assigned a fantasy-point value by Sleeper are treated as scoring 0 fantasy points.
rules_evidence.establishes: A non-participant is a zero, not a void, so availability risk is a real loss on this contract and on the over rungs, and the per-game distribution has an atom at 0.

rules_evidence.quote: The fantasy-point total published by Sleeper at expiration is used, with no additional rounding, and corrections after expiration are not considered.
rules_evidence.establishes: The source of truth is Sleeper's number at expiration, so stat-correction timing and Sleeper's own scoring conventions (not the league's stat sheet) determine settlement; strikes with decimals (9.2) exist.

rules_evidence.quote: rounded to the nearest $0.01 with $0.005 rounded up
rules_evidence.establishes: The ladder is a scalar at $0.01 per point, rounded half up, capped at $1.00 (100 points), so its fair value is the truncated mean and not a tail probability.

rules_evidence.quote: If either player does not play in the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season they will be treated as having scored 0 points.
rules_evidence.establishes: Season H2H treats a missing season as a zero total and ties pay 50 percent, so the contract is a comparison of two season-sum random variables including attrition.

rules_evidence.quote: Dead-heat rules apply in the event that two or more players are tied at the final qualifying position.
rules_evidence.establishes: Top-N rank markets pay 1/N at the cutoff tie, and fantasy scores with 0.1-point increments make ties at the cutoff rare but real for weekly ranks.

rules_evidence.quote: It ranks all WRs, including eligible players without a listed market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Weekly leader contracts are decided over the entire wide-receiver pool, not the listed candidates, so the field's residual mass is part of every listed player's probability.

rules_evidence.quote: This market will be based on ESPN's FFL Points Per Reception (PPR) scoring
rules_evidence.establishes: The game-most fantasy contract settles on ESPN's PPR scoring, not Sleeper's, so scoring-setting differences (e.g. kicker distance tiers, bonuses, fumble values) and ESPN's own stat timing are the settlement source for this series.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players are tied for the most fantasy points the market will resolve to 1/N where N is the number of players tied.
rules_evidence.establishes: Game-most fantasy is a maximum over every player in one game with dead-heat 1/N splitting, a single-game order statistic over both rosters.

variants_and_edge_cases: Per-game over thresholds with non-integer strikes (9.2 for a kicker, 34 and 49 'at least' for any-game highs) mix player types: the full KXNFLFFPTS text (read from the live market, the stored sample is truncated) lists the Sleeper kicker table (FG 0-39 +3, 40-49 +4, 50-59 +5, 60+ +6, XP +1, misses -1) and a D/ST table with points-allowed tiers from +10 to -4.

Season-high contracts (KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH, KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE for rookies) are the maximum of up to 17 single-game scores, and rookie pools combine many players, so they depend on the upper tail of each game's distribution and on availability.

Weekly and positional leader markets (KXNFLFFWEEKLEAD, KXNFLFFWEEKTOP, KXNFLFFLEADER, KXNFLFFLEADERTOP, KXNFLFFPLAYOFFLEADER) rank all players in the group using Sleeper's group membership at expiration; the Weeks 15-17 market sums three games and excludes defence, kickers and IDP.
Season ladders and totals use regular-season games only; the per-game ladder is capped at $1.00 for 100 points, which is rarely binding, and rounding half-up is explicit.

Sleeper's fantasy values are published for the 'full game (including overtime)' and corrections after expiry are ignored, so a late stat correction does not change the settlement even if the league changes the official stat.

The Weeks 15-17 leader market excludes kickers, defence/special teams and IDP, whereas the per-game KXNFLFFPTS ticker includes kickers (sample: Will Reichard above 9.2); overtime and post-expiration-correction sentences appear only in some series' sampled text, not all eleven.

KXNFLFANTASYMOST is the only series on ESPN PPR scoring and the only single-game order statistic: the winner is the top scorer among all players of both teams in one game (typically a quarterback, given 4-point passing touchdowns plus rushing), and its text says 'full game' without an explicit overtime or non-participant clause.
contract.settlement_data_source: Sleeper's published fantasy points (default full-PPR) at expiration, with Sleeper determining player group membership, for eleven series; ESPN's FFL PPR scoring for KXNFLFANTASYMOST. Official game stats feed both platforms; Sleeper corrections after expiration are ignored, while ESPN correction timing is not stated.

mechanism.summary: A full-PPR fantasy score is a linear combination of a player's counting stats, and all of the weight is on four components: receptions (one point each), yardage (a tenth of a point per rushing or receiving yard, 0.04 per passing yard), touchdowns (six, with four for a passing touchdown) and negatives (interceptions, lost fumbles). The player must first be on the field; availability and snap share set an atom at zero and a ramp. Opportunity (targets, carries, dropbacks) comes from team volume and role; yield comes from efficiency and matchup; touchdowns come from goal-line and red-zone opportunity with a very large luck component and discrete six-point jumps. Components covary within a player (receptions with yards) and across teammates (a quarterback's touchdown pass is a receiver's touchdown), so total variance is far higher than the sum of marginals suggests. Ranking and leader contracts are order statistics over a whole pool with correlated members, and 'any game' contracts are maxima over a season; the settlement defers to Sleeper's own numbers and group definitions. One series (game-most fantasy points) is scored on ESPN's PPR settings and asks for the top scorer among all players of a single game.

stages.name: Participation: active status, snaps and the zero atom
stages.description: The player must be active and on the field; inactive or non-playing players are scored zero by contract. Snap share and role caps (a returning player, a rotational receiver) determine whether he gets opportunities. This stage produces an atom at zero (5-15 percent of player-weeks for those with injury designations) and a ramp.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated: atom at 0 for inactive, ramp for limited players, near-constant for healthy starters.

stages.name: Opportunity volume: targets, carries, dropbacks
stages.description: Team plays and pass rate generate the pool of dropbacks and rushes, and the player's role determines his share; script moves volume toward passing or running by state. Opportunities are strongly overdispersed and are the most predictable part of fantasy points. Quarterbacks enter the pools of KXNFLFFH2HSEASON, position leaders and weekly leaders: their points come from dropbacks (nfl.proe, nfl.pace, nfl.script), starter status (nfl.qb) and rushing yards and touchdowns (nfl.qb_rushing), scored at 0.04 per passing yard, 4 per passing touchdown and the full rushing value. The catalog measurement values the starter-minus-backup gap from market line moves; that component is a benchmark only and is replaced here by an own valuation (starter versus backup EPA per dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency, or nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop for team ratings).
stages.distribution: Counts with negative-binomial dispersion; team volume ~ plays 60-70, pass rate 55-60 percent.

stages.name: Yardage and reception yield
stages.description: Receptions earn one point irrespective of yards, so PPR rewards high-volume short-area roles, while yards add a tenth of a point per yard. The yield per opportunity depends on depth, efficiency and matchup, and the PPR reception point makes catch counts, not yards, the stable core of the score for slot receivers and backs. For quarterbacks the yield term is nfl.qb_efficiency (passing yards and touchdown rate per dropback); for skill players it is per-target and per-carry yield, each adjusted for the opponent's pass and run defence.
stages.distribution: Receptions binomial in targets; yards compound; receptions and yards are positively correlated within a player-game.

stages.name: Touchdown scoring: goal-line opportunity and luck
stages.description: Touchdowns are six points each, so one touchdown can equal 60 yards, and they come from goal-line and red-zone usage with a Poisson-like process whose variance dominates fantasy score variance. The expected rate is determined by play-level opportunity location; realised touchdowns are partly luck and regress.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like with mean 0.3-0.8 per game for starters; each touchdown a six-point jump (passing: four points for the quarterback, six for the receiver).

stages.name: Negative events and kicker special case
stages.description: Interceptions, lost fumbles and kicker misses subtract points; quarterbacks carry most of the downside, and kickers' scores are driven by the number of field-goal and extra-point opportunities, which depend on team drives and red-zone stalls. Kicker and D/ST weights are listed in the full KXNFLFFPTS rules text (read from the live Kalshi market on 2026-11-08; the stored sample is truncated before them) and are composed in stage s11. Kicker points follow field-goal and extra-point opportunities set by drive count (nfl.drives), red-zone stall rate (nfl.redzone) and the kicker's distance-specific accuracy (nfl.kicker); interceptions and lost fumbles use nfl.int_rate and nfl.fumble_luck. The ladder and per-game ticker KXNFLFFPTS includes kickers, whereas the Weeks 15-17 leader market excludes kickers, defence/special teams and IDP.
stages.distribution: Low-count events with small penalties; kicker points are discrete sums of 3-5 point field goals and 1 point extra points.

stages.name: Aggregation: component covariance and team stacks
stages.description: The score is the sum of components that move together: a touchdown pass is four points for the quarterback and six for the receiver, shootouts raise every player in the game, and teammates compete for the same carries and targets. This covariance determines the variance of the total, the joint distribution for H2H comparisons and top-N ranks.
stages.distribution: Variance of the score is the sum over components and covariances; positive within a pass-catching stack, negative among backs in the same room.

stages.name: Order statistics: season highs, weekly leaders and position ranks
stages.description: A season-high market is the maximum of the player's remaining single-game scores; a weekly leader is the maximum over the whole position pool; a season leader is a cumulative maximum. Each needs the right tail of the per-game distribution and the field beyond the listed players.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail; maximum of N draws grows with log N; weekly leader of 100+ WRs has expected maximum around 30 points (assumption).

stages.name: Settlement: Sleeper scoring, group definitions and timing
stages.description: Contracts settle on Sleeper's published points at expiration; group membership (WR versus RB, rookie status) is determined by Sleeper, and corrections after expiration are ignored. Differences between Sleeper's settings and other fantasy platforms change the score. KXNFLFANTASYMOST is the exception: it settles on ESPN's PPR scoring, whose default settings differ from Sleeper's in kicker and bonus details, so the same stat line can score differently.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from official stats to Sleeper points; settlement risk comes from classification and correction timing.

stages.name: Season accrual for season-total, season H2H and season-leader fantasy contracts
stages.description: KXNFLFFSEASONTOTAL, KXNFLFFH2HSEASON, KXNFLFFLEADER and KXNFLFFLEADERTOP settle on regular-season full-PPR sums, so banked Sleeper points to date are fixed and only the remaining games are random: their number per player (byes, injury absences, late rest of clinched starters), the role regime that can change after a teammate's injury or a trade, and the per-game point distribution from stages s1-s6. The Weeks 15-17 leader is a three-game sum inside that horizon.
stages.distribution: Banked total plus a sum over a random number of remaining games with persistent role state; heavy left tail from lost games and a long right tail for touchdown-heavy players.

stages.name: Game-most fantasy points across both rosters (ESPN scoring)
stages.description: KXNFLFANTASYMOST pays the player with the most ESPN-PPR fantasy points in one game. The candidate set is every player on both teams, so the probability is a single-game maximum over roughly 10-14 relevant scorers with strong positive dependence inside each offence (a passing touchdown scores for the quarterback and the receiver) and negative dependence between teams through script. Quarterbacks win most often because passing yards, four-point passing touchdowns and rushing add up, but a receiver or back with two touchdowns can overtake; a mobile quarterback's rushing floor raises his share. Scores must be computed under ESPN's default PPR settings rather than Sleeper's.
stages.distribution: Single-game order statistic over correlated player scores; win probabilities concentrated on the two quarterbacks (often 50-70 percent combined) with a long tail of skill players, plus a small 1/N tie atom.

stages.name: Kicker and team D/ST fantasy scores (Sleeper default tables)
stages.description: KXNFLFFPTS lists kicker markets (Will Reichard over 9.2) and team D/ST markets (for example Seattle Seahawks D/ST over 8.8) alongside skill players. Kicker points are a distance-tiered count of field goals (3/4/5/6 points by 0-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60+ yards) plus extra points, minus one per miss, so they come from drive stalls inside range, the coach's kick-or-go choice and the kicker's make curve, and fall when the offence converts red-zone trips into touchdowns. D/ST points are sacks, takeaways, safeties, blocks and return touchdowns plus a points-allowed step from +10 at a shutout to -4 at 35 or more, so they depend on the opponent offence, its quarterback and the score script that forces it to pass.
stages.distribution: Kicker: discrete, lumpy pmf on small integers with mean near 8 and an atom at zero if inactive; D/ST: right-skewed sum of rare events plus a step function, support roughly -4 to 30

talent_strength.note: Component model with efficiency; player skill priors by component are not defined in this archetype's inputs.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent pass and run defence, position yield and coverage shell enter the per-target and per-carry yield (stage s3); how much opponent defence adds beyond role and script is unmeasured (u3).

role_personnel.note: Opportunity shares by role and zone. Quarterback starter status and rushing role are attached for the QB-inclusive pools (season H2H, position and weekly leaders).

availability_news.note: Active status and games played; the zero atom is explicit in the contract.

coaching_scheme.note: Play-caller tendencies enter through pass rate and tempo in the volume inputs; no separate coaching input is needed beyond those, and the contracts do not depend on in-game coaching decisions directly.

environment.note: Single-game tickers (KXNFLFFPTS, KXNFLFFPTSLADDER, weekly leader markets, any-game highs) are single games sensitive to wind, cold and roof, which cut passing and kicking and raise run share; weather and venue are attached in stage s3 with a weather dataset. Season-total and ranking tickers average these out.

game_context_script.note: Game state shifts volume between passing and rushing; the shootout correlation is handled through the covariance input.

efficiency_conversion.note: Yield and touchdown conversion by opportunity.

distribution_variance.note: Components covary and the tail matters for highs and ranks.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Seeding stakes and starter rest (nfl.motivation_seeding) and rest and short-week effects (nfl.rest_travel) are attached for the Weeks 15-17 and any-game tickers; the field grid handles byes. The season ladders themselves are mapped out in series_mapping_issues.

officiating_rules.note: Penalties cancel individual plays and can shave a few points, but crews do not generate a stable per-player effect distinct from role and efficiency in a fantasy score.

settlement_contract.note: Sleeper's scoring, rounding, group membership and correction handling; kicker scoring unverified.

nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.label: Component and teammate-stack covariance of fantasy points
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.mechanism: Correlation matrix of a player's scoring components (receptions, yards, touchdowns) and between teammates' scores (quarterback-receiver, same-backfield).
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.rationale: Variance of the fantasy total is mostly covariance, and head-to-head, top-N and ladder markets depend on it; a quarterback touchdown pass produces four points for him and six for his receiver, which the sum-of-marginals logic ignores.
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-game data compute the correlation between components within a player and between pairs of teammates, by position pair, after removing team-week means; shrink pairwise correlations to position-pair averages with k=80 games; use a Gaussian or t-copula for joint simulation. Output a correlation matrix per game by team and position and variance multipliers for total scores.
raw_data: player-game components: pass yds/TD, rush yds/TD, receptions, rec yds/TD, INT, fumbles lost
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.why: Needed for H2H, top-N and ladder probabilities where correlation changes the answer, and for the shootout effect across a whole game.

nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.label: Play-level expected touchdowns (xTD) from opportunity location
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.mechanism: Sum over a player's carries and targets of the probability that the play scores a touchdown given its yard line, distance to go and air yards.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.rationale: Touchdowns are the largest fantasy variance source and regress strongly; share of red-zone usage alone is a coarse measure, while a play-level expected touchdown count is a direct estimate of true touchdown rate.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.measurement: Fit a logistic model on 2016-2025 plays: P(TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, play type, air yards, role) for carries and targets, then player xTD per game = sum of play probabilities over the last 12 games with half-life 6, shrunk toward position-role mean with k=4 games; forecast = xTD rate x projected opportunities; compare actual TD minus xTD for regression diagnostics.
raw_data: pbp: yardline_100, down, ydstogo, rusher_id, receiver_id, air_yards, touchdown
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.why: Provides the touchdown component of a PPR forecast with a play-level calculation that red-zone share and anytime-TD rates only approximate.

nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.label: Sleeper scoring settings, group membership and correction timing
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.mechanism: Mapping from official stats to Sleeper's default full-PPR points, including kicker and bonus rules, the position group each player is assigned to and when Sleeper publishes or corrects totals.
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.rationale: The contract settles on Sleeper's number, not on the league's stat; a player's position group (WR/RB/TE/QB), rookie flag, rounding and timing of the published value determine the outcome and cannot be assumed from another fantasy platform.
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.measurement: Archive Sleeper's scoring settings (points per yard, per touchdown, per reception, kicker table) and each week's published points at game end, at 24 hours and at settlement; flag differences from the standard stat sheet; keep a table of Sleeper position assignment as of the expiration date; compute a score from official stats and compare with the Sleeper value (error in points).
raw_data: Sleeper player metadata (fantasy_positions), weekly stats, scoring settings
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.why: Defines the target of every contract in the archetype and reduces risk from position classification and corrections, which have no equivalent in the other inputs.

nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.label: Single-game ceiling tail model for any-game highs
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.mechanism: Probability that a player's single-game score exceeds a high threshold (34, 49 points) in a given game, based on per-game distributions with an extreme-value tail.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.rationale: Season-high contracts depend on rare big games rather than the mean; the maximum of 17 games grows with the log of games and is dominated by touchdown clusters and long plays.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.measurement: Score scale = full-PPR fantasy points (1 per reception, 0.1 per scrimmage yard, 6 per TD, 0.04 per passing yard, 4 per passing TD, -2 per INT/fumble lost). Per player-game: body = compound Poisson (touchdowns) plus yardage from the player's nfl.rush_yardage_tail/receiving models; tail above the position's 90th percentile of 2012-2025 player-game scores replaced with a generalized Pareto fitted by maximum likelihood. P(max over N remaining games >= x) = 1 - prod_g (1 - p_g(x)) where p_g is adjusted for the own-model game total from nfl.model_team_points_mean (never a betting total) and P(active), with an inter-game correlation correction from nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covariance. Output at thresholds 30, 40, 50, 60 points.
raw_data: player-game fantasy points history by position
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.why: Directly gives the probabilities for KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH and KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE, which are not threshold events on the mean.

nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.label: Weekly full-pool projection grid and correlation by game
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.mechanism: Projected distribution of fantasy points for every player in a position pool in the week, including bye weeks, inactives and game environment, with shared game effects.
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.rationale: Weekly leader and top-5 contracts are decided across the whole pool, so the probability for a listed player depends on how many other strong options play that week, and on shootouts that lift several players together.
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.measurement: For each week and position pool (WR, RB, TE, QB) project every player with at least 5 percent of position snap share: mean and variance from the component model, game environment effect from the own-model projected team points (nfl.off_epa, nfl.def_epa and nfl.pace; never a sportsbook total) shared across the game's players, and a probability of inactivity from the injury vintage; simulate 20,000 weeks to compute P(rank = 1) and P(rank <= 5) for each player including ties at the cutoff (1/N).
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.why: Provides a defined field model for the weekly leader contracts whose rules say all eligible players in the group are ranked.

nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.label: Single-game fantasy maximum: joint simulation of both rosters under ESPN PPR scoring
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.mechanism: Simulates every relevant player's ESPN-PPR fantasy score in one game jointly (shared drives, touchdown attribution between passer and receiver, script) and reads the probability each player has the maximum.
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.rationale: A game-most contract is not a per-player threshold: it depends on the whole field of both teams and on the strong positive correlation between a quarterback and his receivers, which makes stacking players on one offence crowd the top. ESPN scoring weights differ from Sleeper's in places, so the per-player model must be re-scored on ESPN settings before the maximum is taken.
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.measurement: For each game: draw team drives and touchdowns from the team scoring model, attribute each touchdown to passer/receiver or rusher by player share (targets, carries, red-zone share over last 8 games, half-life 4), draw yards and receptions conditional on attributed plays from player component models (nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covariance), score each player with ESPN default PPR weights (1 per reception, 0.1 per rushing/receiving yard, 0.04 per passing yard, 4 per passing TD, 6 per rush/receiving TD, -2 per interception and lost fumble under ESPN defaults, to be verified); 20,000 simulations; P(max) per player with 1/N for exact ties. As-of kickoff with final inactives.
raw_data: player shares: targets, carries, red-zone opportunities
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.why: Supplies KXNFLFANTASYMOST, the only single-game field maximum in this archetype and the only one on ESPN scoring.

nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.label: Kicker fantasy points under Sleeper default scoring from drive stalls by distance
nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.mechanism: A kicker's Sleeper points are +3 per FG made 0-39 yards, +4 for 40-49, +5 for 50-59, +6 for 60+, +1 per extra point made and -1 per FG or extra point missed, so the score is a weighted count of drive endings: touchdowns (extra-point tries), drives that stall inside range (FG attempts by distance) and the kicker's make curve.
nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.rationale: Kicker scores have a small mean (about 7-9) and a lumpy discrete distribution, and strikes such as 9.2 sit where one long FG changes the outcome; the distance tiers make a stalled drive at the opponent's 35 worth more than one at the 10, and coach 4th-down aggressiveness converts would-be FGs into TD tries. Team TD expectation and FG opportunity move in opposite directions inside the red zone, which a single 'team points' proxy misses.
nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.measurement: Per team-game simulation using the shared drive draws: number of drives from nfl.drives; per drive, ending state (TD, FG attempt, other) from own-model drive outcome rates by field position, with FG attempt distance = line of scrimmage + 17 yards from the drive's stall yard line distribution (nflverse pbp 2018-2025, shrunk to league with k=200 attempts by stall bin) and the coach's FG-versus-go decision from nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate; make probability from nfl.kicker's distance curve (weather and altitude adjusted); extra-point make rate per kicker shrunk to league with k=150 tries; two-point try share by coach. Points = 3*FG(0-39)+4*FG(40-49)+5*FG(50-59)+6*FG(60+)+1*XP - 1*(FG missed + XP missed). Output the full pmf and P(points > strike) as of the latest injury report (kicker active flag; replacement kicker if out).

nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.label: Team D/ST fantasy points under Sleeper default scoring (events plus points-allowed tier)
nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.mechanism: A D/ST score is the sum of event points (+1 sack, +2 interception, +2 fumble recovery, +1 forced fumble, +2 safety, +2 blocked kick, +6 defensive or special-teams TD, +1 special-teams forced fumble or fumble recovery) and a step function of points allowed (0: +10, 1-6: +7, 7-13: +4, 14-20: +1, 21-27: 0, 28-34: -1, 35+: -4), so it is driven by the opponent offence's dropbacks, sack and giveaway rates and by the opponent's scoring distribution.
nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.rationale: D/ST markets (e.g. 'Seattle Seahawks D/ST: Over 8.8') are decided by rare high-value events and a steep points-allowed step; a shutout or a pick-six moves the score by 6-10 points, so the distribution is right-skewed with a negative floor. Sacks and turnovers rise when the opponent trails and must pass, linking D/ST points to the margin, and the points-allowed tier depends on whether Sleeper counts points allowed by the offence (return TDs) as well, which is not stated in the Kalshi text.
nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.measurement: Per team-game, using the shared game draws: opponent dropbacks from the opponent's pass rate by simulated script; sacks = dropbacks x own pressure-to-sack rate (nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition) as negative binomial; interceptions = opponent pass attempts x opponent QB INT rate adjusted for pressure (nfl.int_rate), fumbles and recoveries from league per-play rates shrunk to team with k=400 plays; D/ST TDs from nfl.dst_td_hazard; safeties and blocked kicks at league rates (shrunk team effect, k=40 games). Points allowed = opponent simulated points from nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean conditional on the draw, mapped to the Sleeper tier. Sum event points + tier points per draw; output pmf and P(points > strike). Fit dispersion on 2015-2025 team-games. As-of the latest injury report of both teams' QBs and key pass rushers.

nfl.fantasy_points_model.reason: This is the specification of the aggregation (components times Sleeper weights), not a source of information; keep it tied to nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definitions.

interactions.mechanism: Touchdown points equal red-zone opportunities times conversion, and the number of red-zone trips depends on the score path and the team's total; a goal-line back on a high-scoring favourite gets multiplied opportunities, while the same share on a low-scoring team yields little.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress touchdowns on red-zone carries x team expected points and compare to additive models.

interactions.mechanism: A quarterback and his top receiver share a touchdown pass, so their fantasy scores are positively correlated and the quarterback's total variance includes the receiver's; for H2H of a quarterback versus a receiver on the same team this correlation lowers the variance of the difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of QB and WR1 fantasy points by team and compare variance of the difference with the independent case.

interactions.mechanism: When a starter is inactive his snaps and carries are taken by the next player on the depth chart, with a larger share to the one with a similar role, so one teammate's absence changes another's expected points non-uniformly by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare backups' snaps and fantasy points in games without the starter, split by role similarity.

interactions.mechanism: In a high-total game several receivers have high scores, so the weekly leader is more likely to come from a shootout, and probabilities across players in the same game are positively correlated; independent field assumptions understate how often one game supplies the leader.
interactions.how_to_test: Check historical share of weekly WR leaders coming from games in the top quartile of totals.

interactions.mechanism: The chance of a 34-point or 49-point game grows rapidly with touchdown count (three touchdowns plus yardage), so the high rungs are driven by the product of goal-line opportunity and big-play rate rather than by mean points.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(34+) conditional on touchdown count and on long-play count; compare to a normal approximation.

interactions.mechanism: Fantasy value per target is catch probability times (1 reception point + 0.1 per yard) plus touchdown value, so the slope of points on target share depends on the receiver's depth: a short-area high-aDOT-low target profile gains mostly reception points at high catch rate, while deep targets are caught less often but carry more yards, so scoring is not linear in target share across depth profiles.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit points per target by aDOT bin and catch-rate bin, and test whether the slope of total points on targets differs across aDOT terciles.

interactions.mechanism: D/ST points have a step in points allowed (+10, +7, +4, +1, 0, -1, -4) and event counts that rise when the opponent trails and throws; a defence facing a weak offence gains twice, through the higher tier and more sacks and interceptions in a passing script, so the response to the opponent's expected points is piecewise and convex at the low end.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2015-2025 team-games regress D/ST Sleeper points on opponent own-model expected points with tier dummies and compare the slope of event points across opponent-expectation bins.

interactions.mechanism: A kicker's FG count depends on drives that stall inside range, so a more efficient red-zone offence or a more aggressive 4th-down coach converts FG tries into touchdowns: kicker points rise with team scoring only until red-zone conversion is high, then extra points replace field goals and the score flattens.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin team-games by own-model expected points and red-zone TD rate and compare kicker Sleeper points; test whether 4th-down aggressiveness terciles shift FG attempts at fixed expected points.

nonlinearities.shape: discrete six-point jumps: score distribution multi-modal at multiples of 6 plus a yardage base
nonlinearities.why: One extra touchdown moves a score by six points, so the cumulative distribution has steps; threshold probabilities move non-smoothly with the touchdown rate.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: zero if inactive, partial ramp for returning players, near constant for starters
nonlinearities.why: Fantasy output follows snaps closely, and snaps are step-like in injury status, which gives a bimodal distribution around the zero atom.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy right tail with probability of 34+ falling by a factor of 3-4 for each additional 10 points
nonlinearities.why: High fantasy scores come from rare multi-touchdown games, so probabilities for the highest rungs fall much faster than a normal tail with the same variance would predict.

nonlinearities.shape: expected maximum grows with log of pool size and heavy-tailed marginals
nonlinearities.why: The weekly position leader sits far out in the distribution of the pool, so small changes in a player's tail change his leader probability by more than his mean does.

contract.settlement_definition: Six live series, all with sampled rules text, in two shapes of additive in-game count, kept in one archetype by decision: per-team and both-team counts share the opportunities-times-rate chain. One-team counts for a named game: field goals (KXNFLFG 'Minnesota 4+', floor_strike 3.5), sacks (KXNFLTEAMSACK 6+, 'Any sacks recorded during a 2-point conversion attempt do not count') and total yards of offense (KXNFLTEAMYDS 450+); each states that if the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start the market stays open and resolves on 'the official final result', and if it does not start within 48 hours it resolves to a fair price. Both-team counts for the Feb 8, 2026 Seattle vs New England game: combined sacks (KXNFLGAMESACK, at least 9), successful 2-point conversions (KXNFL2PTCONV, at least 2) and successful 4th down conversions (KXNFL4DCONV, at least 5), whose sampled secondary text is empty so postponement, overtime and source are unstated. No sampled text says whether overtime events count or names a data source; official league statistics are implied. The multi-week next-interception series (KXNFLNEXTINT) moved to unreg:team_window_event_hazards.

rules_evidence.quote: Any sacks recorded during a 2-point conversion attempt do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The team sack count excludes two-point attempts, so only sacks on ordinary snaps count and the opportunity pool is opponent dropbacks outside conversion tries.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: A delay inside 48 hours keeps a one-team count market live and settles it on the official final result; beyond 48 hours the market resolves to a fair price, a rule shared by the field-goal, sack and yards series.

rules_evidence.quote: If Seattle and New England collectively record at least 9 sacks in the Seattle vs New England professional football game
rules_evidence.establishes: The both-team sack contract is the sum of both defences' sacks; unlike KXNFLTEAMSACK its sampled text has no 2-point-try exclusion and no secondary clause.

rules_evidence.quote: collectively records at least 5 successful 4th down conversions
rules_evidence.establishes: Counts successful fourth-down conversions by both teams combined (floor_strike 5); the number is attempts by both coaches times success rate, so it depends on coach aggression and score state.

variants_and_edge_cases: One-team series (KXNFLFG, KXNFLTEAMSACK, KXNFLTEAMYDS) carry the 48-hour postponement rule ('remain open and resolve based on the official final result'; fair price if not started within 48 hours); the three both-team series have no such sentence, although the primary text of the both-team series names the game 'originally scheduled' for a date, so postponement handling is unstated for them.

KXNFLTEAMSACK excludes sacks recorded during a 2-point conversion attempt; KXNFLGAMESACK (both teams) does not repeat the exclusion, so the treatment of conversion-try sacks in the combined count is unstated.

KXNFL2PTCONV and KXNFL4DCONV count successful conversions by both teams; the texts do not say whether a conversion on a play with an accepted penalty, a kick-based point after, or a fourth-down conversion by penalty (automatic first down) counts, which affects the realised counts.

No sampled text for any of the six series states whether overtime sacks, field goals, yards or conversions count; all samples named 'during the' or 'in the' game, so overtime is presumably included but unestablished (u5).

Family routing: per-team counts KXNFLFG -> s1+s2, KXNFLTEAMSACK -> s1+s3, KXNFLTEAMYDS -> s1+s4; both-team counts KXNFLGAMESACK -> s3+s6, KXNFL2PTCONV and KXNFL4DCONV -> s5+s6. KXNFLNEXTINT moved to unreg:team_window_event_hazards; score-path, rare-play and league-count series moved to their own archetypes.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules texts (the one-team series say 'official final result'). Kalshi series metadata is reported by reviewers (not in contract_rules_sample.json, not verified by me) to name settlement sources (the league, ESPN) for the series checked.

mechanism.summary: Per-game counts (field goals, sacks, yards, successful two-point and fourth-down conversions, for one team or both teams combined) are opportunities times a per-opportunity rate: field goals come from drives that stall inside the kicker's range, sacks from opposing dropbacks times a pressure-to-sack conversion, yards from plays times yards per play, and conversions from each coach's decision to try times a success rate, all reshaped by score path, weather and overtime. The counts are overdispersed and discrete, so thresholds are tail masses of a mixture over score states, and both-team counts add a script-driven negative dependence between the two teams. Per-team and both-team counts share this chain and are kept in one archetype by decision; the multi-week next-interception series, the score-path functionals, rare play calls and league-wide rare-event counts have their own archetypes.

stages.name: Opportunity counts for the team in the game
stages.description: Counts are built on opportunities: plays and dropbacks for a team, drives and stalled drives, and for both-team counts the sum over two offences. The offence's tempo and the opponent's ball control determine how many occur, and overtime adds possessions if it counts. For the sack contracts the relevant pool is the opponent's dropbacks outside two-point tries.
stages.distribution: Plays, drives and dropbacks per team-game: approximately normal with small skew; the earlier ranges (plays 120-135 combined, drives 22-26, dropbacks 35-45 per team) are unsourced placeholders to compute from play-by-play

stages.name: Field goals: stalled drives inside range and kicker conversion
stages.description: A team's field goals (KXNFLFG, 4+ is a strike of 3.5) need a drive that stalls inside the kicker's range, a decision to kick rather than go for it, and a make. The rate of stalls inside range is the complement of red-zone touchdown efficiency, kicker accuracy falls with distance, wind and cold, and coach aggression on fourth down removes attempts. The count is small with a mean near 1.6 per team and a thin upper tail, so a 4+ threshold is a tail event of drive volume times stall rate times make probability.
stages.distribution: Count of field goals per team is a small overdispersed count (0-5 range seen in the draft; the mean of about 1.6 is an unsourced placeholder to compute); make probability falls with distance and wind

stages.name: Sacks: dropbacks times pressure conversion
stages.description: A defence's sacks (KXNFLTEAMSACK, KXNFLGAMESACK) come from the opponent's dropbacks times the rate at which pressure turns into sacks, with the quarterback's sack avoidance and the offence's protection as modifiers. Counts are low with heavy dispersion. Quarterback status (nfl.qb) enters as a probability that the starter plays and an in-game exit hazard; KXNFLGAMESACK sums two defences' sacks, which are linked negatively through script (the trailing team drops back more and absorbs more sacks while the leader runs) and positively through shared pace and weather.
stages.distribution: Sacks per team-game overdispersed with a small mean; the mean (about 2.3 in the earlier draft) is an unsourced placeholder to compute from play-by-play

stages.name: Total yardage: plays times yield per play
stages.description: Total yards (KXNFLTEAMYDS, 450+ is a strike of 449.5) follow plays and success rate with a per-play yield distribution that has explosive-play tails; drive-level variance makes the totals overdispersed. Weather shifts both rates modestly (penalty rates are not modelled), and the script changes which play types dominate. The volume side comes from team plays (nfl.pace), drives (nfl.drives) and the script that tilts run/pass mix (nfl.script), multiplied by per-play yield; the 450+ strike is expected to sit well above the mean (an unsourced placeholder, to compute from play-by-play), so it depends on the explosive-play tail.
stages.distribution: Total yards per team right-skewed by explosive plays; the mean of about 330 and sd of about 80 in the earlier draft are unsourced placeholders to compute from play-by-play

stages.name: Conversion counts: two-point tries and fourth-down tries
stages.description: KXNFL2PTCONV and KXNFL4DCONV count successful conversions by both teams, so each is attempts times success. Attempts come from each coach's two-point and go-for-it policy by field position, distance and score state: trailing teams late are expected to go for two and for it more often (a hypothesis, not established here), and a close game may rarely invite either, so the count may depend on the simulated path as well as on coach habit. Success comes from short-yardage offence against the opposing defence, with red-zone and goal-to-go efficiency for two-point tries from the 2-yard line. Stakes are suspected to raise attempts but are unmeasured.
stages.distribution: Two-point successes per game mostly 0-2 (the strike of 2 is a rare double); fourth-down successes per game 0-6 (strike 5 is a tail), small overdispersed counts with strong score-path dependence (ranges are unsourced placeholders to compute)

stages.name: Count dispersion and rare in-game events
stages.description: Counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because opportunities and rates are correlated within a game and across stats; blowouts produce extreme sack counts while close games produce long drives. Rare events (safeties, overtime) add small masses at the tails and, if overtime counts, extra possessions. The model needs a dispersion parameter per stat and score state rather than a single Poisson assumption, and for both-team counts a negative correlation between teams through script and a positive one through shared pace and weather.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial with a dispersion parameter that differs by stat; safety and overtime frequencies are unsourced placeholders to compute from play-by-play

talent_strength.note: Offensive success rate and kicker quality set the baseline rates for yards, field goals and conversions; defensive strength enters through the sack inputs (nfl.pass_rush and the sack decomposition); no interception input is attached.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing pass rush and protection decide sack counts for a given team.

role_personnel.note: Kicker identity and starting quarterback are the personnel factors for field goals and sacks.

availability_news.note: Quarterback status and in-game exit risk shift dropbacks and sack hazards; practice-report vintages are not archived publicly (u3).

coaching_scheme.note: Go-for-it, two-point and fourth-and-goal policy decide attempts for the field-goal and conversion counts.

environment.note: Wind and cold depress passing and kicking and so field goals, sacks and yards.

game_context_script.note: Score state (nfl.script, measured on the own-model margin distribution after the round-3 patch) shifts dropbacks, rushes and aggression; overtime adds possessions if it counts.

pace_volume.note: Plays, drives and dropbacks are the opportunity base for every count.

efficiency_conversion.note: Red-zone conversion, offensive success rate and kicker accuracy are the per-opportunity rates for field goals, yards and conversions.

distribution_variance.note: Negative-binomial dispersion by stat and score state converts means into tail probabilities for 'N+' strikes.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Playoff and must-win stakes plausibly raise fourth-down and two-point attempts (the both-team samples are all for one game, Seattle vs New England on Feb 8, 2026) but no input measures a stakes effect; this is an unverified hypothesis.

nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.label: Count-statistic dispersion by stat and score-state split
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.mechanism: Negative-binomial dispersion parameters and mean multipliers for the in-game counts settled by this archetype (field goals, sacks, total yards and successful two-point and fourth-down conversions) by score state and game total; interceptions and rush attempts are not settled by any series here and are out of scope.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.rationale: Thresholds like 4+ field goals or 6+ sacks are tail masses; a Poisson assumption understates them, and dispersion changes with whether the game is a blowout or a close contest.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.measurement: From 2012-2025 team-games fit, per stat (field goals, sacks, total yards, conversions), a negative binomial with mean = opportunities x rate and dispersion k by stat and by score-state bucket (lead>=14, within 7, trail>=14); shrink k toward the league-stat value with a gamma prior (equivalent to 200 team-games); output PMF for each stat given expected mean and state mixture over the pre-game margin distribution.
raw_data: team-game counts: FG made, sacks, total yards, successful 2-point and 4th-down conversions
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.why: Turns means into tail probabilities for the 'N+' strikes used in the per-game count series.

nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.label: Win-streak and undefeated-hazard path model across 32 teams
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.mechanism: Probability distribution of the longest win streak, the week of the last first loss, and the number of ties, from a correlated season simulation with shared rating uncertainty.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.rationale: Streak and undefeated contracts depend on the sequence of game outcomes and on strength dispersion, not just on win totals; ties break streaks without being losses, and a bye week is an unrecorded week. It is now week 9 of the season, so most of these contracts are partly decided by banked results and the input must carry the current season state, not restart at Week 1.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.measurement: Do not build a separate simulator: use the single shared season simulator nfl.standings_sim (with the shared rating-uncertainty draw and tie probability of the win-totals record, 0.25 percent per game and rating prior sd of 4.0 points as the shared assumptions) run on REMAINING games only, conditioned on the results already played as of the current week (completed scores, ties, each team's current win streak and undefeated flag, banked ties), current injuries and quarterback status. For each of 100,000 runs record: the longest streak (under both tie treatments, see u2) for each team, the week of each team's first loss (ties not losses; same-week first losses tied), season tie count (banked + simulated), and the worst-to-first indicator; output probabilities for each contract rung.
raw_data: schedule order, byes, completed results to date, current streak and undefeated flags
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.why: Retained for reference only: the streak, undefeated and worst-to-first series moved to season_win_totals_and_futures, which now stages this input.

nfl.primetime_flex_probability.label: Primetime window assignment and flex-scheduling probability
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.mechanism: Number of national-window games a team has in the published schedule and the probability that flexible scheduling adds or removes games before the season ends.
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.rationale: The primetime count is a deterministic function of the schedule apart from flex decisions, which depend on team records and appeal and are announced 6 to 12 days ahead; the count of 5+ games is therefore mostly known at release with a flex-driven change.
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.measurement: Base count B_t = number of games for team t designated in the released schedule in national windows (Thursday night, Sunday night, Monday night, Thanksgiving, Christmas, excluding the Wednesday opener and Saturday-doubleheader windows unless the contract says otherwise). For each remaining week w in the flex-eligible windows per current league rules (verify each season against the league's published flex policy), compute P(team t flexed in) and P(flexed out) by logistic regression on 2023-2025 flexible-slot decisions with features team win%, opponent win%, playoff-leverage flag, team's primetime count so far (cap of 7 games) and the league's 12-day notice deadline. Expected final count = B_t + sum_w (P_in - P_out); output the full PMF by Poisson-binomial convolution. As-of latest flex announcement.
free_sources: NFL schedule releases and flex announcements
raw_data: schedule by team with network window and original vs final kickoff
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.why: Retained for reference only: KXNFLPRIMETIME was re-filed to off_field_events, so this input no longer feeds a stage here.

nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.label: Defence sack-count decomposition: opponent dropbacks, pressure rate, conversion
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.mechanism: Expected sacks by this defence equal opponent expected dropbacks times pressure rate times pressure-to-sack conversion, with opposing quarterback's sack avoidance and the offence's pass protection.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.rationale: The 6+ sacks contract is a tail of a thin count; the mean depends on three multiplicative factors with different regression speeds, and the conversion factor is quarterback specific.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.measurement: Expected opponent dropbacks from nfl.pace and nfl.script; team pressure rate over last 12 games (half-life 6, shrink k=120 dropbacks); conversion = sacks / pressures with opposing quarterback's career-regressed rate (shrink k=100 pressures) and pass-rusher availability adjustment; E[sacks] = dropbacks x pressure rate x conversion; add overdispersion from the count model. Needs pressure data or a sack-plus-hit proxy.
raw_data: pbp: sack, qb_hit, qb_dropback, passer, defteam
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.why: Splits the team sack count into three separately estimable factors and brings the opposing quarterback into a defensive count.

nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.label: Separate offence and defence scoring rates for season and weekly extremes
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.mechanism: Estimates each team's points scored and points allowed per game as separate rates with their own uncertainty, so that season scoring extremes and the weekly highest-scoring team can be simulated.
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.rationale: A single margin rating cannot give points for and points against; the most/least points scored and allowed are extremes over 32 teams that depend on pace, defence and offence separately, and the weekly high score is the maximum of 32 correlated-through-nothing but heavy-tailed team scores. Contracts are priced from the right tail of each team's score distribution.
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.measurement: For each team compute opponent-adjusted points per game for offence and defence separately: ridge regression of team points on offence and opposing-defence indicators with home indicator, over the last 17 games weighted exp(-ln2 x games_ago/8) with a one-third reversion to league mean before the season (offence k=6 games, defence k=6 games shrink to mean). Simulate remaining games conditioned on points already banked (as of the current week): team season points = banked + sum of simulated scores, each score drawn from a negative binomial with mean from the team's own rates (sd about 9.5 points per team-game, an assumption to refit) and a shared per-team rate draw (sd 1.2 points per game). Weekly high score = max over that week's 32 (or fewer on byes) simulated scores. Output P(team has min/max points scored/allowed) with 1/N ties, and P(team has the weekly high). As-of: after the last completed game.
raw_data: schedules: game_id, week, team scores, home flag
pbp: plays and epa per team

interactions.mechanism: Trailing teams throw more and take more hits late, so opposing defences with a lead produce more sacks per dropback, while a leading offence that runs reduces the opposing sack pool; the sign of the script effect on the sack count depends on which team leads.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate sacks per opponent dropback by the defence's score state and quarter.

interactions.mechanism: Field goals per game equal drives times the chance of stalling in range, which is the complement of the red-zone touchdown rate; a strong red-zone offence produces fewer field goals even with many drives, so drives and red-zone efficiency move the count in opposite directions.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress field goals per game on drives and red-zone touchdown rate and test the interaction coefficient.

interactions.mechanism: Go-for-it and two-point decisions are expected to rise when a team trails late (down 8, 14 or more in the fourth quarter), so the conversion counts would depend on whether the game produces a late deficit and on the coach's aggressiveness; this is a hypothesis to test, with no evidence offered here, and the sampled both-team series are all one game.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team-game 4th-down and 2-point attempts on time spent trailing by 9+ in the second half, with a coach random effect.

interactions.mechanism: Count dispersion depends on the score path because blowouts may produce extreme sack counts while close games produce long drives; mixing across score states creates fat tails in the marginal count distribution, so the threshold probability need not be that of a single negative binomial (a hypothesis to test).
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the mixture of state-specific negative binomials with a single negative binomial on tail frequencies of sacks and field goals.

interactions.mechanism: Trailing teams run more plays at a faster tempo and pass more, which raises opposing sack opportunities and total yards together, while a leading team runs the clock and shortens the game; the direction depends on which team leads, so plays and drives respond to the score state and not only to team tempo.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress plays, dropbacks and yards per team-game on time spent trailing and own tempo, with team effects, 2015-2025.

nonlinearities.shape: right-skewed count tail: tail probability rises faster than a Poisson model for a given mean
nonlinearities.why: Over-dispersion increases the mass for 6+ sacks and 4+ field goals, so strikes in the upper tail are underpriced by Poisson assumptions.

nonlinearities.shape: steep logistic decay of make probability with distance, with a kicker-specific range threshold
nonlinearities.why: A few extra yards cut the field-goal make probability by several percentage points beyond 45 yards, so the field-goal count is a nonlinear function of the distance distribution of stalled drives, with wind and cold shifting the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold in win probability and score deficit: attempt rates jump when trailing late
nonlinearities.why: Go-for-it and two-point attempt rates are near the neutral baseline until the deficit and clock make kicking pointless and then rise steeply, so the conversion counts have a regime change in the simulated score path rather than a smooth response.

nonlinearities.shape: convex: sack probability per dropback rises faster than linearly with pressure rate at the extremes
nonlinearities.why: Teams at the high end of pressure rate convert pressure to sacks at similar rates but against quarterbacks with poor sack avoidance the conversion rises sharply, which fattens the upper tail that a 6+ team sack strike depends on.
